

===== PAGE: about_ai_data_reconciliation_reports.html | About AI Reconciliation Reports =====
## About AI Reconciliation Reports
 AI Reconciliation uses built-in algorithms to identify study records with anomalies, duplicate, or missing information. AI Reconciliation lists those findings in the following reports: 
 Conditions Reports 
- Conditions without Treatments 
- Worsening Conditions 
- Overlapping Conditions 
- Overlapping non-worsening Conditions and ongoing MH 
- Invalid CTCAE Grade 
- Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade 
 Treatments Reports 
- Overlapping Treatments 
- Treatments without Conditions and ongoing MH 
  Study managers can use the reports to reduce data entry errors and accelerate study data reconciliation. 
 Important: Required Configurations for AI Reconciliation Reports 
 AI Reconciliation runs reports selectively based on the datasets you configure in Event Analysis tab within Data Surveillance Configuration . The table below lists the required and optional dataset configurations for each report : 
 AI Reconciliation Report Type 
 Required 
 Optional 
 | Overlapping Conditions 
 | Condition (Adverse Events (AE)) 
 | None 
 | Overlapping treatments 
 | Medication (Concomitant Medication   (CM)) 
 | Procedure ( Concomitant Procedures ( CP)) 
 | Worsening Conditions 
 | Condition (AE), History (Medical History (MH)) 
 | None 
 | Overlapping non-worsening conditions and ongoing MH 
 | Condition (AE), History (MH) 
 | None 
 | Conditions without treatment 
 | Condition (AE), Medication (CM) 
 | Procedure (CP) 
 | Treatment without Conditions and ongoing MH 
 | Condition (AE), Medication (CM), History (MH) 
 | Procedure (CP) 
 | Invalid CTCAE Grade 
 | Condition (AE) (with CTCAE Grade mapped) 
 | None 
 | Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade 
 | Condition (AE) (with CTCAE Grade mapped) , Lab measurement 
 | None 
## Data Updates in AI Reconciliation Reports 
 Data gets updated in AI Reconcilication reports after each data refresh.  
 Data in the Treatments without Conditions and Conditions without Treatments, or Ongoing MH reports updates in two ways: 
- Instant Updates –   You can view the changes in the report data instantly based on an action. For example, if you link conditions and treatments in the Conditions without Treatments or Treatments without Conditions or ongoing MH reports, the confidence level lowers for the finding. This change is reflected instantly when you refresh AI Reconciliation. The new, lowered confidence level also applies to other findings with the same condition and treatment pair in the study, if the condition and treatment occur in the same time frame.
- Periodic Updates – You can view changes in the report data over a period of time For example, changes in the the Conditions without Treatments and Treatments without Conditions or ongoing MH reports are due to a decision model that is updated at least once annually. The decision model determines if a record is indeed a finding, and the associated confidence level. The decision model leverages a Knowledge Graph (KG) t hat contains information such as the conditions and treatments and their relationships, which enables Data Managers and Clinical Operations users to identify and decide if data discrepancy exists in reconciled data. In the Knowledge Graph, relationships are built based on biomedical drug databases and enriched with WHODrug/MedDRA to enable integration with clinical data. The strength of the condition-treatment relationship is predicted using a machine learning model trained on features developed from historical studies. 
## Impacts of MEDRA and WHODrug Dictionary Versions 
 The Conditions Without Treatments and Treatment Without Conditions and Ongoing MH reports rely on the Medidata proprietary Knowledge Graph to match treatments and conditions. and thereby, to find records with missing entries. The Knowledge Graph uses the following coding dictionary versions to provide results: 
- MEDRA: 28.0-English 
- WHODrug: Global-B3-202503-English-Drugs (March 2025), Global-B3-English-Atcs. 
 We recommend you code verbatim terms using the above dictionary versions and join files with conditions and treatment forms (external data) using the verbatim term as key in  Data Connect Transformations. If your study uses other data dictionary versions, Data Surveillance may fail to accurately establish the links between treatments and conditions, resulting in a higher number of findings. You can use AI Reconciliation to review and reconcile such findings by linking conditions and treatments that occur in the same time frame. 
 Note : Results for no other AI Reconciliation reports are impacted by MEDRA and WHODrug versions listed here.

## Overlapping Conditions Report
 The Overlapping Conditions report lists patient data records for patients that AI Reconciliation determines to have specific conditions recorded multiple times, where the condition records have:
- The same coded term. 
- Overlapping start and end dates. 
 Data managers can review the records listed in the Overlapping Conditions report to ensure that every condition for a patient gets reported only once. For each record, the report also provides a list of other conditions that occurred simultaneously as the condition of interest, but AI Reconciliation does not identify those conditions as being related. Therefore, those conditions are not considered as overlapping. 
 From the Overlapping Conditions report, you can: 
- View the list of report findings and associated finding details. 
- View and submit Rave queries on the report findings. 
- Mark findings as reviewed or unreviewed 
- View the patient profile of the patient associated with the record. 
- Agree or disagree with AI Reconciliation's confidence assessment of a finding .
- Link other treatments, conditions, or ongoing medical history as being related to a finding. 
- View a list of other conditions that occurred at the same time as the condition of interest, but not considered as overlapping. 
## Conditions without Treatments Report
 During a study, patients are administered treatments in response to their conditions when the condition is treatable. The Conditions Without Treatments report lists patient data records for patients that AI Reconciliation determines as having conditions without any associated treatment recorded within a stipulated number of days from the condition start date. 
 Note : If ConMed and ConProc fields are not configured , AI Reconciliation algorithm attempts to find treatments for all conditions.
 Data managers can review the records listed in the Conditions Without Treatments report to ensure that patients get treated as per the study protocol.  
 For each individual record listed, the Conditions Without Treatments also provides: 
- A list of other treatments that occurred within the same time frame as the condition of interest, but AI Reconciliation  does not designate the treatment as related   to the condition. 
- A list of t reatments the patient took that are related to the condition, but the patient took them outside of the condition time frame. For example, if you have a headache today and take an aspirin three weeks later, it falls outside the time frame of when the headache occurred. 
 From the Conditions Without Treatments report, you can: 
- View the list of report findings and associated finding details. 
- View and submit Rave queries on the report findings. 
- Mark findings as reviewed or unreviewed 
- View the patient profile of the patient associated with the record. 
- Agree or disagree with AI Reconciliation's confidence assessment of a finding .
- Link other treatments the patient took as being related to the condition. 
## Worsening Conditions Report
 During a study, patients can report existing conditions that worsen over the period of the study. The Worsening Conditions report shows a list of patients with conditions identified as worsening if they have: 
- No associated ongoing medical history (MH) or non-worsening conditions recorded before the worsening condition start date. 
 OR 
- Non-worsening conditions reported after the worsening condition start date. 
 The records in the report have  worsen or exacerbat or aggravat  as a prefix in the Reported Term column, indicating that the condition occurred previously and is now worsening. Study managers can review the records and take the appropriate action for patients with worsening conditions. 
 The AI Reconciliation algorithm also identifies the following for each patient record in the Worsening Conditions report:
- Unrelated records indicating the patient's on-going medical history (MH). 
- Unrelated conditions reported before the worsening condition start date. 
- Unrelated conditions reported after the start date of the worsening condition.
 With the Worsening Conditions report, you can: 
- View the list of report findings and associated finding details. 
- View and submit Rave queries on the report findings. 
- Mark findings as reviewed or unreviewed 
- View the patient profile of the patient associated with the record. 
- Agree or disagree with AI Reconciliation's confidence assessment of a finding .
- Link other treatments, conditions, or ongoing medical history as being related to a finding. 
## Overlapping non-worsening Conditions and Ongoing MH Report
 A patient's conditions may remain stagnant throughout the period of the study. The Overlapping non-worsening Conditions and ongoing MH report shows a list of patients with non-worsening conditions that repeat within the patient's ongoing medical history. Data managers can check why a non-worsening condition for a patient in a study repeats within the patient's ongoing medical history, while reconciling data and take the appropriate action as per study protocol. 
 Each individual record in the Overlapping Non-worsening Conditions and Ongoing Medical History report: 
- Indicates that the AI Reconciliation algorithm found a condition with the same preferred term as in the patient's ongoing medical history.
- Is a listing irrespective of the start or end dates for the ongoing medical history. 
- Has no additional associated records.  
 With the Overlapping non-worsening Conditions and ongoing MH report, you can: 
- View the list of report findings and associated finding details. 
- View and submit Rave queries on the report findings. 
- Mark findings as reviewed or unreviewed 
- View the patient profile of the patient associated with the record. 
- Agree or disagree with AI Reconciliation's confidence assessment of a finding .
## Invalid CTCAE Grade Report
 The Invalid CTCAE Grade report identifies discrepancies in grades assigned to adverse events as per Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0 criteria (CTCAE v 5.0) . The CTCAE classification grades adverse events based on a scale from 1 to 5. 
 These discrepancies are defined as:
- Grade is present but not required : The adverse event record has an assigned numeric CTCAE grade but that adverse event is not present in the CTCAE version 5.0 criteria.
- Grade is not present but is required : The adverse event record does not have an assigned numeric CTCAE grade but that adverse event is present in the CTCAE version 5.0 criteria.
- Grade is invalid : The adverse event record has an assigned numeric CTCAE grade and that adverse event is present in the CTCAE version 5.0 criteria, but the grade present is not an "allowable" grade.
 Data Managers can review the records listed in the Invalid CTCAE Grade report to reconcile the grading of adverse events with the actual data reported.
 A patient record in the Invalid CTCAE Grade report:
- Indicates that the AI Reconciliation algorithm found a condition had an invalid grade, a required grade was not present, or a present grade was not required. 
- Displays confidence corresponding to the the AI Reconciliation algorithm assigned confidence. 
 With Invalid CTCAE Grade report, you can:
- View the list of report findings and associated finding details. 
- View and submit Rave queries on the report findings. 
- Mark findings as reviewed or unreviewed 
- View the patient profile of the patient associated with the record. 
- Agree or disagree with AI Reconciliation's confidence assessment of a finding .
## Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade Report
 The Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade report identifies discrepancies in the adverse events records which need additional lab records to calculate grade as per CTCAE v 5.0 .
 The AI Reconciliation algorithm for the Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade report evaluates a subset of adverse events that:
- Require CTCAE grading and exist within the CTCAE knowledge base. 
- Do not meet the criteria for records (findings) included in the Invalid CTCAE Grade report. 
- Require additional lab records for the CTCAE grade to be assigned. 
 Each adverse event record in the Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade report is a finding or in other words, a data anomaly, if relevant lab records on which the CTCAE grade relies on, is not collected within the adverse event's start and end dates. Relevant lab records are those where both analyte name and sample type are recorded in the lab dataset. For more information, see Map Lab Measurements Data . 
 Additional lab records are:
- Unrelated Same Timeframe records , which are lab records taken within the same time frame as the patient's reported condition, but match neither or only one, of the sample type or analyte name as per the CTCAE knowledge base. 
- Related Outside Timeframe records , which are lab records taken outside the patient's adverse event time frame, and match one or both, of the analyte name and the sample type as per the CTCAE knowledge base. 
 With Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade report, you can:
- View the list of report findings and associated finding details. 
- View and submit Rave queries on the report findings. 
- Mark findings as reviewed or unreviewed 
- View the patient profile of the patient associated with the record. 
- Agree or disagree with AI Reconciliation's confidence assessment of a finding .
## Overlapping Treatments Report
 The Overlapping Treatments report shows a list of patients with two or more of the same treatments whose start and end date overlap. 
 Data managers can review the records listed in the Overlapping Treatments Report report to ensure that every treatment for a patient gets reported only once. For each record, the report also provides a list of other treatments that occurred simultaneously as the treatment of interest, but AI Reconciliation does not identify those treatments as being related. Therefore, those treatments are not considered as overlapping. 
 With the Overlapping Treatments report, you can: 
- View the list of report findings and associated finding details. 
- View and submit Rave queries on the report findings. 
- Mark findings as reviewed or unreviewed 
- View the patient profile of the patient associated with the record. 
- Agree or disagree with AI Reconciliation's confidence assessment of a finding .
- Link other treatments as being related to a finding. 
- View a list of other treatments that occurred at the same time as the condition of interest, but not considered as overlapping . 
## Treatments Without Conditions or on-going MH Report
 During a study, patients are administered treatments in response to their conditions when the condition is treatable. The Treatments without Conditions or on-going MH report lists records for patients that AI Reconciliation determines as having concomitant treatments without any associated ongoing medical history or conditions recorded before or on the treatment start or end date. 
 Data managers can review the records listed in the Treatments without Conditions or on-going MH report to ensure that patients get treated as per the study protocol. 
 For each individual record listed, the Treatments without Conditions or on-going MH also provides: 
- A list of other conditions that occurred within the same time frame as the treatment of interest,   but AI Reconciliation does not designate the treatment as related   to the condition. 
- A list of conditions the patient experiences that are related to the treatment, but the patient experiences them outside of the treatment time frame.  
- A list of on-going medical history that the patient experiences. 
 With the Treatments Without Conditions and ongoing MH report, you can: 
- View the list of report findings and associated finding details. 
- View and submit Rave queries on the report findings. 
- Mark findings as reviewed or unreviewed 
- View the patient profile of the patient associated with the record. 
- Agree or disagree with AI Reconciliation's confidence assessment of a finding .
- Link other treatments as being related to a finding. 
- Link other treatments the patient took as being related to the condition.

===== PAGE: about_data_surveillance.html | About Data Surveillance =====
## About Data Surveillance
 Data Surveillance is a comprehensive suite of data surveillance software capabilities that encompasses a drag-and-drop listings builder, automated query generation for Medidata Rave sourced data, issue management for non-Medidata sourced data, AI-powered data reconciliation, patient profiles, and visualizations.  Data Surveillance leverages AI to streamline data aggregation, standardization, and management workflows so that multiple users can act on real-time data in ways that reduce burden, shorten review timelines, increase quality, reduce risk, and improve patient safety. 
## What Is Data Surveillance?
 Data Surveillance is a comprehensive suite of data surveillance software capabilities provided by the Clinical Data Studio solution. 
 Data Surveillance encompasses a drag-and-drop listings builder, automated query generation for Rave sourced data, issue management for non-Medidata sourced data, AI-powered data reconciliation, patient profiles, and visualizations. 
## What Is the Purpose of Data Surveillance?
 Data Surveillance leverages AI to streamline data aggregation, standardization, and management workflows so that multiple users can act on real-time data in ways that reduce burden, shorten review timelines, increase quality, reduce risk, and improve patient safety. 
 With Studio’s Data Surveillance capabilities, You can: 
- Create data review listings without programming. 
- Generate Rave queries automatically and in bulk. 
- Reconcile data using automatically generated, AI-powered reports. 
- Visualize real-time data on your own whenever you want. 
- Visualize disease progression response for oncology trial patients 
- Build complete patient profile designs., and  
- Track data cleaning progress and quickly identify and address outstanding tasks. 
## Who Uses Data Surveillance?
 Clinical research associates, medical monitors, data managers, clinical scientists, safety physicians, and more use Data Surveillance.
## How Does Data Surveillance Work?
 Data Surveillance   ingests your team's study data from:  
- Rave, or Veeva EDC. 
- Third-party vendor data—for example, protocol deviations, lab data, or any data not uploaded through Rave—which gets uploaded through Ingestor . 
 Important : Patient IDs in Rave must be unique, otherwise Data Surveillance's analysis produces multiple, duplicate records for the same patient ID.
In Data Surveillance, s tudy data automatically refreshes four times daily at approximately 9:00am (EST), 3:00pm (EST), 9:00pm (EST) and 3:00am (EST), and the data presented within the user interface is current as of 11:00 pm (EST) the previous day, 5:00 am (EST) the same day, 11:00 am (EST) the same day, 5:00 pm (EST) the same day, respectively. Each study data refresh produces a data snapshot. Updated data from Rave and   activated datasets from Data Connect   are available in 6 to 12 hours within Data Surveillance and RBQM . For more information, see Clinical Data Studio's Data Pipeline . 
 Once Data Surveillance pulls the study's data sets and variables into your study environment, you can use the following Data Surveillance capabilities: 
- Data Surveillance Configuration 
- Map the data that Data Surveillance and RBQM  consume to produce the statistical analysis and visual renderings for:
- Statistical Monitoring analyses 
- Data anomaly detection and trends 
- Event incidence and under-over reporting events 
- Potential duplicate patients 
- Rounding and propagation of vital sign records 
- AI Reconciliation reports 
- RECIST 1.1 dashboard reports 
- Clean Patient Tracker missing page counts . 
- Third-party, fully ingested studies patient milestone data . 
- Create, activate, and deactivate vendors to which you want to communicate vendor data issues. 
- Create and update derived variables to include custom dataset fields in patient profiles designs as well as Data Surveillance and RBQM reports and analysis. 
- Create stacked datasets and view the list of stacked datasets in your study. 
- Data Sets 
- View and investigate your study's data sets . 
- Holistically explore and investigate your entire set of study data, and 
- Investigate patients' case report forms in Rave. 
- Data Listings 
- Create draft listings by configuring conditional expressions that run against your study data to capture patient records within a specified variable that match the expression's defined conditions . For example, you can configure an expression to capture patient data records for  female patients below age 50 who have had a serious adverse event . 
- Preview draft listings to ensure the listing passes preliminary validation. 
- Approve listings for team-wide use in your study. 
- Review and validate the data listing's full set of results . As part of the review process, you and your study team can: 
- Add internal review comments directly on individual data records that appear in a data listing's results. 
- View and submit Rave queries on Rave-enabled data listings' records directly in Data Surveillance. 
- Mark individual data records as reviewed . 
- Track data listings for unreviewed records in Clean Patient Tracker . 
- Report and track external data issues in Vendor Queries . 
- Clean Patient Tracker 
- Track unvetted and unreviewed patient data , and further drill down directly to complete the outstanding data cleaning tasks in other Data Surveillance capabilities such as Data Listings and AI Data Reconciliation. 
- Open EDC Queries 
- View the detailed list of all open and answered queries raised against patient data in your study . 
- AI Reconciliation 
- Identify duplicate or missing patient record information using automated AI Reconciliation reports. 
- Custom Graphs 
- Create data visualizations to chart the relationship between any combination of datasets on a single visual using real-time study data on demand. 
- Patient Profiles 
- Design patient profiles , which can include headers , flags ,  tables , and timelines . 
- Configure the patient profile design layout . 
- View patient profiles with actual study data to: 
- Evaluate how the profile design is taking shape in real time. 
- Mark patient profiles as reviewed. 
- View patient profile design reports to enable reviewers and stakeholders to efficiently view and sign off on the design. 
- RECIST 1.1 Dashboard : 
- Compare site entered overall tumor measurements with those that the RECIST 1.1 algorithm calculates. 
- Data Surveillance Template Library :
- Save and store commonly used listing, QTL, custom numeric KRI, or custom percentage KRI configurations and visualizations for reuse within a study. 
 You can also:
- Refresh listings to produce results based on the latest study data . 
- Refresh AI Reconciliation to produce reports based on the latest study data. 
- Trigger Clean Patient Tracker to recalculate outstanding records based on the latest study data . 
 Note: The f ollowing Data Surveillance capabilities support screen-failed patient data: Data Sets , Vendor Queries , Listings , AI Reconciliation , Patient Profiles , Custom Graphs , and RECIST 1.1 Dashboard .   
 What Are the Benefits of Data Surveillance? 
 Data Surveillance:
- Automates data review and query management. 
- Simplifies data reconciliation with the help of AI. 
- Enables study teams to explore data and rectify inconsistencies with advanced analytics and visualizations. 
- Helps ensures data integrity. 
## How Do I Access Data Surveillance?
 Access to Data Surveillance requires that you are invited to a study that is integrated with and linked to the Data Surveillance app in Medidata. Once you receive an invitation and you activate your Medidata account, you can log in to Medidata and access your studies in Data Surveillance. To learn more, see Access Data Surveillance .
 Note : You require permissions to access and perform specific actions in each Data Surveillance capability. To learn more, see Data Surveillance Building Blocks and Permissions .

===== PAGE: about_rbqm.html | About RBQM =====
## About RBQM
 RBQM is a comprehensive suite of risk surveillance software capabilities that support a holistic risk-based quality management (RBQM) approach to data quality. RBQM enables study teams to comprehensively manage site, study, and patient risk using collaborative risk management workspaces, dynamic dashboards, and auto-generated, AI-powered data visualizations.  
## What Is RBQM?
 RBQM is a comprehensive suite of risk surveillance software capabilities provided by the Clinical Data Studio solution. RBQM supports a holistic risk-based quality management (RBQM) approach to data quality. 
## What Is the Purpose of RBQM?
 RBQM brings your risk-based strategies to all your clinical data in one place. With RBQM's capabilities, you can: 
- Track the health of RBQM tasks and risk metrics using key performance indicators. 
- Create risk assessments to document, monitor, and address study risks in highly collaborative workspace. 
- View, monitor, and address all study risks in one consolidated risk inventory. 
- Quickly configure and monitor key risk indicators (KRIs) and quality tolerance limits (QTLs). 
- Uncover site performance and compliance risks using AI-powered visualizations and reports to discover data anomalies and unusual trends. 
- Perform targeted analyses to identify fraud and misconduct and data veracity issues. 
- Perform robust data interrogation, data review, and reconciliation at the individual patient level and at the aggregate level. 
- Identify data quality and patient safety issues sooner. 
- Capture, review, and manage protocol deviations from clinical data sources to ensure data consistency and regulatory compliance 
## Who Uses RBQM?
 Clinical study managers, clinical research associates, site monitors, central monitors, safety monitors, medical monitors, data managers, biostatisticians, programmers, clinical reviewers, and more use RBQM. 
## How Does RBQM Work?
 RBQM   ingests your team's study data from:  
- Rave EDC 
- Third-party vendor data—for example, protocol deviations, lab data, or any data not uploaded through Medidata Rave —which gets uploaded through Ingestor . 
 In Data Surveillance and RBQM, s tudy data automatically refreshes four times daily at approximately 9:00am (EST), 3:00pm (EST), 9:00pm (EST) and 3:00am (EST), and the data presented within the user interface is current as of 11:00 pm (EST) the previous day, 5:00 am (EST) the same day, 11:00 am (EST) the same day, 5:00 pm (EST) the same day, respectively. Each study data refresh produces a data snapshot. Updated data from Rave and activated datasets from Data Connect are available in 6 to 12 hours within Data Surveillance and RBQM. For more information, see Clinical Data Studio's Data Pipeline . 
 RBQM enables you to refresh its capabilities to render analyses based on RBQM's most recently ingested study data. You can schedule data refreshes to occur and on a preset frequency or manually trigger data refreshes ad-hoc. See: 
- Schedule or trigger KRI Dashboard to refresh and output the latest study data analysis . 
- Schedule or trigger QTL Dashboard to refresh and output the latest study data analysis . 
- Schedule or trigger Statistical Monitoring to refresh and output the latest study data analysis . 
 Once RBQM pulls the study's data sets and variables into your study environment, you can use the following RBQM capabilities: 
- RBQM Configuration 
- Map the data that Data Surveillance and RBQM  consume to produce the statistical analysis and visual renderings for:
- Statistical Monitoring analyses 
- Data anomaly detection and trends 
- Event incidence and under-over reporting events 
- Potential duplicate patients 
- Rounding and propagation of vital sign records 
- AI Data Reconciliation reports 
- RECIST 1.1 dashboard reports 
- Clean Patient Tracker missing page counts . 
- Third-party, fully ingested studies patient milestone data . 
- Configure risk assessments. 
- Create custom QTLs and   custom KRIs so that you can track your study's QTLs and KRIs on the QTL Dashboard and  KRI Dashboard . 
- Create and update derived variables to include custom dataset fields in patient profiles designs as well as Data Surveillance and RBQM reports and analysis. 
- Configure and enable modules to auto-generate signals on the Signals page. 
- Create stacked datasets and view the list of stacked datasets in your study. 
- Add, edit, and delete review reports to capture activity logs and study findings across data review and reconciliation cycles.  
- Risk Based Quality Management Summary 
- Track in one centralized location the health of RBQM tasks and metrics using high-level key performance indicators. 
- Navigate directly to the RBQM capabilities you need to address risks identified in the summary. 
- Risk Assessment 
- Document and manage the data , processes , and risk categories identified as critical to the study outcome. 
- Document and manage risks associated with each critical data, critical process, and risk category.
- Score risks to measure and determine which risks most require focus and mitigation. 
- Add risk mitigation strategies to decrease or eliminate risks.

- Review and approve risk plan reports .

- Track, monitor , and manage risks .
- Plan Documents

- Uncover unexpected data associations or trends using: 
- Data Anomaly Detection – Determine your study data's outliers, anomalies, unusual data associations, risks, trends, and missing data  at the data point-, patient-, site-, and country-level.

- Potential Duplicate Patients – Identify and investigate:
- Sites with potential duplicate patients across all site locations in your study.

- Event Incidence – View the reported events and the incidence rate in which those events occurred within a  domain at the site and study level.

- Save and store commonly used data listing, QTL, custom numeric KRI , or custom percentage KRI configurations for reuse within a study. 
- Protocol Integrity Report: Capture, track, and process and review protocol deviations from Rave queries, clinical data listings, and manual entries 
 Note: The f ollowing RBQM capabilities support screen-failed patient data: Protocol Integrity Report , Weekend and Holiday Visits (Statistical Monitoring) , Signals , and Audit Trail Review .

 RBQM enables study teams to:
- Comprehensively manage site and study risk throughout the study. 
- Execute efficient RBQM processes with end-to-end workflows. 
- Track and mitigate risks in real-time with dynamic dashboards. 
- Resolve emerging problems faster with centralized issue management. 
- Monitor and mitigate risks to patient safety. 
- Uses AI-powered, machine-learning capabilities to identify anomalies and trends in patient data that would otherwise go undiscovered using manual data review.

===== PAGE: access__view__and_create_plan_documents.html | Access, View, and Create Plan Documents =====
## Access, View, and Create Plan Documents
 Plan Documents are an integral part of a clinical study used to:
- Streamline operational planning. 
- Transform risk-prone data into actionable, dynamic plans that actively guide team member actions. 
- Enhance transparency and mitigate risks, ensuring alignment, accountability, and improved compliance across teams. 
 Note : You can access and view plans only if you have the View Data Quality Plan building block added to your Cloud Administration role. To create plan documents, you must have the Manage Data Quality Plans building block. For more information, see  RBQM Building Blocks and Permissions .
## Access Plans
 You can view your study's current set of data plans as well high-level details associated with each plan. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Plan Documents  in the left-hand menu.
The Plan Documents table shows the following:
 Column Descriptions 
- Name – The plan name. 
- Status – The status of the plan, draft or published.  
- Last Modified –The plan's creation date or when the last saved edit occurred. 
- Edited By – The user who most recently updated the plan. 
- If necessary,  filter or sort the Plan Documents table. 
## View Plans
 To help find the information you need, you can view existing plan documents to show:
- Specific plans by name. 
- Only plans created by specific users. 
- Only plans that were last updated by specific users. 
- If necessary, access the Plan Documents table . 
- Optional . Create a plan.
The plan document version is set at version 1 by default. 
- Click the plan name for any plan.
The plan's detailed view appears with the following details:
- Library  – Includes a list of built-in elements you can drag and drop into your plan.  
- Misc 
- Study 
- Tables 
- Document Workspace – A text editor where you can drag and drop library elements, or type, or paste text to include into your plan. 
- Table of Contents – By default, the table of contents option is disabled. Enable it to include a table of contents in your plan. 
## Sort the Current Plans Table
 To help find the plans you need, you can sort the Plan Documents table's columns vertically in ascending or descending alphanumeric order. For example, you can sort to more quickly find a plan name. Or you can sort the Last Updated column to find the most recently updated or longest unupdated plan.

 Note: Deviation Description - Plan Documents Integration
 The Protocol Deviation Assessment Plan (PDAP) defines automated detection rules, severities, and categories for protocol deviations.
 Drag the Deviation Descriptions table element into the workspace to configure the PDAP . You can have only  one active (published) plan document and one draft document at any given time . To make changes to a published plan, you must create a  new draft from the active published version . 
 When you publish the new draft, the system automatically replaces the active version and archives the previous version in the read-only version history . 
 Updating the PDAP automatically flags and highlights associated protocol deviation records in the Protocol Integrity Report (PIR) so users can identify plan changes. To learn more, see  Protocol Integrity Report .

===== PAGE: access_and_view_data_anomaly_detection_plots.html | Access and View Data Anomaly Detection Plots =====
## Access and View Data Anomaly Detection Plots
 You can select which of your study data variables' analysis you want to view on the Statistical Monitoring >  Data Anomaly Detection page.
- Access RBQM , and then click Statistical Monitoring > Anomalies in the left-hand menu. 
- On the Data Anomaly Detection page, select a Domain Set. 
- Select a Variable.
The list of plots associated with the selected variable show in the Plot table below. The table only lists plots with outlier data.
- Plot Name – The variable or variables that RBQM analyzes. 
- # Outliers – The total number of the variable's data point that are considered outliers. 
- Click a plot name.
 The selected plot renders in the plot visualization along with summary information. To learn how to read and understand data anomaly detection plots, see Investigate Data Using Data Anomaly Detection Plots . 
 In addition, high-level performance-related metrics pertaining to the selected variable update next to the plot list: 
- Total # of Outliers  – The total number of distinct data points that are considered outliers for the selected variable. 
- % of Outliers  – The percentage of all the domain set's outliers that are associated with the selected variable. 
- Mean Score Overall – The selected variable's overall mean discrepancy score for all data points. 
- More Score Outliers  –  The mean discrepancy score for data points that are outliers in the selected variable. 
- Strength of Association – A numeric value that indicates the probability that patients at an individual site will have reported the same or similar numeric or text values for a particular variable. Strength of association calculates on a range from 0.00 to 1.00. The higher a variable's strength of association with the site variable, the more likely it is that you can predict the value of that variable for a new patient at a given site. To learn more, see  Strength of Association Description and Calculation Methodology .

- Click any column header to sort the table by that column. The sorted header shows in blue font.  indicates that the column is sorted in descending numeric order (highest value at the top, lowest at the bottom).

===== PAGE: access_and_view_visualizations.html | Access and View Custom Graphs =====
## Access and View Custom Graphs
 Custom Graphs enables you and your study team members to chart the relationship between any combination of datasets on a single visual using real-time study data.  
 For example, you can create Custom Graphs for: 
- Medical monitors to view the number of adverse events per site.
- Site monitors to track patient enrollment rate.   
- Data managers to view missed visits or data entry delays. 
- CRAs to view, track, and compare patients records for pulse against blood pressure.  
- Study managers to see the number of nonrandomized patients in the study or track the number of study dropouts per month. 
 You can view and interact with any visualization created in your study. 
 Custom Graphs can plot data in a bar chart, stacked bar chart, line chart, multiline chart, scatter chart, donut chart, segmented donut chart, or tabular chart. 
 Graphically viewing study data relationships enables you to more effectively: 
- Gain a clearer understanding or perspective of the study data. 
- Identify study trends and patterns. 
- Track study performance. 
- Build and share reports or present on study data metrics using clear, visually appealing graphical renderings. 
## Access and View Custom Graphs
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click Custom Graphs in the left-hand menu.
The Custom Graphs table shows the following:
 Column Descriptions 
- Type – The type of graphical representation used to plot
- – Donut chart. 
- – Line chart. 
- – Bar chart. 
- – Scatter chart 
- – Tabular chart 
- Name – The custom name used to identify the visualization. 
- Creator – The user who created the visualization. 
- Last Modified – The date that the visualization was created or most recently modified. 
- Description  – Details such as what data is plotted in the visualization or the visualization's purpose or rationale. 
- Last Modified By – The user who created or most recently modified the visualization. 
- If necessary, filter or sort the Custom Graphs table.
 Important: Custom Graphs sort visits that appear relative to Medidata Rave or visit metadata provided. If no metadata exists, visits do not appear sorted correctly in the visualization chart.
- In the Custom Graphs table, click the row of the visualization you want to view.
The visualization appears below the table. Custom Graphs plot study data in a bar chart, stacked bar chart, line chart, multiline chart, donut chart, or segmented donut chart. Click a chart type below to learn how to interpret and interact with the chart.
 Bar Chart 
- Bar charts typically visualize and compare variable data points based on value, count, or frequency. 
- Each bar represents a variable data point within a data set. 
- You can hover your cursor on any bar to view the data point's x- and y-axis value. 
 Stacked Bar Chart 
- Stacked bar charts segment the variable represented in each bar by subcategory and visualize the variable's relative distribution of data by subcategory. 
- Each bar represents a variable data point within a data set. 
- Each bar can be stacked—or segmented— to show one or more data categories within the variable data point. 
- You can hover your cursor on a bar segment to highlight that data category in all bars and to view the data category value, x-axis value, and y-axis value. 
- The legend shows all subcategories within the primary variable being visualized. 
- You can hover your cursor on a subcategory label in the legend to highlight all segments representing that subcategory. 
- You can click a subcategory label to remove all segments representing that subcategory from the chart. Reclick to view the subcategory's segments again. 
 Line Chart 
- Line charts typically visualize and track variable data point trends on a timeline or frequency. 
- You can hover your cursor on any data point in line charts to view the data point's x- and y-axis. 
 Multiline Chart 
- Multiline charts plot for multiple lines on a single visual to simultaneously view and compare trends across multiple data subcategories within a variable. 
- Each line represents a subcategory. 
- You can hover your cursor on a data point in specific line to view that value's x- and y-axis value. 
- The legend shows all subcategories within the primary variable being visualized. 
- You can hover on a subcategory label in the legend to highlight that subcategory's line in the chart. 
- You can click a subcategory label in the legend to remove that subcategory's line from the chart. Reclick to view the subcategory's line again. 
 Donut Chart 
- Donut charts visualize the total count of values within a single variable. D onut charts show values  up to  two decimal points. 
 Note : Donut charts may not chart all patients in a data set if there are missing or incomplete patient records. Therefore, for donut charts using the Percentage aggregation, the value shown inside the donut may not add up to 100%. 
 Segmented Donut Chart 
- Segmented donut charts split the variable represented in the donut chart by subcategory and visualize the variable's relative distribution of data by subcategory. 
- You can hover your cursor on a segment in the donut chart to view that subcategory's value. 
- The legend shows all subcategories within the primary variable being visualized. 
- You can hover on a subcategory label in the legend to highlight that subcategory's segment in the chart. 
- You can click a subcategory label in the legend to remove that subcategory's segment from the chart. Re-click to view the subcategory's segment again. 
 Note : Segmented donut charts may not chart all patients in a data set if there are missing or incomplete patient records. Therefore, for segmented donut charts using the Percentage aggregation, the value shown inside the donut may not add up to 100%.
 Scatter Chart 
- Scatter charts plot for multiple dots on a single visual to simultaneously view and compare data points across multiple data subcategories within a numeric variable. 
- Each color represents a subcategory within the numeric variable. 
- You can hover your cursor on a data point to view that value's x- and y-axis value. 
- The legend shows all subcategories within the primary variable being visualized. 
 Note : Scatter plots only work for integer or float type variables, and do not support any aggregations. 
 Tabular Chart 
- Tabular Custom Graphs aggregate data by summing, averaging, etc. multiple dataset variables and display in a table format. The chart shows data in rows and columns with information summarized (aggregated) at the intersection points. The tabular charts show counts or percentages of categorical study data. 
- You can drag and drop a single tabular dataset into the row, then select a variable from the dataset into the row. The column field remains disabled if no dataset is added to the row. You can add multiple variables into the column field. That is, you can have multiple columns for each row in the tabular visualization. 
 Note : Only activated datasets with collection type as t abular visual used in Data Connect, are available as tabular datasets in Data Surveillance. You must therefore ensure that tabular visual collections are created in Data Connect . Contact your Medidata representative for further information.
 Summary Table 
 A Summary table appears below the chart for bar, line, and donut Custom Graphs. Count values in the summary table appear truncated up to two decimals. Each row represents a chart segment, and the color filler with the count in the columns. Any aggregations or calculations applied to the data while configuring the visualization chart, appears in the summary table. The summary table also includes patient level information such as Patient ID, Country, Site Number etc. You can click the Patient ID hyperlink to view the related patient's profile design in Patient Profiles. You can also export a summary table. You can filter, sort, or search the summary table dynamically by applying these parameters to the chart, including filtering with _TXT variables. 
 For example, if you apply a Country filter to a line chart, the summary table below the chart also updates to show the country you filter by, after you click   Apply . To search, you must enter at least four characters into the Search field. 
## Filter the Custom Graphs Table
 To help find the Custom Graphs you need, you can filter the Custom Graphs table to show Custom Graphs:
- Based on chart type; that is, donut chart, line chart, or bar chart. 
- Based on name. 
- Created by specific users. 
- If necessary, access the Custom Graphs table . 
- Click the Filter button, at the top-right corner of the Custom Graphs table. 
- Click one or more of the following filters:
- Type – Filter to show Custom Graphs based on chart type. 
- Name – Filter to show Custom Graphs based on name. 
- Created By – Filter to show only Custom Graphs created by specific users. 
- Select one or more filter items. 
- Click Apply .

===== PAGE: activate_and_deactivate_kris.html | Activate and Deactivate KRIs =====
## Activate and Deactivate KRIs
 You can activate key risk indicators (KRIs)  so that their data gets filtered, analyzed, calculated, and shown in: 
- KRI Dashboard 
- Risk Assessment 
- Risk Inventory 
 You can deactivate KRIs that no longer require analysis so that RBQM no longer consumes the KRI data for analysis and visualization in the KRI Dashboard, Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory. 
## Activate KRIs
 You can activate KRIs that are ready for consumption in RBQM. Activating a KRI triggers a KRI's data to get filtered, analyzed, calculated, shown in KRI Dashboard , Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory after the next data refresh. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > KRIs in the left-hand menu.
The Key Risk Indicators page appears. 
- On the Key Risk Indicators page > KRI Configurations list > Activate column, click  in the corresponding row of the KRI you want to activate.
 The Activate column now shows   for that KRI, indicating the KRI is active. 
## Deactivate KRIs
 You can deactivate KRIs that no longer require analysis. Deactivated KRIs do not get calculated or shown in the KRI Dashboard, Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory following the next data refresh. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > KRIs in the left-hand menu.
The Key Risk Indicators page appears. 
- On the KRIs page > Key Risk Indicators list > Activate column, click   in the corresponding row of the KRI you want to deactivate. 
- Enter a reason for deactivating the KRI in the Deactivation Note dialog box and then click  .
 Tip : Notes provide the reasoning for why the KRI analysis is no longer required. For example, deactivated the KRI due to resolved values no longer posing a risk.
 The Activate column now shows   for that KRI, indicating the KRI is inactive.

===== PAGE: activate_and_deactivate_listings.html | Activate and Deactivate Listings =====
## Activate and Deactivate Listings
 You can activate approved and draft data listings to appear in the Data Listings page > Approved Listings tab and Draft Listings tab, respectively. For activated listings, you can edit, approve, preview, review, and take other actions on the data listing on the Data Listings page. 
 By default, all new listings are set to active status. 
 You can also deactivate approved and draft data listings to not appear in the Data Listings page > Approved Listings tab and Draft Listings tab, respectively. For deactivated listings, you cannot edit, approve, preview, review, and take other actions on the data listing on the Data Listings page. 
 Deactivating approved and draft data listings removes unwanted or irrelevant data listings from appearing on the Data Listings page. Therefore, you can better find and take action on pertinent data listings.
## Activate Listings
 You can activate approved and draft data listings to appear in the Data Listings page > Approved Listings tab and Draft Listings tab, respectively. For activate listings, you can: 
- Edit approved or draft listing configurations. 
- Approve draft listings. 
- Preview draft listing results. 
- Review approved listing results. 
- Track approved or draft listings in Clean Patient Tracker. 
- Refresh an approved listing's results. 
- Export an approved listing's results. 
- View a listing's history data snapshots. 
 By default, all new listings are set to active status. 
- 
 If necessary, access the Manage Listing page. 
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click Listings in the left-hand menu.
The Data Listings page shows. 
- Click Manage Listing on the upper-right side of the Data Listings page.
 The Manager Listing page > Listings table shows all draft and approved listings in your study and each listing's associated details.
 Table Column Descriptions 
- Name – The listing's Object identifier (OID). 
- Expression – The data listing's user-defined conditional expression, which Data Surveillance runs against your study data to capture the patient records within a specified variable that match the expression's defined specifications. In general, expressions are built to identify and report high-risk data points that your study team can review and investigate as necessary. 
- Created By – The user who created the listing.

 Tip : Clicking the Activate column header sorts the table to show activated listings at the top in ascending alphabetical order. Clicking the Activate column header again sorts the table to show deactivated listings at the top in descending alphabetical order.

## Deactivate Listings

- Edit approved or draft listing configurations. 
- Approve draft listings. 
- Preview draft listing results. 
- Review approved listing results. 
- Track approved or draft listings in Clean Patient Tracker 
- Refresh an approved listing's results. 
- Export an approved listing's results. 
- View a listing's history data snapshots. 
 Deactivating approved and draft data listings removes unwanted or irrelevant data listings from appearing on the Data Listings page. Therefore, you can better find and take action on pertinent data listings.

===== PAGE: activate_and_deactivate_qtls.html | Activate and Deactivate QTLs =====
## Activate and Deactivate QTLs
 You can activate custom quality tolerance limits (QTLs) so that their data gets filtered, analyzed, calculated, and shown in the QTL Dashboard, Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory . If a custom QTL no longer requires analysis, you can deactivate that QTL so that the data no longer gets filtered, analyzed, calculated, or shown in the QTL Dashboard, Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory. 
## Activate QTLs
 You can activate custom QTLs that are ready for consumption in the QTL Dashboard, Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory.  Activating a QTL triggers a QTL's data to get filtered, analyzed, calculated, and shown in the QTL Dashboard, Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory after the next data refresh. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > QTLs in the left-hand menu.
 The Quality Tolerance Limits page, which contains the Quality Tolerance Limits list, appears 
- In the Quality Tolerance Limits list > Activate column, click   in the corresponding row of the QTL you want to activate.
The Activate column now appears   for that QTL, indicating the QTL is active.
## Deactivate QTLs
 You can deactivate custom QTLs that no longer require analysis. Deactivated QTLs do not get calculated or appear in the QTL Dashboard, Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory following the next data refresh. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > QTLs in the left-hand menu.
The Quality Tolerance Limits page, which contains the Quality Tolerance Limits list, appears.
- In the Quality Tolerance Limits list > Activate column, click   in the corresponding row of the QTL you want to deactivate. 
- Enter a reason for deactivating the QTL in the Deactivation Note dialog box and then click  .
 Tip : The note should provide reasoning for why the QTL analysis is no longer required. For example, QTL is deactivated due to resolved values no longer posing a risk.
 The Activate column now appears   for that QTL, indicating the QTL is inactive

===== PAGE: add__edit__and_delete_tables.html | Add, Edit, and Delete Tables =====
## Add, Edit, and Delete Tables
 Tables are containers of study information that allow you to display subject data of up to 12 variables. You can add the following types of tables to your profile designs:
- Wide table 
- Patient information table 
- Transposed table 
## Wide Tables
 A wide table allows for up to 12 columns of data. You create wide tables for multiple record datasets that you do not need to display in a timeline, such as medical history. All data in a wide table must come from the same data set.
 You can: 
- Add wide tables to your design. 
- Copy wide tables between studies. 
- Select to display wide tables in a timeline and configure the timeline display  options. 
- Select to display numeric data in your timeline as a graph and configure the graph display  options. 
- Configure wide table display and highlight conditions. 
- Remove display and highlight conditions. 
- Append a single note to display at the bottom of the table in the patient profile view. 
- Resize the column width. 
- Edit wide table details, such as:
- Rename wide tables, 
- Rename variables, 
- Change a variable's placement within the table, and 
- Remove variables from tables.

- On the right side of the page: click  Data , click-and-drag a variable in the data sets, and then drop the variable in a column to the left. Repeat as many times as necessary for each variable you want to add to your table.
 Notes:
- A blue "Rave" () or "External" ( ) label appears next to the data set to identify the origin of the data set. 
- Data sets with a green left border contain at least one variable that is currently applied to the study. 
- Data sets with a blue left border contain no variables that are currently applied to the study. 
- Variables with a green border on all sides are currently applied to the design. 
- If the table already contains a selected variable, then you cannot click and drag any other variables from the Data tab. 
- A blue "Derived" icon ( ) shows next to derived variables . 
- Variables with the suffix _OID indicate object identifier (OID)s. 
- Variables with the suffix_TXT, _INT, _DTC indicate enriched fields. Source fields refer to the original source of a data point, while enriched fields add extra information or context to the source data. Enriched fields are used to provide more detail about the about source fields, or to add derived information that is not directly present in the original source. If the data set variables include unknowns, the data set replaces them with interpolated (enriched) fields like _INT, or_ DTC . For example, if the source date is missing the day, the enriched _INT field (integer) interpolates the 1st day of the month, and the _DTC field (datetime) drops the unknown value. The values in the enriched fields differ when dates have unknown (UN   or   UNK ) values. If the source field uses dictionary terms, the enriched _TXT field shows the coded terms. For example, AESer and AESer_TXT. If you use _TXT values, you see end user strings rather dictionary coded values, that is, No/Yes rather than 0/1 in your profile design. 
- Data set and variable names appended with a blue flag indicate that they are identified in Risk Assessment  as   critical data for the study. 
- If you use a dataset with datetime operations, then you should use the date field and its enrichments, for example: _INT,   DT , _DTC—from the source Medidata Rave dataset to ensure data accuracy in the patient profiles. 
 Important : Do not include blank spaces between columns to avoid patient profile column sorting issues.

## Configure Wide Table Element Display Conditions
 You can configure tables and timelines to display  on a conditional basis. We provide this functionality because sometimes there are situations where an element is created to display data that may not apply to all subjects. For example, if an element is created to display pregnancy status data points, then you would want the element to only display  data that applies to female subjects.
 Therefore, you can create conditions—such as “dem.gender=Female”—so that Medidata Patient Profiles knows to hide this particular element in reports for male subjects. As a result, taking the previously mentioned example, the report will not display  an empty timeline for male subjects. This yields a cleaner, more aesthetic looking report.
 When adding or editing a wide table, do the following:
- To the right of the Wide Table section, click  Table Options .
- In the Conditional Options section, click   next to Element .
 Note : If display  condition variables are missing, a yellow marker appears next to Element . On hovering over the yellow marker, a message "This data variable does not exist in this study and needs to be replaced or removed." appears. 
- Click-and-drag a variable from the data sets, and then drop the variable in the Variable column. To use variables used in configuring wide tables to build display  conditions, see  Conditional Options In Tables Restored .
- Select an  Operator . 
- Select a  Value . 
- Click  , and select an expression. 
- Click  OK . 
- Click  Save  in the Wide Table section. 
 Note :  You can use conditional display  options with Hide "No Data" Elements to hide wide tables with no data. For more information, see  Hide Elements with No Data . 
## Configure Wide Table Row Display Conditions
 When designing profiles, there may be times when you must display the same data in two tables, but you must apply opposing conditions to the rows containing that data. For example, if you want to show significant adverse events (AE) in one table and nonsignificant adverse events in another table. In such case, you can build two tables with the same AE data set variables. On the first table, you can build a condition with ae.SAE=Yes. On the second table, you can have the condition of ae.SAE=No.
 Another example of applying row display conditions is if you know an adverse event table will have empty records, but it is unnecessary to display "No Data." You can create a condition where:
 "ae.AE Term = is not missing AND ad.AE Start Date = is not missing". 
 As a result, empty rows do not display  in the report.
 When adding or editing a wide table, do the following:
- To the right of the Wide Table section, click  Table Options .
- In the Conditional Options section, click   next to  Row .
 Note : If display  condition variables are missing, a yellow marker appears next to Row . On hovering over the yellow marker, a message "This data variable does not exist in this study and needs to be replaced or removed." appears. 
- Click-and-drag a variable from the data sets, and then drop the variable in the Variable column. 
- Select an  Operator . 
- Select a  Value . 
- Click  , and select an expression. 
- Click  OK . 
- Click  Save  in the Wide Table section.

## Configure Wide Table Highlight Conditions
 Using highlight conditions, you can design your wide tables with colored highlighting to bring attention to certain rows in your table. For example, you could design an adverse event table with highlights. The table could highlight a grade 4 adverse event row in yellow and a grade 5 in red.
 When adding or editing a wide table, do the following:
- To the right of the Wide Table section, click  Table Options .
- In the Conditional Options section, click   next to Highlight 1 or Highlight 2 .
 Note : If highlight condition variables are missing, a yellow marker appears next to Highlight 1 or Highlight 2 . On hovering over the yellow marker, a message "This data variable does not exist in this study and needs to be replaced or removed." appears. 
- Click-and-drag a variable from the data sets, and then drop the variable in the Variable column. 
- Select an  Operator . 
- Select a  Value . 
- Click  , and select an expression. 
- Click the colored block next to Text Color and select a color. 
- Click the colored block next to Background Color and select a color. 
- Click  OK . 
- Click  Save  in the Wide Table section.

## Patient Information Tables
 You can configure patient information tables to present data from a single record per patient dataset in one, two, or three columns and multiple rows. Patient information tables can include age, condition type, site, investigator name, or any other data point that is useful to identify the patient. A patient information table is part of the default profile layout. 
 You can:
- Add patient information tables to designs. 
- Append a single note to display  at the bottom of the table in the patient profile view. 
- Edit patient information table details, such as
- Rename patient information tables; 
- Rename variables; 
- Change a variable's placement within the table; and 
- Remove variables from tables.

 Notes:
- A blue "Rave" ( ) or "External" ( ) label appears next to the data set to identify the origin of the data set. 
- Data sets with a green left border contain at least one variable that is currently applied to the study. 
- Data sets with a blue left border contain no variables that are currently applied to the study. 
- Variables with a green border on all sides are currently applied to the design. 
- A blue "Derived" icon ( ) shows next to derived variables . 
- Variables with the suffix_TXT, _INT, _DTC indicate enriched fields. Source fields refer to the original source of a data point, while enriched fields add extra information or context to the source data. Enriched fields are used to provide more detail about the about source fields, or to add derived information that is not directly present in the original source. If the data set variables include unknowns, the data set replaces them with interpolated (enriched) fields like _INT, or_ DTC . For example, if the source date is missing the day, the enriched _INT field (integer) interpolates the 1st day of the month, and the _DTC field (datetime) drops the unknown value. The values in the enriched fields differ when dates have unknown (UN   or   UNK ) values. If the source field uses dictionary terms, the enriched _TXT field shows the coded terms. For example, AESer and AESer_TXT. If you use _TXT values, you see end user strings rather dictionary coded values, that is, No/Yes rather than 0/1 in your profile design. 
- Data set and variable names appended with a blue flag indicate that they are identified in Risk Assessment as   critical data for the study. 
- If you use a dataset with datetime operations, then you should use the date field and its enrichments—for example: _INT,   DT , _DTC—from the source Rave dataset to ensure data accuracy in the patient profiles. 
 Important : Use SRPP datasets only and not MRPP datasets.
- Optional : To add more columns to the table, click  , and repeat Step 5 above. 
- Optional : Click  Note to append a single note to display  at the bottom of the table in the patient profile. To learn more, see Append Notes to Elements .
 Tip : Adding a note to display  at the end of a table gives patient profile reviewers added insight into the profile's study data.
- Click  Save .

## Transposed Tables
 Transposed tables allow for multiple values that are separate lines of data to display in a single table row. You can create transposed tables for data that is structured in a long, skinny format to display in a wide table format. This data also typically includes a field for “Test” in which all of the available tests fall under that field, and a field for “Result” which displays the result of the test name that resides on the same record. Generally, that is external lab data, physical exam data, questionnaires, and so on. Transposed tables also  display  the same test name in a single column to allow you to easily view the data over time.
 You can:
- Add transposed tables to designs. 
- Select to display numeric data in your transposed table as a graph and configure the graph display  options. 
- Configure wide table display  and highlight conditions. 
- Append a single note to display  at the bottom of the table in the patient profile view. 
- Edit transposed table details, such as:
- Rename transposed tables. 
- Add variables to tables. 
- Rename variables. 
- Remove variables from tables. 
- Select, view, and remove test values.

## Display Transposed Table Data Graphs
 Graphs allow you to plot data points, such as lab values, in a line or scatter plot graph. You can use multiple graphs in a profile to highlight key data or safety values.
 When adding or editing a transposed table, do the following:
- In the Transposed Table section, click  Table Options .
- In the Graph Options section, select or enter the following information:
 Field Descriptions 
- Table and Graph  - Select to display  transposed tables in graphs, tables, or both.
- Table Only - Select to display in tables. This is the default option. Selecting this option disables all graph options. 
- Graph Only - Select to display in graphs.  
- Show Both - Select to display in tables and graphs.  
- Table Position - Select to display table the above or below the graph. This option appears only if you select 'Show Both' in Table and Graph . 
- Graph Name  – Enter a unique name for the graph. 
- Graph Height – Select the height in which you want your graph to  display. 
- Graph Width – Select the number of graphs that you want to  display within the same row on the graph. 
- Point Color – Click the corresponding color block, and select the color in which you want the data points to  display on the graph. 
- Point Size – Enter or select the size in which you want the data points to  display on the graph. 
- Line Width – Enter or select the point size in which you want the lines connecting data points to display. 
- Date Axis at Top of Graph – Select to have the data's corresponding data point display at the top of the graph. 
- Break Line Missing Data – Select to display a break in the line where a data point is missing. 
- Red Border if Value Outside Shaded Range – Select to display a red border to highlight a graph if one of the values it outside of the shaded range for that specific graph. 
- Red Border if Value Outside Limits – Select to display a red border to highlight a graph that contains a value that is outside of the defined X-axis or Y-axis for the graph; in other words, if the data is outside of the plotted range. 
- Visit Date Column – Select the column containing the date variable. This defines how the graphs present data points along the date axis and timeline. 
- Click  Save  in the Transposed Table section. 
## Configure Transposed Table Element Display Conditions
 You can configure tables and timelines to display on a conditional basis. We provide this functionality because sometimes there are situations where an element is created to display data that may not apply to all subjects. For example, if an element is created to display pregnancy status data points, then you would want the element to only display  data that applies to female subjects. 
 Therefore, you can create conditions—such as “dem.gender=Female”—so that Medidata Patient Profiles knows to hide this particular element in reports for male subjects. As a result, taking the previously mentioned example, the report will not display  an empty timeline for male subjects. This yields a cleaner, more aesthetic looking report.
 When adding or editing a transposed table, do the following:
- To the right of the Transposed Table section, click Table Options .
- In the Conditional Options section, click   next to  Element .
 Note : If display  condition variables are missing, a yellow marker appears next to Element . On hovering over the yellow marker, a message "This data variable does not exist in this study and needs to be replaced or removed." appears. 
- Click-and-drag a variable from the data sets, and then drop the variable in the Variable column. To use variables used in configuring transposed tables to build display  conditions, see  Conditional Options In Tables Restored .
- Select an  Operator . 
- Select a  Value . 
- Click  , and select an expression. 
- Click  OK . 
- Click  Save  in the Transposed Table section. 
 Note : You can use conditional display  options with  Hide "No Data" Elements to hide transposed tables with no data. For more information, see Hide Elements with No Data .
## Configure Transposed Table Row Display Conditions
 When designing profiles, there may be times when you need to display the same data in two tables, but you must apply opposing conditions to the rows containing that data. For example, if you want to show significant adverse events (AE) in one table and nonsignificant adverse events in another table. In such case, you can build two tables with the same AE data set variables. On the first table, you can build a condition with ae.SAE=Yes. On the second table, you can have the condition of ae.SAE=No.
 Another example of applying row display conditions is if you know an adverse event table will have empty records, but it is unnecessary to display "No Data." You can create a condition where:
 "ae.AE Term = is not missing AND ad.AE Start Date = is not missing". 
 As a result, empty rows do not display  in the report.
 When adding or editing a transposed table, do the following:
- To the right of the Transposed Table section, click  Table Options .
- In the Conditional Options section, click   next to  Row .
 Note : If display  condition variables are missing, a yellow marker appears next to Row . On hovering over the yellow marker, a message "This data variable does not exist in this study and needs to be replaced or removed." appears. 
- Click-and-drag a variable from the data sets, and then drop the variable in the Variable column. 
- Select an  Operator . 
- Select a  Value . 
- Click  , and select an expression. 
- Click  OK . 
- Click  Save  in the Transposed Table section.

===== PAGE: add__edit__and_delete_timelines.html | Add, Edit, and Delete Timelines =====
## Add, Edit, and Delete Timelines
 Timelines allow you to visually compare specific data points over the duration of a study in a single output. Typically, the timeline plots all of the visits for a particular patient and any events (created within the wide table noted as an event table) given a start date and end date are provided for the defined event. For example, you can view visit dates, study days, adverse events (AE), con meds, dosing, and so on in a single visual element.  
 Timelines allow you to: 
- Effectively compare data against each other, and  
- View correlations in one output rather than having to cross-reference multiple data sets. 
 Timelines can include randomization, visit data, and event tables or individual date variables.
 With timelines, you can:
- Add timelines to designs. 
- Copy timelines between studies. 
- Add variables and event tables to timelines. 
- Assign colors to variables display in the timeline. 
- View variables' value labels and new labels. 
- Edit timeline details. 
- Remove variables and events. 
- Append a single note to display at the bottom of the timelines in the patient profile view.
