===== PAGE: add_and_edit_custom_numeric_and_percentage_kris.html | Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs =====
## Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs
 Within a given study environment , you can define and add custom  numeric KRIs and percentage KRIs that target specific facets of your study data that you want to monitor for risk. If necessary, you can also edit the details of the custom KRIs that you create. 
## Add Custom Numeric KRIs
 A c ustom numeric KRI is a key risk indicator that analyzes a single user-specified variable or data set and produces a numeric output for the results or observances.  You can define and add custom numeric KRIs that target specific facets of your study data that you want to monitor for risk. For example, if you are running a blood pressure trial, you can define custom numeric KRIs to calculate the mean of blood pressure values in your study. You can then use the study findings to determine if any sites or countries show signs of risk related to blood pressure data. D ata sets and variables appear with a Rave, external or derived label next to the name. 
 After adding a custom numeric KRI, you can activate the KRI so that the KRI data gets filtered, calculated, analyzed, and shown in:   
- KRI Dashboard 
- Risk Assessment 
- Risk Inventory 
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > KRIs in the left-hand menu.
The Key Risk Indicators page appears. 
- Do one of the following:
- To add a new custom numeric KRI from scratch: click Add Custom KRI > Numeric . 
- To add a new custom numeric KRI based on an existing custom numeric KRI template: click Import Template , select the Template Group , select the template you need from the Templates list, and then click Import . To learn more about templates, see  Data Surveillance Template Library . 
- In the Custom Numeric KRI dialog box, select or enter the following:
- Name  – Enter a succinct label that identifies the custom numeric KRI. The custom numeric KRI name must be unique and no more than 255 characters. The name entered for the KRI in KRI Configuration is how the name appears in the KRI Dashboard. 
- Description  – Enter more details about what the KRI is, what it is meant to calculate and track, or any other helpful information. The description has a 2000 character maximum. 
- Data Set – Select the  data set  that you want the custom KRI to perform the KRI calculation on.
 Note : You can use published audit data sets to build KRIs, however you cannot use data sets for cross data comparison.   This means while building a KRI, you cannot use an audit data set along with a Rave data set. You can use a single published audit data set.  
- Variable  – Select the variable  that you want the custom KRI to perform the KRI calculation on.
 Note : The Variable field does not appear if you select Count or Rate in the Calculation Type field.
 Note : If data set variables include unknowns, the data set replaces them with interpolated (enriched) fields like _INT, or_ DTC . For example, if the source date is missing the day, the enriched _INT field interpolates the 1st day of the month, and _DTC fields drop the unknown value. If the source field uses dictionary terms, the enriched _TXT field shows the coded terms. 
- Threshold Type – Select User Defined or System Defined. For the user-defined threshold type, you can further define:  
- Moderate Risk Threshold – Enter the value that represents the lowest risk limit for the KRI. 
The Custom Numeric KRI value must be a positive number less than the High Risk Threshold value.
- (Optional) High Risk Threshold –  Enter a value that represents the highest risk limit for the KRI. 
The  Custom Numeric KRI value must be a nonzero positive number higher than the Moderate Risk Threshold value.
- Calculation Type  – Select the type of calculation that you want the custom numeric KRI to perform on the selected variable. You can select one of the following standard calculation types:
 Notes
- If you select a Calculation Type that does not correlate with the selected Variable, then the Variable field clears. 
- Also, the Data Set, Variable, and Calculation Type selection combination for a new custom KRI must be unique for your study environment. 
- Count  –  Calculates the average record count in the selected data set. The Count calculation is only available at the data set level. This calculates count at the patient level for each site and country and then takes average of patient-level counts to arrive at site-, country-, and study-level values. 
- Count Values – Calculates the average count of records in the study that meet a specified criteria based on the selected field. Valid only for fields with a value of 1 or 0. This calculates count at patient-, site-, country-, and study-level values. 
- Mean  – Calculates the mean value of a numeric data field based on the selected variable at the site. This calculates the mean of a variable at the patient/site/country/study level depending on the values users are seeing. 
- Rate  – Calculates the total average record count divided by patient time on study in months in the selected data set over time. The Rate calculation is only available at the data set level. This calculates rate for a dataset at the patient/site/country/study level depending on the values users are seeing. 
- Rate Values – Calculates the average percentage in a site of non-missing, non-zero values for a given variable. Use cases include the fraction of Adverse Events which are Serious, where Serious was 1 for an SAE, and 0 for a non-SAE event, or the fraction of a lab parameter out of normal range. Valid only for fields with a value of a 1 or 0. This calculates count at patient-, site-, country-, and study-level values and multiply by 100.
- Standard Deviation – Calculates variance in a set of observed values based on the selected field. This calculates value for a field at the patient/site/country/study level depending on the values users are seeing. 
- Risk Category  –  The specific, standard risk area that you want the KRI to target its analysis on.
 Note : The KRI Dashboard groups KRIs by risk category.
- Optional . To build an expression to filter for the specific subset of data that you want the custom numeric KRI to perform statistical analysis on, click the Add Filter Criteria check box, and then do the following:
- Select a variable within the Filter Criteria Query .
 Special Notes
- You can only filter the data population subset within one data set. 
- When you define an individual condition, the condition is evaluated for whether there is at least one instance where the condition is true across all data in that domain for a given patient. If you build a grouped conditional set, the individual conditions in the set are independently evaluated for truth but not contextually evaluated within the same folder. 
- Select a comparator, such as = or !=, and then select or enter a comparator value.
The list of selectable comparators differ whether you select a date, number, or text variable.  The comparator value serves as the conditional threshold, which measures and flags whether specified conditions are met in reference to the selected comparator.

## Add Custom Percentage KRIs
 A custom percentage KRI is a key risk indicator based on a user-defined binary expression that assesses if patients meet specified conditions or criteria within a targeted risk area. 
 Within a given study environment, you can define and add custom percentage KRIs to target and monitor specific study data for risk. With custom percentage KRIs, you can build functional expressions to query your study database to assess if patients meet certain conditions or criteria. The expressions contain one or more conditions. You build conditions by applying mathematical and logical operations on date, numeric, or text data set variables from the list of data sets available within a study environment. 
 For example, you can build a percentage KRI that reports the percentage of all study patients who experienced a systolic blood pressure over 140. Or you can build a percentage KRI that calculates the percentage of all study patients with a history of hypertension who had thrombocytopenia between study days 5 and 10. 
 After adding a custom percentage KRI, you can activate the KRI so that the KRI data gets filtered, calculated, and shown in: 
- KRI Dashboard 
- Risk Assessment 
- Risk Inventory 
 Percentage KRI value calculations appear as percentages. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > KRIs in the left-hand menu.
The Key Risk Indicators page appears. 
- Do one of the following:
- To add a new custom percentage KRI from scratch: click Add Custom KRI > Percentage . 
- To add a new custom percentage KRI based on an existing custom percentage KRI template: click Import Template , select the Template Group , select the template you need from the Templates list, and then click Import . To learn more about templates, see Data Surveillance Template Library . 
- In the Custom Percentage KRI dialog box, select or enter the following:
- Name  – Enter a succinct label that identifies the custom percentage KRI. The custom numeric KRI name must be unique and no more than 255 characters. The name entered for the KRI in KRI Configuration is how the name appears in the KRI Dashboard, Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory. 
- Risk Category  –  The specific, standard risk area that you want the KRI to target its analysis on.
 Note : The KRI Dashboard groups KRIs by risk category. 
- Description  – Enter more details about what the KRI is, what it is meant to calculate and track, or any other helpful information. The description has a 2000 character maximum.
- Threshold Type – Select User Defined or System Defined. For the user-defined threshold type, you can further define:  
- Moderate Risk Threshold – Enter the value that represents the lowest risk limit for the KRI.
The Custom Percentage KRI value must be between 1 and 100. 
- (Optional) High Risk Threshold –  Enter a value that represents the highest risk limit for the KRI.
The Custom Percentage KRI value must be between 1 and 100. 
- To begin building a single expression: From the list of Data Sets , click and drop a variable within the Numerator Query .
 Special Notes
- You can use published audit data sets to build KRIs; however, you cannot use data sets for cross data comparison.   This means while building a Numeric KRI, you cannot use an audit data set along with a Rave data set within the Numerator Query. You can use a single published audit data set. 
- RBQM currently does not support building percentage KRIs with data sets using datetime operations. 
- When you define an individual condition, the condition is evaluated for whether there is at least one instance where the condition is true across all data in that domain for a given patient. If you build a grouped conditional set, the individual conditions in the set are independently evaluated for truth but not contextually evaluated within the same folder. 
- Select a comparator, such as = or !=, and then select or enter a comparator value.
The list of selectable comparators differ whether you select a date, number, or text variable.  The comparator value serves as the conditional threshold, which measures and flags whether specified conditions are met in reference to the selected comparator.
 Note : For multiple-record data, similar KRIs with inverse queries may not produce inverse percentage values.

## Edit Custom KRIs
 After creating and saving a new custom KRI, you can edit the custom KRI. For example, if the KRI was originally set at a different threshold or if you want to change the KRI description to provide more detail, you can edit as needed.
 Note : If you update an existing user-defined KRI, the new changes affect all calculations and analytics that consume that user-defined KRI. All system KRI details are always read-only.
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > KRIs in the left-hand menu.
The Key Risk Indicators page appears. 
- Click any custom KRI name in Name column.
 Tip : Custom KRIs show in blue, hyperlinked text.
- In the Custom KRI dialog box, change or edit any of the following information:
- Name  – Enter a succinct label that identifies the custom KRI. The custom KRI name must be unique and no more than 255 characters. The name entered for the KRI in KRI Configuration is how the name appears the KRI Dashboard. 
- Description  – Enter more details about what the KRI is, what it is meant to calculate, or any other helpful information. The description has a 2000 character maximum. 
- Reason for change – Enter details about why you are editing the KRI.
 Note - Reason for change is a mandatory field. You cannot save a KRI you edit without entering the reason for change.
- Data Set – Select the data set  that you want the custom KRI to perform the KRI calculation on. 
- Threshold Type – Select User Defined or System Defined. For the user-defined threshold type, you can further define:  
- Moderate Risk Threshold – Enter the value that represents the lowest risk limit for the KRI. 
The Custom Numeric KRI value must be a positive number less than the High Risk Threshold value.
The Custom Percentage KRI value must be between 1 and 100. 
- (Optional) High Risk Threshold –  Enter a value that represents the highest risk limit for the KRI. 
The  Custom Numeric KRI value must be a nonzero positive number higher than the Moderate Risk Threshold value.
The Custom Percentage KRI value must be between 1 and 100.
 Note - If you only specify the Moderate Risk threshold, KRIs appear green if values are below moderate risk, and red if the values are above the moderate risk threshold.
- Calculation Type – The type of calculation you want to the KRI to be based on. For example, Count, Count Values, Mean, or Rate. 
- Risk Category –  The specific, standard risk area that you want the KRI to target its analysis on.
 Note : The KRI Dashboard groups KRIs by risk category. 
- For Percentage Numeric KRIs, the condition or conditions that define the expression. To know more about expressions, see  Percentage KRI Expression . 
- Click Save .
 Note : You can edit on inactive KRIs. If activated, the updated custom KRI details appear in KRI Dashboard after the next data refresh.

## Add and Edit Custom QTLs
 Within a given study environment , you can define and add custom  quality tolerance limits (QTLs) that target specific facets of your study data that you want to monitor for risk. If necessary, you can also edit the details of the custom QTLs that you create. 
## Add Custom QTLs
 Quality tolerance limits (QTLs) are study-level metrics that indicate if a study parameter's reported data has breached a pre-identified data quality threshold . QTLs target and monitor the greatest risks to  a study's: 
- Safety 
- Conduct 
- Performance 
- Compliance 
- Data quality 
 QTLs that reach or exceed a threshold indicate that the QTL's target study parameter may warrant investigation and mitigation. Tracking QTLs helps: 
- Ensure the study conduct operates as planned. 
- Identify as well as prevent or mitigate systematic issues early on in the study that may: 
- Threaten patient safety or study efficacy. 
- Invalidate the reliability of the study findings. 
 After  creating and activating custom QTLs in QTL Configuration, you can track QTL performance in RBQM's  Quality Tolerance Limits page . 
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > QTLs in the left-hand menu.
 The Quality Tolerance Limits page, which contains the Quality Tolerance Limits list, appears. 
- Do one of the following:
- To add a new custom QTL from scratch, click Add Custom QTL . 
- To add a new custom QTL based on an existing QTL template: click Import Template , select the Template Group , select the template you need from the Templates list, and then click Import . To learn more about templates, see  Data Surveillance Template Library . 
- In the Quality Tolerance Limit dialog box, select or enter the following:
- Parameter  – Enter a title for the study variable that you want to assess at the study level. 
- Definition  – Enter more details that explain what the parameter is meant to monitor and how it is measured.
- Expectation % – Enter the QTL's expected mean value as a percentage based on historical data.
 Note : Your project team should establish the QTL's expected value during the study startup and before data collection begins. This helps avoid potential bias influenced by preexisting knowledge and assumptions from historical data from previous studies, literature, and other avenues.
- Final Population (# of patients) – Total number of patients expected to enroll in the study. The final population should be equal to or more than the expected population.
 Tip : Adjust the expected number of patients to correspond with protocol revisions or if the study is over- or under-enrolled.
- Trigger Point – The minimum required number of patients that meet the QTL's conditions for RBQM to analyze and output the QTL's results in the QTL Dashboard.
 Tip : We recommend entering 25 or higher in Trigger Point to ensure RBQM produces a more reliable QTL analysis and prevent any erroneous early excursions or threshold violations .
- To begin building an expression: From the list of Data Sets , click, drag, and drop a variable within the Numerator Query .
 Special Notes
- If data set variables include unknowns, the data set replaces them with interpolated (enriched) fields like _INT, or _DTC. For example, the source date is missing the day, the enriched _INT field interpolates the 1st day of the month, and _DTC fields drop the unknown value. If the source field uses dictionary terms, the enriched _TXT field shows the coded terms. 
- RBQM currently does not support building custom QTLs with data sets using datetime operations. 
- When you define an individual condition, the condition is evaluated for whether there is at least one instance where the condition is true across all data in that domain for a given patient. If you build a grouped conditional set, the individual conditions in the set are independently evaluated for truth but not contextually evaluated within the same folder. 
- Select a comparator, such as = or !=, and then select or enter a comparator value.
The list of selectable comparators differs whether you select a date, number, or text variable. The comparator value serves as the conditional threshold, which measures and flags whether specified conditions are met regarding the selected comparator.
 Note : For multiple-record data, similar QTLs with inverse queries may not produce inverse percentage values.

 Note : You cannot edit currently activated custom QTLs.
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > QTLs in the left-hand menu.

- Parameter  – Enter a title for the study variable that you want to assess at the study level. 
- Definition  – Enter more details that explain what the parameter is meant to monitor and how it is measured.
- Reason for Change – Enter the reason for updating the QTL details. 
- Expectation % – Enter the QTL's expected mean value as a percentage based on historical data.
 Note : Your project team should establish the QTL's expected value during the study startup and before data collection begins. This helps avoid potential bias influenced by preexisting knowledge and assumptions from historical data from previous studies, literature, and other avenues.
- Final Population (# of patients) – Total number of patients expected to enroll in the study.

- Select a comparator, such as = or !=, and then select or enter a comparator value.
The list of selectable comparators differs whether you select a date, number, or text variable. The comparator value serves as the conditional threshold, which measures and flags whether specified conditions are met regarding the selected comparator.
 Note : For multiple-record data, similar QTLs with inverse queries may not produce inverse percentage values.

- Optional . To add conditions to the expression, click, drag, and drop  or to the block within the Numerator Query that contains Add Condition . You can add as many conditions as you need.
- AND  – Specifies that all individual conditions and conditions grouped within a grouped conditional set must be met for the expression to be considered true. 
- OR  – Specifies that at least one individual condition or grouped conditional set must be met for the expression to be considered true. 
- Repeat Steps 3-5 to build as many conditions as needed. 
- If necessary, close any grouped conditional sets using   and  .
 Tip : The Numerator Expression section details the full condition set as you build to help you determine if the logic you are configuring is correct. You can click Hide Preview to hide the Expression section.
- Optional.  If you want the QTL to target specific data population subsets, follow steps 5-9 but perform the steps in the Denominator Query . 
- When finished building the expressions, click Save .
The updated custom QTL appears in the Quality Tolerance Limits list as inactive by default. To learn how to activate QTLs, see Activate and Deactivate QTLs .

===== PAGE: add_and_manage_critical_data.html | Add and Manage Critical Data =====
## Add and Manage Critical Data
 You can identify and include as part of your risk assessment the data that is most critical to your study outcome . For example, administrative and demographic information, diagnosis, treatment, prescription drugs, laboratory tests, physiologic monitoring data, hospitalization, patient insurance , and so on. 
 Adding critical data to the risk assessment helps you focus on and monitor the most important data to ensure:
- Protocol compliance, patient safety, data quality, and data integrity. 
- Product or treatment efficacy. 
 You can:
- Add critical data to the risk assessment. 
- Add and manage the risks associated with critical data. 
- View the critical data and their associated high-level details included in the risk assessment. 
- View the risks associated with critical data. 
- Edit critical data details. 
- Delete critical data. 
- View and export Critical Data Audit Reports. 
 Note : S tudy data automatically refreshes twice daily at approximately 9:00am (EST) and 9:00pm (EST), and the data presented within the user interface is current as of 11:00 pm (EST) the previous day, and 11:00 am (EST) the same day, respectively. Each study data refresh produces a data snapshot. Updated data from Medidata Rave and  activated datasets from Data Connect  is available in 12 to 18 hours within  RBQM.   For more information, see  Clinical Data Studio Data Pipeline . 
## Add Critical Data to the Risk Assessment
 You can identify and include as part of your risk assessment the data that is most critical to your study outcome . For example, administrative and demographic information, diagnosis, treatment, prescription drugs, laboratory tests, physiologic monitoring data, hospitalization, patient insurance , and so on. 
 You can add critical data by: 
- Creating new critical data at the study level. 
- Using a preexisting study-level critical data template. 
 When adding critical data, you can configure specific data points associated with the critical data that you want to flag as critical to the study and track for risk.
 Adding critical data to the risk assessment helps you focus and monitor the most important data to ensure:
- Protocol compliance, patient safety, data quality, and data integrity. 
- Product or treatment efficacy. 
 Tip : After adding a critical data to the risk assessment, you can associate risks to the critical data . And then in addition, you can:
- Associate QTLs , KRIs , and risk mitigations to the risk. 
- Monitor the risk in the Risk Inventory . 
- Manage the risk from the Risk Assessment or Risk Inventory . 
- Access RBQM , and then click Risk Assessment > Critical Data in the left-hand menu. 
- On the Critical Data page, click Add Critical Data .
- Click the Critical Data menu, and do one of the following: 
- To add a new, unique critical data, select >>New Critical Data . 
- To add a critical data from a critical data template that resides at the client division or study group level, click a template name. 
- Select or enter the following: 
- Name – Enter up to 255 characters as the name of the critical data, for example, Tumor Assessment. This is a required field. The name must be unique. 
- Category – This is a required field. 
 Unable to render {include} The included page could not be found.
- Group Name – Optional . Enter up to 225 characters describing the type of critical data, for example, Oncology. The group name does not have to be unique. 
- Description – Optional . Enter up to 3000 characters to provide a more detailed description of the critical data. For example, "CT scan of a tumor at visit 5." 
- Rationale – Optional . Enter up to 3000 characters to provide the reason for the critical data. For example, "Data supports the primary endpoint of the study." 
- Optional . In Data Points , select the following: 
- Data Set – The study data set containing specific data points associated with the critical data that you want to flag as critical to the study and track for risk. 
- Variable – The variables associated with a critical data that you want to flag as critical to the study and track for risk.
 Tip : Click the Plus icon, , to add more data points. Click the X icon, , to remove data points.
 Note : When configuring  data listings , custom KRIs , and  patient profile design elements , the list of available data sets appends the names of d ata sets and variables containing critical data points with a blue flag . The blue flag does not appear next to data set and variable names containing the newly added critical data points until the next data refresh.
- Click Save .
 Note : When you add study-level critical data, it is available only for your study. Contact your administrator if you believe that the critical data belongs in the list of client division templates.
## Flag Data Points in Critical Data Elements
 When adding and managing a Risk Assessment's critical data elements, you can  associate   specific study data points   to the critical data elements. When you associate data points to critical data elements, then when  configuring data listings , custom KRIs , and  patient profile design elements , the list of available data sets appends the names of d ata sets and variables containing critical data points with a blue flag .  
 Flagging critical data points helps your study team to proactively identify and monitor threats to data quality and integrity when reviewing data and when configuring: 
- Data listings 
- Custom KRIs 
- Patient profile design elements . 
- Do one of the following: 
- Add critical data to the risk assessment . 
- Edit critical data details. 
- In  Data Points , select the following: 
- Data Set  – The study data set containing specific data points associated with the critical data that you want to flag as critical to the study and track for risk. 
- Variable  – The variables associated with a critical data that you want to flag as critical to the study and track for risk.
 Tip : Click the Plus icon, , to add more data points. Click the X icon, , to remove data points.
- Click  Save .
 Notes
- The list of data sets in the Listings, KRI Configuration, and Patient Profiles capabilities do not append a  blue flag next to data set and variables names containing the newly added critical data points until the next data refresh. 
- Data points configured as critical will not show as flagged critical data points throughout Clinical Data Studio until the next system data refresh.

- Add and associate risks to critical data. 
- View and edit critical data risks. 
- Link and unlink QTLs to critical data risks. 
- View and edit the details of QTLs associated with risks. 
- Evaluate the performance of QTLs associated with risks. 
- Link and unlink Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) to critical data risks. 
- View and edit the details of KRIs associated with risks. 
- Add, view, edit, and delete critical data risk mitigations. 
- Mark critical data risks as reviewed. 
- Close critical data risks. 
- Delete critical data risks. 
 To learn more, see: 
- Add and Manage Risks 
- View and Monitor the Risk Inventory 
- Add and Manage QTLs Associated with Risks 
- Add and Manage KRIs Associated with Risks 
- Add and Manage Risk Mitigations

- As a reference for another study's risk assessment. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Risk Assessment > Critical Data in the left-hand menu.
The Critical Data page > Critical Data table shows the following details for all critical data included in the active risk assessment:
 Column Descriptions 
- Name – The unique name of the critical data; for example, Tumor Assessment. 
- Category –  
 Unable to render {include} The included page could not be found.
- Group Name – A user-entered description of the type of critical data; for example, Oncology. 
- Data Points – The number of specific study data points associated with a critical data that are flagged as critical to the study. 
- #Risks – The number of risks associated with the critical data.
 Tip : On the Critical Data table, you can click the Down Arrow , , to the left of a critical data name to view the list of risks associated with that critical data.
- Add Risk – Click to add a new risk to associate with the critical data. To learn more, see Add and Manage Risks . 
 Tip : To filter the Critical Data table to show only critical data assigned to a specific category, click the View by menu, and then select a category.
## View the Risks Associated with Critical Data
 You can view the list of risks associated with critical data in your risk assessment. For example, you can view the critical data risks:
- For oversight to ensure the study team is following the risk plan, or 
- As a reference for another study's risk assessment. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Risk Assessment > Critical Data in the left-hand menu.
 The Critical Data page appears. 
- Optional . To filter the Critical Data table to show only critical data assigned to a specific category, click the View by menu, and then select a category. 
- On the Critical Data table, click the Down Arrow , , to the left of the critical data name whose risks you want to view.
A table shows the list of risks associated with the critical data and the following risk details:
 Column Descriptions 
- Risk ID – The risk's system-assigned unique ID. You can click a risk ID to view and edit the risk review details . 
- Risk Name – The name of the risk. 
- Review Status – A color-coded pill icon shows the review status for each risk associated with the critical data:
- Red – Overdue. The Current Date > Target Review Date, indicating the risk review is overdue. 
- Yellow – Due Soon. The Current Date is between Last Review Date and Target Review Date, indicating the risk review is due soon. 
- Green – Reviewed. The Last Review Date = Current Date, indicating the risk is reviewed. 
- Gray – Closed. The Risk Status is closed. 
- Risk Score – A calculated number (score) that reflects the risk's severity. When adding a risk or updating a risk's review details, you can score each of the following risk factors, Probability, Impact, and Detectability, on a scale of 1 to 3. The risk score is calculated by multiplying each risk factor's score together (Probability x Impact x Detectability). The maximum risk score is 27. 
- A risk score of 1-3 appears with a green color-coded block and indicates a minimal risk. 
- A risk score of 4-9 appears with a yellow color-coded block and indicates a moderate risk. 
- A risk score of 10-27 appears with a red color-coded black and indicates a high risk.

- Rationale – Optional . Enter up to 3000 characters to provide the reason for the critical data. For example, "Data supports the primary endpoint of the study." 
- Optional . In Data Points , select the following:

## View and Export Critical Data Audit Reports
 Audit Reports allow you to  track actions made on the critical data in your study . This provides a single, traceable record of updates for audit readiness. For example, you can 
- Identify specific changes that were made (like, adding critical data to the risk assessment). 
- Track the study personnel who made updates. 
- Identify when the updates were made. 
 Note:   You require permissions to view the audit trail. To learn more, see   RBQM Building Blocks and Permissions .
- Access RBQM , and then click   Risk Assessment > Critical Data   in the left-hand menu. The Critical Data page shows. 
- Click the Clock     icon next to the page header. A new browser tab opens to the Audit Viewer > Critical Data Audit Report page. 
- Optional: You can click  Show Filters above the upper-right corner of the table to filter the reports by Start Date and End Date .  
 Tip :     In Audit Viewer, you can click   Export   and then  Excel ,   CSV , or   PDF   to  download the report locally and view offline or sort data by column headings. Report exports include the entire history, regardless of the filters applied in the Audit Viewer window. 
 Important:  Critical Data Audit Report records actions made on critical data in your study after 30-July-2026. Any actions made on critical data prior to this date is excluded from the audit report.
 Note:   Any changes to risks on Critical Data page will be recorded in Risk Inventory Audit Report. To learn more, see Generate Risk Inventory Audit Report . 
## Delete Critical Data
 You can delete a critical data from the risk assessment. For example, if you must update the risk assessment critical data based on a protocol amendment or a critical data was added to the risk assessment in error.
- Access RBQM , and then click Risk Assessment > Critical Data in the left-hand menu.
- On the Critical Data page, click the Actions menu, , on the far right of the row of the critical data you want to delete.
- Click Delete .

===== PAGE: add_and_manage_elements.html | Add and Manage Elements =====
## Add and Manage Elements
 The workflow progress bar below depicts where adding elements occurs within the recommended patient profile design workflow. 
 Elements are containers of study information that serve as the building blocks for your profile designs. 
## About Elements
 Elements are containers of information that comprise a set of related patient data. You configure the structure, display, and types of information to include in your profiles by adding elements to your profile design. You then populate your elements with variables. For example, you can add a Vital Signs table to your design. You would then add individual variables such as 'patient start date,' 'event name,' or 'blood pressure' to each column within the table. The Patient Profiles design work space allows you to quickly access the variables in your data sets from which you can click-and-drag to populate the elements in your design. 
 Patient Profiles provides the following element types: 
- Add and Manage Headers 
- Add, Edit, and Delete Tables 
- Add, Edit, and Delete Timelines 
 You can: 
- add elements , 
- duplicate elements , 
- delete elements ,  
- append notes to elements , 
- hide elements with no data , 
- copy elements between studies . 
## Add Elements
- 
 Access the design. 
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click Patient Profiles in the left-hand menu.
 The Patient Profile Designs page shows the Published Designs and Draft Designs   tabs, which contain the list of designs in your study environment. 
- On the Patient Profiles Designs page, do one of the following: 
- Click the Published Designs tab.
 Published Designs Tab Column Descriptions 
- Name  – The patient profile design's name. 
- Type – Indicates whether the patient profile is one of the following types: 
- Detect – The patient profile design is integrated with an accessible directly from other Data Surveillance and RBQM capabilities. 
- View Only – A read-only patient profile design. 
- Last Refresh Date – The time stamp when the last data refresh was performed for the profile design. 
- Published Date  – The time stamp when the profile design was marked as master. This field displays for Published Designs. 
- Updated By  – The user who most recently updated the patient profile design. 
- Click the Draft Designs tab.
 Draft Designs Tab Column Descriptions 
- Name  – The patient profile design's name. 
- Last Updated – The time stamp of when the most recent update was made to the draft patient profile design. 
- Updated By  – The user who most recently updated the patient profile design. 
- Optional . Click any column header to sort the designs list. Clicking once sorts the list in descending order (A to Z, 0 to 9) by the selected column header; twice sorts in ascending order (Z to A, 9 to 0).
 Note : Published Designs and Draft Designs lists appear in the reverse chronological order based on the Published Date and the Last Updated dates, respectively. 
- Click anywhere within the row of the design you want to access. 
 The Design page appears and shows the Profiles tab by default.

## Hide Elements with No Data
 You can configure tables and graphs to show only elements that have data present in a profile design. Hiding elements without data enables you to better focus on pertinent information to create a more targeted patient profile analysis. 
- 
 Access the design. 
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click Patient Profiles in the left-hand menu.
 The Patient Profile Designs page shows the Published Designs and Draft Designs   tabs, which contain the list of designs in your study environment. 
- On the Patient Profiles Designs page, do one of the following: 
- Click the Published Designs tab.
 Published Designs Tab Column Descriptions 
- Name  – The patient profile design's name. 
- Type – Indicates whether the patient profile is one of the following types: 
- Detect – The patient profile design is integrated with an accessible directly from other Data Surveillance and RBQM capabilities. 
- View Only – A read-only patient profile design. 
- Last Refresh Date – The time stamp when the last data refresh was performed for the profile design. 
- Published Date  – The time stamp when the profile design was marked as master. This field displays for Published Designs. 
- Updated By  – The user who most recently updated the patient profile design. 
- Click the Draft Designs tab.
 Draft Designs Tab Column Descriptions 
- Name  – The patient profile design's name. 
- Last Updated – The time stamp of when the most recent update was made to the draft patient profile design. 
- Updated By  – The user who most recently updated the patient profile design. 
- Optional . Click any column header to sort the designs list. Clicking once sorts the list in descending order (A to Z, 0 to 9) by the selected column header; twice sorts in ascending order (Z to A, 9 to 0).
 Note : Published Designs and Draft Designs lists appear in the reverse chronological order based on the Published Date and the Last Updated dates, respectively. 
- Click anywhere within the row of the design you want to access. 
 The Design page appears and shows the Profiles tab by default. 
- On the Design page > Elements tab, click an element type in the  Add element  section. 
- Under Table Options, select Hide "No Data" Elements . The Elements appear as per the following options:
 Elements Display 
- If you select  Hide "No Data" Elements , and there is no data for the patient in the data set: 
- The element does not appear. 
- If under Graph Options, you select Table and Graph: Show Both , when applicable, the element and graph do not appear. 
- If under Graph Options, you select Table and Graph: Graph Only , the graph does not appear. 
- If you set up an expression under Table Options > Conditional Options > Display Conditions > Row to show data with specific values, for example, where AE Serious = Y: 
- the element does not appear if no data in the data set meets the conditional criteria, for example, the patient has had adverse events, but not serious AEs. 
- and also set up the element to show the graph, when applicable, the element and the graph do not appear if no data in the data set meets the conditional criteria. 
- and under Graph Options, you select Table and Graph: Graph Only , the graph does not show if no data in the data set meets the conditional criteria.
- If there is data for the patient in the data set, then irrespective of whether you select  Hide "No Data" Elements: 
- The element appears. 
- If under Graph Options, you select Table and Graph: Show Both , when applicable, the element and graph appear. 
- If under Graph Options, you select Table and Graph: Graph Only , the graph appears. 
- If you set up an expression under Table Options > Conditional Options > Display Conditions > Row to show data with specific values, for example, where AE Serious = Y: 
- the element appears if data in the data set meets the conditional criteria, for example, the patient has had adverse events, but not serious AEs. If the element is an event table, the event table appears in the timeline and in the legend. 
- and also set up the element to show both the graph, when applicable, the element and the graph appear if data in the data set meets the conditional criteria. 
- and under Graph Options, you select Table and Graph: Graph Only , the graph appears if data in the data set meets the conditional criteria, for example, the patient has had adverse events, but not serious AEs. 
 If you do not select  Hide "No Data" Elements, and there is no data for the patient in the data set:
- The element shows a No Data message. 
- If under Graph Options, you select Table and Graph: Show Both , the element shows a No Data message and the graph appears empty. 
- If under Graph Options, you select Table and Graph: Graph Only , the graph appears empty. 
- If you set up an expression under Table Options > Conditional Options > Display Conditions > Row to show data with specific values, for example, where AE Serious = Y: 
- the element shows a No Data message, if there is no data in the data set that meets the conditional criteria, for example, the patient has had adverse events, but not serious AEs. If the element is an event table, the event table appears in the timeline and in the legend. 
- and also set up the element to show the graph, when applicable, the element shows a No Data message and the graph appears empty, if there is no data in the data set that meets the conditional criteria. 
- and under Graph Options, you select Table and Graph: Graph Only , the graph appears empty, if there is no data in the data set that meets the conditional criteria.

===== PAGE: add_and_manage_flags.html | Add and Manage Flags =====
## Add and Manage Flags
 You can add  %KRIs  as flags to headers in your profile design. KRIs are predefined metrics that enable you during the study to systematically: 
- Identify and track known or anticipated risks to data quality, 
- Evaluate country and site performance in a study, and 
- Ensure study conduct operates as planned. 
 Adding %KRIs as flags allow you to gauge a patient's status and the study's progress. 
 You can also r emove flags from headers. 
 Note : Your team can create and activate percentage KRIs in RBQM's KRI Configuration capability. To learn more, see:
- KRI Configuration 
- Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs 
- Activate and Deactivate KRIs

===== PAGE: add_and_manage_headers.html | Add and Manage Headers =====
## Add and Manage Headers
 Headers identify the information contained in a section within the profile. Headers also hold variable information. Rows without headers—such as patient information tables, which contain information only—benefit from having headers atop the row to label and define the table.
 You can:
- Add headers 
- Copy headers 
- Name and rename headers 
- Add header rows 
- Rename header variables 
- Change the placement of a header row 
- Remove header rows 
- Append notes to headers

 The Patient Profile Designs page shows the Published Designs and Draft Designs   tabs, which contain the list of designs in your study environment. 
- On the Patient Profiles Designs page, do one of the following: 
- Click the Published Designs tab.
 Published Designs Tab Column Descriptions 
- Name  – The patient profile design's name. 
- Type – Indicates whether the patient profile is one of the following types: 
- Detect – The patient profile design is integrated with an accessible directly from other Data Surveillance and RBQM capabilities. 
- View Only – A read-only patient profile design. 
- Last Refresh Date – The time stamp when the last data refresh was performed for the profile design. 
- Published Date  – The time stamp when the profile design was marked as master. This field displays for Published Designs. 
- Updated By  – The user who most recently updated the patient profile design. 
- Click the Draft Designs tab.
 Draft Designs Tab Column Descriptions 
- Name  – The patient profile design's name. 
- Last Updated – The time stamp of when the most recent update was made to the draft patient profile design. 
- Updated By  – The user who most recently updated the patient profile design. 
- Optional . Click any column header to sort the designs list. Clicking once sorts the list in descending order (A to Z, 0 to 9) by the selected column header; twice sorts in ascending order (Z to A, 9 to 0).
 Note : Published Designs and Draft Designs lists appear in the reverse chronological order based on the Published Date and the Last Updated dates, respectively. 
- Click anywhere within the row of the design you want to access. 
 The Design page appears and shows the Profiles tab by default. 
- On the Design page, click the Elements tab. 
- In the Saved elements table, click the name of the header you want to update. 
- Click  within the header row you want to remove from the header.

===== PAGE: add_and_manage_kris_associated_with_risks.html | Add and Manage KRIs Associated with Risks =====
## Add and Manage KRIs Associated with Risks
 Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) are predefined study metrics that enable you for the duration of the study to systematically:  
- Identify and track known or anticipated risks to data quality. 
- Evaluate country and site performance in a study. 
- Ensure study conduct operates as planned. 
 Examples of KRIs include patient accrual rates and data query rates.
 You can track KRI performance using KRI values . KRI value calculations reflect as a percentage, count, mean, rate, or standard deviation. 
 You can:
- Link KRIs to risks to evaluate and monitor whether the risk level is improving based on how you are managing or mitigating the risks. 
- View and edit the details of KRIs associated with risks 
- Unlink KRIs from risks. 
 To learn more about KRIs, see About Key Risk Indicators .
## Link and Unlink KRIs to Risks
 Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) are predefined study metrics that enable you for the duration of the study to systematically:  
- Identify and track known or anticipated risks to data quality. 
- Evaluate country and site performance in a study. 
- Ensure study conduct operates as planned. 
 Examples of KRIs include patient accrual rates and data query rates.
 You can track KRI performance using KRI values . KRI value calculations reflect as a percentage, count, mean, rate, or standard deviation. 
 You can link KRIs to risks. If necessary, you can also unlink KRIs from risks. To learn more about KRIs, see About Key Risk Indicators .
## Link KRIs to Risks
 You can link KRIs to risks in two ways: 
- You can create a KRI directly in Risk Management. However, this type of KRI's details always require manual entry and updates, even if your instance of Risk Management is integrated with Data Surveillance and RBQM . 
 Note : You can use a KRI created in Risk Management only for tracking purposes. You cannot share a KRI created in Risk Management with Detect currently.
- If your instance of Risk Management is integrated with Medidata Detect, then you can link preconfigured system KRI or custom KRIs derived from KRI Configuration . For such KRIs, the KRI value automatically populates and derives from Medidata Detect's statistical analysis and aligns with KRI Dashboard data refreshes.
 You can access the risks to which you want to associate KRIs in two ways:
- When viewing a holistic view of the risks in your study's risk inventory. 
- When viewing the risks associated with specific critical data, critical processes, or risk categories in the risk assessment. 
- If necessary, do either of the following:
 Access the Risk Inventory. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Risk Assessment > Risks in the left-hand menu. 
The Risk Inventory page appears. 
 Access the critical data, critical processes, or categorization in the Risk Assessment. 
- Access RBQM , and then in the RBQM left-hand menu , do any of the following: 
- To add risks to critical data, click the Critical Data tab.
 The Critical Data page appears. 
- To add risks to critical processes, click the Critical Processes tab.
The Critical Processes page appears.
- To add risks to risk categories, click the Categorization tab.
The Categorization page appears. 
- Do either of the following:
- If on the Risk Inventory page : In the Risks tab > Risks table > Risk ID column, click the Risk ID for the risk to which you want to associate a new KRI. 
- If on the Critical Data page, Critical Processes page, or Categorization page, do one of the following :
- To link KRIs to a new risk : In the Add Risk column, click the blue Plus icon, , in the row of the corresponding critical data, critical process, or risk category to which you want to associate a new risk.
 Note : Before you can add a KRI to a new risk, you must first enter a Risk Name and Review Frequency on the Risk Details tab. To learn more, see Add Risks to the Risk Assessment .
- To link KRIs to an existing risk :  In the Name column, click the Down Arrow , , to the left of the critical data, critical process, or risk category whose risks you want to view, and then in the Risk ID column, click the risk ID to which you want to associate a new KRI. 
- In the Risk Review or Add Risk subpage, click the  KRIs tab. 
- Click the Key Risk Indicator menu, and then do either of the following:
- To create a new, unique KRI, click >> Create New KRI . 
- To link a preconfigured system KRI or custom KRI that already exists in your study's Detect Configuration Manager > KRI Configuration > Key Risk Indicators list, click the name of the KRI you want to use.
 Note : If your instance of Risk Management is integrated with Medidata Detect, then you can select system KRIs and custom KRIs from the Key Risk Indicator menu. If your instance is not integrated with Detect, then you can only select the following system KRIs:
- AE Entry Delay
- Non-System Query Delay
- Number of AEs per Subject-Year
- Number of SAEs per Subject-Year
- Percent Missing Visit
- Percent Non-System Query
- Percent Out of Window Visit
- Percent System Query
- Screen Failure Percentage
- System Query Delay
- Visit Entry Delay
 You cannot edit any system KRI fields in Risk Management. When Detect is integrated with Risk Management, Detect analyzes the data and populates the KRI Value field. Otherwise, the KRI Value field is blank. 
- Select or enter the following: 
 Field Descriptions 
- Name – This field only appears when creating a new, unique KRI. Enter up to 64 characters for the KRI name. 
- Description – Enter up to 255 characters to describe the KRI. Examples include: P atient accrual rates or data query rates. If your instance of Risk Management is integrated with Medidata Detect and the KRI is a system KRI or a custom KRI derived from KRI Configuration, then you cannot edit the Description. The Description entry automatically derives from and gets populated by Detect. 
- Value – Enter a numeric KRI Value from a third-party tool or vendor to track the KRI. This number can come from a third-party system or from a statistical tool you use to calculate KRI values.
 Note : If your instance of Risk Management is integrated with Medidata Detect and the KRI is a system KRI or a custom KRI derived from KRI Configuration, then you cannot edit the value. The KRI value automatically populates and derives from  Medidata Detect's statistical analysis of your study data. 
 Tip : For system KRIs or custom KRIs that derive from KRI Configuration, the Medidata RBQM Metric Status shows one of the following statuses: 
- Integrated – The KRI Value is populated by Detect. 
- Not Available – Appears when: 
- Your instance of Risk Management is not integrated with Medidata Detect, or
- The KRI Value analysis from Medidata Detect is unavailable.
 Note : If your instance of Risk Management is integrated with Medidata Detect, check with your Detect data administrator to determine why the KRI analysis data is not being pulled into Risk Management. The refresh of KRI analysis data in Risk Management occurs simultaneously with the refresh of KRI Dashboard data.
 The Medidata RBQM Metric Status does not appear for KRIs that were originally created in Risk Management .
- Click Save . 
## Unlink KRIs to Risks
 You can unlink KRIs to risks; for example, if you no longer deem the KRI as a good measurement of risk performance.
 Note : If your instance of Risk Management is integrated with Medidata Detect, and the KRI you want to unlink is integrated with KRI Configuration, then unlinking the KRI only removes its association from the risk in Risk Management. The KRI remains stored in KRI Configuration and is available to link to risks again in Risk Management.
 You can access the risks to which you want to unlink KRIs in three ways:
- When viewing a holistic view of the risks in your study's risk inventory. 
- When viewing a holistic view of the KRIs associated with risks in your study. 
- When viewing the risks associated with specific critical data, critical processes, or risk categories in the risk assessment. 
- If necessary, do either of the following:
 Access the Risk Inventory. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Risk Assessment > Risks in the left-hand menu. 
The Risk Inventory page appears. 
 Access the critical data, critical processes, or categorization in the Risk Assessment. 
- Access RBQM , and then in the RBQM left-hand menu , do any of the following: 
- To add risks to critical data, click the Critical Data tab.
 The Critical Data page appears. 
- To add risks to critical processes, click the Critical Processes tab.
The Critical Processes page appears.
- To add risks to risk categories, click the Categorization tab.
The Categorization page appears. 
- Do either of the following:
- If on the Risk Inventory page, do either of the following :
- In the Risks tab > Risks table > Risk ID column, click the Risk ID containing the KRI you want to unlink. 
- Click the KRIs tab, and then in the Attached to Risk ID column, click the risk ID containing the KRI you want to unlink. 
- If on the Critical Data page, Critical Processes page, or Categorization page, do one of the following : In the Name column, click the Down Arrow , , to the left of the critical data, critical process, or risk category whose risks you want to view, and then in the Risk ID column, click the risk ID containing the KRI you want to unlink. 
- In the Risk Review subpage, click the  KRIs tab. 
- If necessary, if there are multiple KRIs associated with the risk, click the down arrow next to the KRIs tab, and select the KRI you want to unlink from the risk.
- To the right of the Key Risk Indicator field, click Remove KRI .
The KRI is no longer listed in the Risk Review window > KRIs tab, and the KRI is no longer linked to the risk.

===== PAGE: add_and_manage_qtls_associated_with_risks.html | Add and Manage QTLs Associated with Risks =====
## Add and Manage QTLs Associated with Risks
 QTLs are study-level metrics that indicate if a study parameter's reported data has breached a preidentified data quality threshold or upper limit . QTLs monitor the emergence of systematic errors on critical variables and data that can be prone to subjective bias, ultimately impacting: 
- Patient safety 
- Study conduct and performance 
- Compliance 
- Data quality 
- Study reliability 
 You can: 
- Link QTLs to risks to evaluate and monitor whether the risk level is improving based on how you are managing or mitigating the risks. 
- View and edit the details of QTLs associated with risks. 
- Document QTL deviations. 
- Unlink QTLs from risks. 
 To learn more about QTLs, see About Quality Tolerance Limits . 
## Link and Unlink QTLs to Risks
 QTLs are study-level metrics that indicate if a study parameter's reported data has breached a preidentified data quality threshold or upper limit . QTLs monitor the emergence of systematic errors on critical variables and data that can be prone to subjective bias, ultimately impacting: 
- Patient safety 
- Study conduct and performance 
- Compliance 
- Data quality 
- Study reliability 
 You can link QTLs to risks. If necessary, you can also unlink QTLs from risks. To learn more about QTLs, see About Quality Tolerance Limits . 
## Link QTLs to Risks
 You can link QTLs to risks in two ways: 
- Create new, unique QTLs directly within the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory. 
- Add preconfigured QTLs to the risk assessment from the RBQM Configuration > QTL Configuration capability. 
 You can then manage QTL details and track QTL performance in several ways. You can: 
- Manually enter and update QTL details such as expectation , observed value, threshold , and upper limit . Manually maintained QTLs are not integrated with the rest of RBQM. RBQM does not conduct statistical analysis on these types of QTLs.  
- Create QTLs in Risk Assessment or QTL Configuration. 
- Link a QTL originally created in Risk Assessment with RBQM so that: 
- The QTL gets stored and updated in the RBQM Configuration > QTL Configuration module. After linking, subsequent QTL updates made in QTL Configuration propagate to the QTL in Risk Assessment. 
- RBQM consumes the QTL, and if activated , produces the QTL's performance analysis in the QTL Dashboard, Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory with each data refresh. 
 To learn more about how to read QTL graphs, see Evaluate the Performance of QTLs Associated with Risks . 
 You can access the risks to which you want to associate QTLs in two ways:
- When viewing a holistic view of the risks in your study's risk inventory. 
- When viewing the risks associated with specific critical data, critical processes, or risk categories in the risk assessment. 
- If necessary, do either of the following:
 Access the Risk Inventory. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Risk Assessment > Risks in the left-hand menu. 
The Risk Inventory page appears. 
 Access the critical data, critical processes, or categorization in the Risk Assessment. 
- Access RBQM , and then in the RBQM left-hand menu , do any of the following: 
- To add risks to critical data, click the Critical Data tab.
 The Critical Data page appears. 
- To add risks to critical processes, click the Critical Processes tab.
The Critical Processes page appears.
- To add risks to risk categories, click the Categorization tab.
The Categorization page appears. 
- Do either of the following:
- If on the Risk Inventory page : In the Risks tab > Risks table > Risk ID column, click the Risk ID for the risk to which you want to associate a new QTL. 
- If on the Critical Data page, Critical Processes page, or Categorization page, do one of the following :
- To link QTLs to a new risk : In the Add Risk column, click the blue Plus icon, , in the row of the corresponding critical data, critical process, or risk category to which you want to associate a new risk.
 Note : Before you can add a QTL to a new risk, you must first enter a Risk Name , Date Entered , and Review Frequency on the risk's Details tab. To learn more, see  Add Risks to the Risk Assessment .
- To link QTLs to an existing risk :  In the Name column, click the Down Arrow , , to the left of the critical data, critical process, or risk category whose risks you want to view, and then in the Risk ID column, click the risk ID to which you want to associate a new QTL. 
- In the Risk Review or Add Risk subpage, click the  QTLs tab. 
- Click the Quality Tolerance Limit (QTL) menu, and then do either of the following:
- To create a new, unique QTL, click >> Create New QTL . 
- To link a preconfigured study-level QTL that already exists in the RBQM Configuration > QTL Configuration > Quality Tolerance Limits list, click the name of the QTL you want to use.
 Note : Only QTLs that are currently activated in QTL Configuration show in the Quality Tolerance Limit (QTL) menu. To learn more, see  Activate and Deactivate QTLs . 
- Select or enter the following:
 Field Descriptions 
- Name (Required) – This is a parameter required for defining the QTL. Enter up to 255 characters for the name of the QTL. This is a required field if you are creating your own tracking QTL. You can edit this field. When the QTL is integrated with the RBQM Configuration, the updated name appears in both applications. A parameter is a study variable that is assessed at the study level.  When used in the context of a QTL, parameters are measures that detect potential issues that can  be mitigated. Example: The percentage or number of participants with premature discontinuation of the investigational drug. 
- Definition – Enter up to 500 characters to define the QTL. Include how the QTL gets measured. Example: P ercentage of participants randomized who do not meet inclusion/exclusion criteria. 
 Note: When the Share QTL toggle on the right side of the QTLs tab is On, you cannot edit the following fields: Expectation, Observed Value, Threshold, Upper Limit, Final Population, and Trigger Point.
 Instead, the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory automatically populates these fields based on how each QTL is configured in QTL Configuration and based on the QTL's performance metrics from  QTL Dashboard . The data in these fields update in alignment with the scheduled and manually triggered data refreshes performed in QTL Dashboard . 
- Expectation – T he expected percentage of the patient population that will not meet the study parameter's criteria. QTL percentages that RBQM assesses as in range of the expectation are considered healthy and do not require any action. 
- Observed Value – T he observed percentage of patients that do not meet the study parameter's criteria as of the most recent data analysis. For example, in RBQM, this value comes from the date RBQM performed a data analysis on your study data. For QTLs that are not integrated with RBQM, the percentage entered in the Observed Value field appears as Observed Today % in the QTL graph.   
- Threshold – The minimum percentage of the patient population that cannot meet the study parameter's criteria before RBQM considers the parameter to be at risk. P arameters whose QTL values exceed the threshold indicate potential underlying systemic issues, which can compromise study safety and integrity. You should investigate such parameters to determine the root cause and to prevent or mitigate study issues. The Threshold value must be less than the Upper Limit.  
- Upper Limit – The minimum percentage of the patient population that cannot meet the study parameter's criteria before RBQM considers the parameter to be high risk. P arameters whose QTL values exceed the upper limit indicate potential underlying systemic issues, which can compromise study safety and integrity. You should investigate such parameters to determine the root cause and to prevent or mitigate study issues. 
- Final Population (#No. of Subjects) (Required for shared QTLs) – Total number of patients expected to enroll in the study. The final population should be equal to or more than the expected population. This field is hidden if the Share QTL button is switched to Off. 
- Trigger Point (Required for shared QTLs) – The minimum required number of patients that meet the QTL's conditions for RBQM to analyze and produce the QTL's results in the QTL Dashboard. This field is hidden if the Share QTL button is switched to Off. 
- Modification Note (Required) – When initially linking a preexisting QTL to a risk or editing an existing QTL, you must add a note explaining the modification. The Modification Note field does not show if you create a new QTL. 
- Action Plan – Enter up to 2000 characters to explain the action required if a QTL is exceeded.  
- Deviations – Deviations occur when the QTL value has breached the QTL's predefined threshold or upper limit . Detection of deviations from the predefined quality tolerance limits should trigger an evaluation to determine if action is needed. You can document QTL deviations by clicking   Add and then selecting or entering the following:
- Start Date – Select the date in which the QTL value initially exceeded the QTL threshold. 
- End Date – Optional . Select the date in which the QTL value returned below the QTL threshold. 
- Occurrence – Enter the maximum value of the QTL threshold breach. 
- Action Taken and Outcome/Impact on the Trial – If a QTL is exceeded, explain the deviation. Enter up to 2000 characters describing the rationale if the trial results are still acceptable. (For example, for submission for marketing authorization or for analyzing the safety profile of a marketed compound.) Clearly state if the results are not valid. 
- Justification for Quality Tolerance Limit – Enter up to 500 characters describing the rationale and any limitations to the use of the subject of the QTL.  
- Justification for Expectation –  Enter up to 500 characters of published data or historical data from previous trials within the organization. When referencing historical data, it is important to state whether systematic issues have been excluded. 
- Justification for Threshold – Enter up to 500 characters explaining the rationale for the value set in place for the QTL threshold. For example, why would a QTL value exceeding the threshold be cause for concern? 
- Algorithms – Enter an explanation of the algorithm used to produce the QTL metrics for traceability and auditing purposes. 
- Source of Data – If the Share QTL button is switched to On, then this field automatically populates with Detect as the field entry and is noneditable. 
- Supporting Details – Enter any extra or miscellaneous QTL information you want documented. 
- Optional . Toggle the Share QTL button to On , , to link the QTL with RBQM so that: 
- The QTL gets stored and updated in the RBQM Configuration > QTL Configuration capability. After linking, subsequent QTL updates made in QTL Configuration propagate to the QTL in the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory. 
- RBQM consumes the QTL, and if the QTL is activated , then RBQM produces the QTL's performance analysis in the QTL Dashboard, Risk Assessment, and Risk Inventory with each data refresh.
 Note: Special Notes About Shared QTLs
- The Share QTL toggle is set to Off by default when you create when you initially link a QTL to a risk. Ensure that the Share QTL toggle is On  if you want to share the QTL with RBQM. 
- You can hover your cursor on the Information icon, , next to the Medidata RBQM Metric field to confirm whether the QTL is currently integrated with the RBQM.  
- When the Share QTL toggle is  On , then the toggle is set to On for every risk using that QTL. Switching the toggle to Off turns sharing off for every risk using that QTL.  
- QTL Dashboard provides analysis data to the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory for shared QTLs so long as the QTL is activated in RBQM Configuration. Check with your RBQM data administrator to determine the frequency of the refresh cycle for analysis data sent to the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory. The refresh of QTL analysis data in the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory occurs simultaneously with the refresh of QTL Dashboard data.  
- Click Save .
 Tip : To learn how to read and understand the QTL graph in the QTLs tab, see Evaluate the Performance of QTLs Associated with Risks .

The QTL remains stored in QTL Configuration and is available to link to risks again in Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory.

- If on the Critical Data page, Critical Processes page, or Categorization page, do one of the following : In the Name column, click the Down Arrow , , to the left of the critical data, critical process, or risk category whose risks you want to view, and then in the Risk ID column, click the risk ID containing the QTL you want to unlink.

- In the Risk Review subpage, click the  QTLs tab. 
- If necessary, if there are multiple QTLs associated with the risk, click the down arrow next to the QTLs tab, and select the QTL you want to view or edit.
- View, select, or enter the following:
 Field Descriptions 
- Name (Required) – This is a parameter required for defining the QTL. Enter up to 255 characters for the name of the QTL. This is a required field if you are creating your own tracking QTL. You can edit this field in the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory. When the QTL is integrated with the RBQM Configuration, the updated name appears in both applications. A parameter is a study variable that is assessed at the study level.  When used in the context of a QTL, parameters are measures that detect potential issues that can  be mitigated. Example: The percentage or number of participants with premature discontinuation of the investigational drug. 
- Definition – Enter up to 500 characters to define the QTL. Include how the QTL is measured. Example: P ercentage of participants randomized who do not meet inclusion/exclusion criteria. 
 Note: When the Share QTL toggle on the right side of the QTLs tab is On, you cannot edit the following fields: Expectation, Observed Value, Threshold, Upper Limit, Final Population, and Trigger Point.
 Instead, the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory automatically populates these fields based on how each QTL is configured in QTL Configuration and based on the QTL's performance metrics from  QTL Dashboard . The data in these fields update in alignment with the scheduled and manually triggered data refreshes performed in QTL Dashboard . 
- Expectation – T he expected percentage of the patient population that will not meet the study parameter's criteria. QTL percentages that RBQM assesses as in range of the expectation are considered healthy and do not require any action. 
- Observed Value – T he observed percentage of patients that do not meet the study parameter's criteria as of the most recent data analysis. For example, in RBQM, this value comes from the date RBQM performed a data analysis on your study data. For QTLs that are not integrated with RBQM, the percentage entered in the Observed Value field appears as Observed Today % in the QTL graph.   
- Threshold – The minimum percentage of the patient population that cannot meet the study parameter's criteria before RBQM considers the parameter to be at risk. P arameters whose QTL values exceed the threshold indicate potential underlying systemic issues, which can compromise study safety and integrity. You should investigate such parameters to determine the root cause and to prevent or mitigate study issues. The Threshold value must be less than the Upper Limit.  
- Upper Limit – The minimum percentage of the patient population that cannot meet the study parameter's criteria before RBQM considers the parameter to be high risk. P arameters whose QTL values exceed the upper limit indicate potential underlying systemic issues, which can compromise study safety and integrity. You should investigate such parameters to determine the root cause and to prevent or mitigate study issues. 
- Final Population (#No. of Subjects) (Required for shared QTLs) – Total number of patients expected to enroll in the study. The final population should be equal to or more than the expected population. This field is hidden if the Share QTL button is switched to Off. 
- Trigger Point (Required for shared QTLs) – The minimum required number of patients that meet the QTL's conditions for RBQM to analyze and produce the QTL's results in the QTL Dashboard. This field is hidden if the Share QTL button is switched to Off. 
- Modification Note (Required) – When initially linking a preexisting QTL to a risk or editing an existing QTL, you must add a note explaining the modification. The Modification Note field does not show if you create a new QTL. 
- Action Plan – Enter up to 2000 characters to explain the action required if a QTL is exceeded.  
- Deviations – Deviations occur when the QTL value has breached the QTL's predefined threshold or upper limit . Detection of deviations from the predefined quality tolerance limits should trigger an evaluation to determine if action is needed. You can document QTL deviations by clicking   Add and then selecting or entering the following:
- Start Date – Select the date in which the QTL value initially exceeded the QTL threshold. 
- End Date – Optional . Select the date in which the QTL value returned below the QTL threshold. 
- Occurrence – Enter the maximum value of the QTL threshold breach. 
- Action Taken and Outcome/Impact on the Trial – If a QTL is exceeded, explain the deviation. Enter up to 2000 characters describing the rationale if the trial results are still acceptable. (For example, for submission for marketing authorization or for analyzing the safety profile of a marketed compound.) Clearly state if the results are not valid. 
- Justification for Quality Tolerance Limit – Enter up to 500 characters describing the rationale and any limitations to the use of the subject of the QTL.  
- Justification for Expectation –  Enter up to 500 characters of published data or historical data from previous trials within the organization. When referencing historical data, it is important to state whether systematic issues have been excluded. 
- Justification for Threshold – Enter up to 500 characters explaining the rationale for the value set in place for the QTL threshold. For example, why would a QTL value exceeding the threshold be cause for concern? 
- Algorithms – Enter an explanation of the algorithm used to produce the QTL metrics for traceability and auditing purposes. 
- Source of Data – If the Share QTL button is switched to On, then this field automatically populates with Detect as the field entry and is noneditable. 
- Supporting Details – Enter any extra or miscellaneous QTL information you want documented. 
- Optional . Toggle the Share QTL button to On , , to link the QTL with RBQM so that: 
- The QTL gets stored and updated in the RBQM Configuration > QTL Configuration module. After linking, subsequent QTL updates made in QTL Configuration propagate to the QTL in the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory. 
- RBQM consumes the QTL, and if the QTL is activated , then RBQM produces the QTL's performance analysis in the QTL Dashboard, RIsk Assessment, and Risk Inventory with each data refresh.
 Note: Special Notes About Shared QTLs
- The Share QTL toggle is set to Off by default when you create when you initially link a QTL to a risk. Ensure that the Share QTL toggle is On  if you want to share the QTL with RBQM. 
- You can hover your cursor on the Information icon, , next to the Medidata RBQM Metric field to confirm whether the QTL is currently integrated with RBQM.  
- When the Share QTL toggle is  On , then the toggle is set to On for every risk using that QTL. Switching the toggle to Off turns sharing off for every risk using that QTL.  
- QTL Dashboard provides analysis data to the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory for shared QTLs so long as the QTL is activated in RBQM Configuration. Check with your RBQM data administrator to determine the frequency of the refresh cycle for analysis data sent to the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory. The refresh of QTL analysis data in the Risk Assessment and Risk Inventory occurs simultaneously with the refresh of QTL Dashboard data.  
- Click Save .
 Tip : To learn how to read and understand the QTL graph in the QTLs tab, see Evaluate the Performance of QTLs Associated with Risks .

## Add and Manage Risk Assessment Participants
 Risk assessment participants are cross-functional study team members who identify and evaluate the critical data, critical processes, risk categories, and associated risks presenting the most potential negative impact to the study. For example, a pharmacist might assess the study protocol to identify risks associated with the toxicity of a drug being studied. Or a site monitor might identify risks to the visit schedule.
 You can add the list of risk assessment participants to the risk assessment. You can also assign participants; for example, a quality assurance director, to formally acknowledge and approve the risk assessment reports .
 In addition, you can also:
- Enable participants to receive  risk notifications through Medidata's Notification Center . 
- View the list of study team members involved in creating the risk assessment and identifying study risks. 
- Edit individual risk assessment participant details. 
- Delete participants from the risk assessment.

 You can view the list of participants and their associated details to learn about the study team members involved in creating the risk assessment and identifying specific risks.

 Column Descriptions

- Role  –  The participant's role in the study.  
- Company –  The participants employer. 
- Acknowledgement Required – A gray toggle to the left,   , indicates that the participant does not need to acknowledge the risk assessment report ; a blue toggle to the right, , indicates that the participant must acknowledge the risk assessment report.
