===== PAGE: identify_and_investigate_sites_that_potentially_round_or_propagate_vital_sign_records.html | Identify and Investigate Sites That Potentially Round or Propagate Vital Sign Records =====
## Identify and Investigate Sites That Potentially Round or Propagate Vital Sign Records
 You can use the Rounding and Propagation heatmaps to identify sites that potentially round or propagate vital sign records.
 Note: Last Updated Timestamp
 The Last Updated timestamp reflects the date and time when the most recent data snapshot generation process started. It does not represent the date and time when the data in Rounding and Propagation was last refreshed. Therefore, the Last Updated timestamp may be earlier than the time at which the refreshed data becomes available in Rounding and Propagation.
## Access and View the Rounding and Propagation Heatmaps
 You can view heatmaps that report the percentage of a particular vital sign's records at each site that RBQM identifies as being rounded or propagated . 
 You can also simultaneously view and compare side by side both the rounding and propagated event analysis at a site. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Statistical Monitoring > Rounding & Propagation in the left-hand menu. 
- On the Rounding & Propagation page, do any of the following:
- Click Rounding Events to view the analysis and summary data for sites with roundings events. 
- Click Propagation Events to view the analysis and summary data for sites with propagation events. 
- Click View Side by Side to open a pop-up window that shows a stacked view of the Rounding Events heatmap on top of the Propagation Events heatmap. 
## Interpret the Rounding and Propagation Heatmaps
 Your proficiency in reading and understanding the Rounding and Propagation heatmaps greatly affects your ability to:
- Distinguish between reliable and potentially unreliable data in the vital signs collection case. 
- Identify and investigate sites that:
- May not be following the study protocol correctly. 
- May be falsifying or fabricating data. 
- May be performing misconduct in aspects of the trial outside of data collection. 
 This determination helps ensure you take efficient, well-informed follow-up actions in how you further investigate or report your study data findings.
 The following details explain how to read and interpret the Rounding and Propagation heatmaps. 
- The top of the Rounding & Propagation page lists high-level site details: 
- Total Sites – The total number of sites in your study that RBQM identifies with potentially rounding events, propagating events, or both. 
- Sites with Rounding – The total number of sites in your study that RBQM identifies with potentially rounding events. 
- Sites with Propagation – The total number of sites in your study that RBQM identifies with potentially propagating events. 
- The Y-axis lists the event names in descending alphabetical order (A at the top; Z at the bottom). 
- The X-axis lists the sites that RBQM identifies as potentially rounding or propagating events. 
- Sites are listed in descending order with sites containing the highest total percentage of rounded or propagated records at the site on the left; sites with the lowest percentage on the right.
 Tip : You can click a site ID in the x-axis to:
- Reposition the heatmap to show the selected site as the first site listed on the left on the x-axis. 
- Dynamic filter the Summary table to show and high highlight same site ID. 
- Each heatmap cell shows: 
- For the Sites with Rounding heatmap, the percentage of all a vital sign's records collected at a site that are rounded records belonging to rounded patients. 
- For the Sites with Propagation heatmap, the percentage of all a vital sign's records collected at a site that are propagated records belonging to rounded patients. 
- Deeper and more intense cell coloring indicates a higher percentage of vital sign records at the site that RBQM identifies as being rounded or propagated. 
- You can hover your cursor on any heatmap cell to view a popup containing the following details: 
- Site   – The site ID. 
- Patient Counted   – The number of patients at the site. 
- Patients Rounded   – The number of patients at the site with at least three rounded records. 
- Rounded Records Counted   – Shows on the Sites with Rounding table. The number of rounded records at the site. 
- Propagated Records Counted   – Shows on the Sites with Propagation table. The number of propagated records at the site. 
- Total Records   – The total number of records for the vital sign at the site.
- You can click any heatmap cell to view in a separate dialog a consolidated list of patients with recorded events at the site and rounded or propagated record details. In the dialog, you can also click a patient ID to view that patient in Patient Profiles.
 Tip : You can click View Side By Side to view the Sites with Rounding heatmap stacked directly on top of the Sites with Propagation heatmap. This helps you simultaneously compare both the rounding and propagated event analysis at a site. 
## Use and Interpret the Summary Tables
 The Rounding Events Summary table and Propagation Events Summary table list all sites that RBQM identifies as potentially rounding or propagating events. By default, s ites are listed in descending order with sites containing the highest total percentage of rounded or propagated records at the site at the top; sites with the lowest percentage at the bottom. From each Summary table, you can: 
- View the Summary table data. 
- Filter the Summary table for a specific site. 
- Sort the Summary table by site or country. 
- Drill down to view individual patient record details for specific events at a site. 
 View the Summary Table Data 
- Navigate to the Summary section below the heatmap.
 Field Descriptions 
- Site – The site ID where RBQM identifies potentially rounded or propagated events. 
- Country – The country in which the site is located. 
- # Affected Patients – The number of patients that RBQM identifies as having their event records rounded or propagated out of the total number of patients at that site. 
- #<event name> – The Summary table lists an individual column for each event listed in the Sites with Rounding or Sites with Propagation heatmap. Depending on whether you are viewing the Rounding Events Summary table or the Propagation Events table, the columns shows you for each site:
- The total number of event records that end in 0 or 5 out of the total number of event records at that site. 
- The total number of event records that are considered propagated (3 or more consecutive values for the same variable for a given patient) out of the total number of event records at that site.  
 Filter the Summary Table by Site 
- Navigate to the Summary section below the heatmap.
By default, the Summary table is sorted by sites with the highest percentage of rounded or propagated records in descending order (highest percentage at the top; lowest at the bottom). 
- Click the Site menu, and select the site you want to filter for and view in the table.
The selected site shows at the top of the Summary table with its row highlighted in blue.
 Tip: I n the Summary table, when you click the row of a particular site ID, then the heatmap synchronously: 
- Repositions to show the selected site as the first site listed on the left on the x-axis. 
- Highlights the site ID in the x-axis in blue font color. 
 Sort the Summary Table 
- Navigate to the Summary section below the heatmap.
By default, the Summary table is sorted by sites with the highest percentage of rounded or propagated records in descending order (highest percentage at the top; lowest at the bottom). 
- Click the Site or Country column header to sort by that column.   indicates that the column is sorted in ascending alphabetical (A at the top; Z at the bottom) or ascending numeric order (lowest value at the top, highest at the bottom). 
- Click a column header twice to sort in descending alphabetical (Z at the top; A at the bottom) or descending numeric order (highest value at the top, lowest at the bottom). 
 View Individual Patient Records at a Site 
- Navigate to the Summary section below the heatmap.
- In the # Affected Patients  column, click the link associated with the site containing the patients you want to review.
The Patients with Roundings Events or the Patients with Propagating Events pop-up window appears. By default, the list is sorted by patient ID in ascending numeric order (lowest value at the top, highest at the bottom). Depending on whether you are viewing the Rounding Events Summary table or the Propagation Events table, the columns show you for each site: 
- A check mark in the Rounding Event column or Propagation Event column for patients that have at least one rounding event or propagation event, respectively. 
- The number of the patient's records that end of 0 or 5 out of the patient's total number of records. 
- The number of the patient's records that are considered propagated (3 or more consecutive values for the same variable for a given patient) out of the patient's total number of records.  
- If necessary, click the Patient column to sort the list in descending numeric order.
- Optional . C lick a patient ID to view that patient in Patient Profiles. 
- Click Close .

===== PAGE: identify_potential_duplicate_patients_in_your_study.html | Identify Potential Duplicate Patients In Your Study =====
## Identify Potential Duplicate Patients In Your Study
 You can use the Potential Duplicate Patients page to investigate and identify potential duplicate patients by: 
- Surveying the Potential Duplicate Patients heatmap's global view to a ssess worldwide site locations with potential duplicate patients. 
- Manually zooming in the heatmap to the site level view to focus on sites with potential duplicate patients. 
- Viewing a summary list of:
- Countries or sites with potential duplicate patients.
- Patients that RBQM identifies as being potential duplicate patients.
- Auto-zooming the heatmap to pinpoint and zoom in on specific c ountries and sites with potential duplicate patients. 
- Investigating and comparing side-by-side the demographic details of potential duplicate patients.
 Identifying and investigating sites with potential duplicate patients helps e nsure data integrity and i mproves the chance of study success. 
 Note: Last Updated Timestamp
 The Last Updated timestamp reflects the date and time when the most recent data snapshot generation process started. It does not represent the date and time when the data in Potential Duplicate Patients was last refreshed. Therefore, the Last Updated timestamp may be earlier than the time at which the refreshed data becomes available in Potential Duplicate Patients.
 Note : To enable the Potential Duplicate Patients heatmap to render properly, you must:
- Configure sites with the correct street addresses in Medidata Cloud Administration . 
- Map potential duplicate patient data in Data Mapping . 
## Identify and Investigate Sites with Potential Duplicate Patients from the Heatmap
 You can s urvey the Potential Duplicate Patient heatmap's global view to assess worldwide site locations that RBQM identifies as having potential duplicate patients. You can then zoom in the map to the site level view to focus on specific geographical regions and site locations with potential duplicate patients. From the site level view, you can drill down and view a site's list of potential duplicate patients. You can then further drilldown and compare a patient's demographic details side by side with other potential duplicate patients within a 100-mile radius. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Statistical Monitoring > Duplicate Patients in the left-hand menu.
 The Potential Duplicate Patients heatmap initially displays the fully zoomed out, global view. 
 Tip : Click image to enlarge.
- Scan the map for site locations:
- Blue circles, , indicate sites that RBQM does not identify as having potential duplicate patients.
- Red circles, , indicate sites that RBQM identifies as having potential duplicate patients.
- Deeper and more intense circle coloring indicates a cluster of sites within the same relative geographical proximity. 
- If necessary, click, hold, and drag anywhere on the map to scroll the map.
- If necessary, click to zoom in or zoom out on the map.
 Tip : At any time, you can click Reset Zoom above the heatmap to restore the heatmap to the highest global zoom level.

- Black pins, , indicate sites that RBQM does not identify as having potential duplicate patients.

- Site – The site ID.
- Duplicate Patients – The number of duplicate patients RBQM identifies at the site.

- Zoom the map to that site's street level location.
 Note : Clicking a black pin filters the heatmap to show only the selected site's black pin and no other sites. Clicking a purple pin filters the heatmap to show only the sites that RBQM identifies as having the same potential duplicate patient. You can click Reset Zoom above the heatmap to restore all site locations in global view.
- View the list of potential duplicate patients at the site below the heatmap.
- In the Site table > Patient row, click a patient ID.
 The Patient table displays comparing the patient's demographic details side by side with other potential duplicate patients within a-100 mile radius.

===== PAGE: integrate_with_external_issue_management_system.html | Integrate With External Issue Management System =====
## Integrate With External Issue Management System
 You can configure Medidata CTMS for signal issue resolution using Integrations. On the RBQM > Configurations > Integrations page, in the CTMS application section, if you select Rave CTMS from the list, your study is integrated with Medidata CTMS for signal issue tracking and resolution.  
 You can raise and track progress for issues in signals using an established, external issue management system, like Medidata CTMS without needed to copy and duplicate work, saving time and improving efficiency.  
 Once a CTMS application is configured with your study, you can raise issues for signals and send to the external CTMS for progress tracking and issue resolution. Metadata about tasks assigned as part of issue tracking, or the change in issue status is transmitted back into Signals. You can view issue related information on the Signal Details page. 
 Important : Integration with the Medidata CTMS issue management system must be configured and set up for the study prior to integrating with Signals for issue resolution.
- Access RBQM , and then click   Configuration   > Integrations   in the left-hand menu.
The Integrations page appears. 
- From the CTMS application list, select the external issue management system that you want to integrate with Signals. For example, if you select  Rave CTMS   from the list, your study is integrated with Medidata CTMS for signal issue tracking and resolution. 
 Note: You can configure only one external CTMS per study. 
- Optional . Click , the Delete icon next to a configured CTMS to remove the integration.

===== PAGE: investigate_data_using_data_anomaly_detection_plots.html | Investigate Data Using Data Anomaly Detection Plots =====
## Investigate Data Using Data Anomaly Detection Plots
 You can use the various Data Anomaly Detection features and capabilities to help you to determine outliers , anomalies, risks, and trends in your study data. 
 Tip : Data Anomaly Detection visualizations and capabilities vary depending on the type of data analysis Statistical Monitoring applies to the variables you select to view. Therefore, being able to identify which data analysis you are viewing in a Data Anomaly Detection plot helps you effectively use and interpret plots.
 While reviewing Data Anomaly Detection plots, you can:
- View individual patient profiles 
- Flag, track, and audit reviewed study data 
- View Rave Queries in Data Anomaly Detection Plots 
- Log, track, and manage issues   discovered based on Statistical Monitoring's data analysis. 
 Note: Last Updated Timestamp
 The Last Updated timestamp reflects the date and time when the most recent data snapshot generation process started. It does not represent the date and time when the data in Data Anomaly Detection was last refreshed. Therefore, the Last Updated timestamp may be earlier than the time at which the refreshed data becomes available in Data Anomaly Detection.
 Tip : Play the video below to learn how to investigate data using data anomaly detection plots.
 &amp;lt;p&amp;gt;&amp;lt;br/&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;  
## Sort, Filter, and Zoom In on Data Anomaly Detection Data
 The Data Anomaly Detection visualization tool provides a unique set of plot sorting, filtering, and zoom options based on which type of data analysis RBQM applies to the selected variable. You can use the sorting, filtering, and zoom options to:
- View and interpret your study data from multiple view points,  
- Find and drill down on specific data. 
 Click a data analysis type below to learn how you can sort, filter, and zoom in on plot data based on which type of data analysis you are viewing.
 Text Analysis 
 Sort the Plot Data 
 You can sort the data in the Text Analysis plot visualization using the following options:
- High - Low Score – Shows text values on the x-axis from left to right in descending order based on error score. That is, the text values with the highest error scores show the left; the text values with the lowest error scores show on the right. This is the default plot setting. 
- Low - High Score – Shows text values on the x-axis from left to right in ascending order based on error score. That is, the text values with the lowest error scores show on the left; the text values with the highest error scores show on the right. 
- Alphabetical Text – Shows text values on the x-axis from left to right alphabetically in ascending order; that is, from A on the left to Z on the right. 
 Tip : Click Reset Plot to reset to the default High - Low Score filter view.
 Filter the Plot to Display Specific Country-, Site-, or Patient-related Data Points 
 By default, the plot shows the frequency with which each text value occurs within the selected variable. But you can also drill down further and filter the plot to view only data points that correspond with a specific country, site, or patient. 
- Navigate to the Summary section below the plot visualization.
 Note : By default, the plot shows all data points associated with the selected variable
- Do any of the following:
 Filter the plot to display specific country-related data points 
- Click the View By filter, select Country , and then either select a country from the Country  filter or click a specific country's row in the table. 
 Filter the plot to display specific site-related data points 
- Click the View By filter, select Site , and then either select a site from the Site filter or click a specific site's row in the table. 
 Filter the plot to display specific patient-related data points 
- Click the View By filter, select Patient , and then either select a patient ID from the Patient  filter or click a specific patient's row in the table below. 
- Click the View By filter, select Data: Top 100 Outliers , and then either select a patient ID from the Patient  filter or click a specific patient's row in the table. 
 Based on your filter selection, the plot visualization highlights the specified country, site, or patient-related data points and dims all other data points. 
 Numeric Analysis 
 Filter the Plot to Display Data Based on Range and Outliers 
 You can filter the Numeric Analysis plot visualization using the following options:
- Outer Values – Filters the plot so that only data points that are outside of the interquartile range show. For example, if a plot contains a high volume of data points, then you can use the Outer Values filter to show only data that is outside of the interquartile range to help you focus more on the data you need. 
- Outliers – Filters the plot to show only outlier data points. Selecting this option helps you better identify anomalies in your study data that may require further investigating or reporting. 
- Box Plot – Filters the plot to show the plot's lower whisker value, 25th percentile value, median value, 75th percentile value, and upper whisker value. Using the Box Plot filter helps you better see the variable's distribution of data. 
 Tip : Click Reset to reset to the default filter view. The default visualization shows all data points and the box plot and whiskers.
 Filter the Plot to Display Specific Country-, Site-, or Patient-related Data Points 
 By default, the data anomaly detection plot shows all data points associated with the selected variable. But you can also drill down further and filter the plot to show only data points that correspond to a specific country, site, or patient. 
- Navigate to the Summary section below the plot visualization.
 Note : By default, the plot shows all data points associated with the selected variable.

- Occurrences – Displays both variables' text values in a frequency distribution plot. Viewing by Occurrences shows all possible text value combinations and the frequency in which each combination occurs across the pair of variables. - Swap Axis  –  Select to swap the X and Y axes. Swapping the X and Y axes allows you to view the variables' data from a different angle or perspective to evaluate how the data is clumping and trending.

## Interpret Data Anomaly Detection Plots
 Your proficiency in reading and understanding Data Anomaly Detection plots greatly affects your ability to determine outliers , anomalies, risks, and trends in your study data. This determination helps ensure you take efficient, well-informed follow-up actions in how you further investigate or report your study data findings.
 Click a data analysis type below to learn how to interpret the plot based on which type of data analysis RBQM applies to the variable.
 Text Analysis Plot 
- The Y-axis shows the error or discrepancy score . 
- The X-axis show each unique text value as entered by the patients in the eCRF for the selected variable. By default, the text values list from highest error score to the lowest error score. 
- The number of times that the text value occurs within the variable shows on the plot in a blue rectangle, orange hexagon, or red pentagon. For example, . 
- Each color-coded shape is defined below:
- Blue Rectangle   – The text value's error score is less than 2.95. This means that the text value has a statistically normal number of occurrences within the variable. 
- Orange Hexagon   – The text value's error score is between 2.95 and 4.95. This means that the text value has a higher- or lower-than-normal number of occurrences within the variable. Thus, RBQM considers the data type an outlier. 
- Red Pentagon   – The text value's error score exceeds 4.95. This means that the text value has a significantly higher- or lower-than-normal number of occurrences within the variable. Thus, RBQM considers the data type an extreme outlier. 
- You can hover your cursor on a blue square, orange hexagon, or red pentagon to view the text value name and its error score. 
- You can click a blue square, orange hexagon, or red pentagon to display additional information about that data point in a separate panel to the right of the plot.
 Field Descriptions 
- Data Point  – The selected data point's raw text value as entered by the patients in the eCRF for the variable. 
- Data Point Score – A numeric score generated by Statistical Monitoring's high-dimensional data anomaly detection algorithms , which measures the discrepancy of an individual data point relative to the overall study data. Data point scores help you uncover outliers, anomalies, risks, and trends in your study data, which may require follow-up action. An error score of less than 2.95 indicates statistically normal data; between 2.95 and 4.95 indicates outlier data; exceeding 4.95 indicates extreme outlier data. 
- Occurrences  – The combined total number of times in which all patients entered the text value for the selected variable. 
- Patient  –  The patient ID for the patient represented in the data point.  
- Site  – The site the patient belongs to.   
- Country  –  The country in which the patient's site is located. 
- #  – The number of times the text value occurred per individual patient represented in the selected data point. 
- X  – Located in the upper-right hand corner of the panel. Click to close the panel. 
- The dotted red line, , represents the outlier threshold  and spans across the plot at the 2.95 error score mark. All text value data points positioned above the line are outliers. All text value data points below the line are in the normal range. 
 Numeric Analysis Plot 
- Each patient data point on the plot is represented by a blue square, orange circle, or red diamond:
- Blue Square  – The patient data point's  discrepancy score is less than 2.95. This means that the patient data point has a statistically normal numeric value within the variable. 
- Orange Circle   – The patient data point's discrepancy score is between 2.95 and 4.95. This means that the patient data point has a higher- or lower-than-normal numeric value within the variable. Thus, RBQM considers the numeric value an outlier. 
- Red Diamond   – The patient data point's discrepancy score exceeds 4.95. This means that the patient data point has a significantly higher- or lower-than-normal numeric value within the variable. Thus, RBQM considers the numeric value an extreme outlier. 
- You can hover your cursor on any blue square, orange circle, or red diamond to view the following data point-specific information:
- Patient  – The patient ID for the patient represented in the data point.  
- Value  – The raw value entered in the eCRF for the patient with regards to the variable. 
- Site  – The site the patient belongs to. 
- Country  – The country in which the site is located. 
- Disc Score  –  A numeric score generated by Statistical Monitoring's high-dimensional data anomaly detection algorithms , which measures the discrepancy of an individual data point relative to the overall study data. Discrepancy scores help you uncover outliers, anomalies, risks, and trends in your study data, which may require follow-up action. An error score of less than 2.95 indicates statistically normal data; between 2.95 and 4.95 indicates outlier data; exceeding 4.95 indicates extreme outlier data. 
- By default, the variable's data points show on an overlay of a box-and-whisker plot. All data points that lie within the green box, , are within the interquartile range range for all data points within the variable. 
- If you choose the Box Plot filter option, the visualization removes all data points from the box-and-whisker plot. Doing so helps you better view the variable's distribution of data in terms of (from top to bottom) the variable's upper whisker value , 75th percentile value, median, 25th percentile value, and lower whisker value . T he green box,  , also shows the interquartile range . For example:
 Text Versus Text Analysis Plot 
 The Text Versus Text Analysis plot allows you to view your data from two perspectives:
- Threshold  – Displays both variables' data in a frequency distribution plot so that you can see which combination of text values are outliers across both variables. This is the default view. 
- Occurrences – Displays both variables' data in a frequency distribution plot so that you can see the number of times two combined text values occur across both variables. Using the Occurrences view helps you see the count of all text value combinations across two variables. 
 When Viewing By Threshold 
- The X-axis shows the paired text values that occur across both variables . 
- The Y-axis shows the paired text values' discrepancy score . 
- The number of times that the paired text values occur within the selected pair of variables shows on the plot in a blue rectangle, orange hexagon, or red pentagon. For example, . Each color-coded shape is defined below:
- Blue Rectangle  – The text value combination's  error score is less than 2.95. This means that the text data type has a statistically normal number of occurrences within the variable. 
- Orange Hexagon   – The text value combination's error score is between 2.95 and 4.95. This means that the text value combination has a  higher- or lower-than-normal number of occurrences within the variable. Thus, RBQM considers the text value combination an outlier . 
- Red Pentagon  – The text value combination's score exceeds 4.95. This means that the text data type has a significantly   higher- or lower-than-normal number of occurrences within the variable. Thus, RBQM considers the text value combination an extreme outlier. 
- You can hover your cursor on a blue square, orange hexagon, or red pentagon to view the data point's text values and discrepancy score.
- You can click a blue square, orange hexagon, or red pentagon to view additional information about that data point in a separate panel to the right of the plot.
 Field Descriptions 
- <Text Value Name 1>  –  One of the raw text values out of the combined pair entered in the eCRF for the patient that occurs across both variables. 
- <Text Value Name 2>  –  The other raw text value out of the combined pair entered in the eCRF for the patient that occurs across both variables . 
- Data Point Score – A numeric score generated by Statistical Monitoring's high-dimensional data anomaly detection algorithms , which measures the discrepancy of an individual data point relative to the overall study data. Data point scores help you uncover outliers , anomalies, risks, and trends in your study data, which may require follow-up action. An error score of less than 2.95 indicates statistically normal data; between 2.95 and 4.95 indicates outlier data; exceeding 4.95 indicates extreme outlier data. 
- Occurrences  – The number of times in which a patient entered a combined pair of text values across both variables. 
- Patient  –  The patient ID for the patient represented in the data point.  
- Site  – The site the patient belongs to.   
- Country  –  The country in which the site is located. 
- Frequency  – The number of times the paired text values occurred per individual patient represented in the selected data point. 
- X  – Located in the upper-right hand corner of the panel. Click to close the panel. 
- The dotted red line, , represents the outlier  threshold and spans across the plot at the 2.95 error score mark. All data points positioned above the line are outliers. All data points below the line or in the normal range. 
 When Viewing By Occurrences: 
- The X-axis shows one variable's set of text values. 
- The Y-axis show the other variable's set of text values. 
- The number of times that the paired text values occur within the selected pair of variables shows on the plot in a blue rectangle, orange hexagon, or red pentagon. For example, . 
- Each color-coded shape is defined below:
- Blue Rectangle  – The text value combination's  error score is less than 2.95. This means that the text value combination has a statistically normal number of occurrences within the variable. 
- Orange Hexagon   – The text value combination's error score is between 2.95 and 4.95. This means that the text value combination has a higher- or lower-than-normal number of occurrences within the variable. Thus, RBQM considers the text value combination an outlier. 
- Red Pentagon   – The text value combination's error score exceeds 4.95. This means that the text value combination has a significantly higher- or lower-than-normal number of occurrences within the variable. Thus, RBQM considers the text value combination an extreme outlier. 
- You can hover your cursor on a blue square, orange hexagon, or red pentagon to view the data point's text values' error score.
- You can click a blue square, orange hexagon, or red pentagon to view additional information about that data point in a separate panel to the right of the plot.

 Sort the Summary Table 
- Navigate to the Summary section below the plot visualization.

- Click any column header to sort by the column. The sorted header shows in blue font.  indicates that the column is sorted in ascending alphabetical (A at the top; Z at the bottom) or descending numeric order (highest value at the top, lowest at the bottom).

 Filter the Plot to Display Specific Country-, Site-, or Patient-related Data Points 
 By default, the data anomaly detection plot shows all data points associated with the selected variable. But you can also drill down further and filter the plot to show only data points that correspond with a specific country, site, or patient. 
- Navigate to the Summary section below the plot visualization.
 Note : By default, the plot shows all data points associated with the selected variable.
- Do any of the following:
 Filter the plot to display specific country-related data points 
- Click the View By filter, select Country , and then either select a country from the Country  filter or click a specific country's row in the table. 
 Filter the plot to display specific site-related data points 
- Click the View By filter, select Site , and then either select a site from the Site filter or click a specific site's row in the table. 
 Filter the plot to display specific patient-related data points 
- Click the View By filter, select Patient , and then either select a patient ID from the Patient  filter or click a specific patient's row in the table. 
- Click the View By filter, select Data: Top 100 Outliers , and then either select a patient ID from the Patient  filter or click a specific patient's row in the table. 
 Based on your filter selection, the data anomaly detection plot visualization highlights the specified country-, site-, or patient-related data points and dims all other data points. 
## Review Individual Patients with Critical Data
 Statistical Monitoring users with authorized Medidata Patient Profiles access can view individual patient profiles from Statistical Monitoring's Data Anomaly Detection page. This enables you to: 
- View individual patient's profile by clicking individual plot data points 
- Quickly drill into Patient Profiles directly from Statistical Monitoring's Data Anomaly Detection plots to help you better understand the patient's data in context. 
- Seamlessly perform data point analysis on specific patients to determine why the patient is an outlier. 
- Conveniently view data in a per-patient format to understand the patients’ journey throughout the trial. 
 To learn more, see  View Individual Patient Profiles from the Data Anomaly Detection Page . 
## Flag, Track, and Audit Reviewed Study Data
 You can mark outlier data points on plots as reviewed. Marking outlier data points as reviewed helps you and other team members identify which data has or has not been reviewed. This optimizes your overall team performance by preventing repeat work and helping your team recognize and focus on the data that still requires review.
 To learn more, see  Flag, Track, and Audit Reviewed Study Data .
## Log and Track Issues
 Authorized users working in Statistical Monitoring can log, track, and manage  issues while jointly reviewing Statistical Monitoring's study data analysis.   This yields the following benefits: 
- Streamlined issue logging. 
- Reduced recurrence of duplicate issues. 
- Clear line of sight of site or country  issues and issue status. 
- Reduced time and cost required to create and manage issues. 
- Enhanced work experience and productivity in a centralized location. 
- Improved ability to identify and mitigate risks to protocol compliance, patient safety, data integrity, and overall study quality. 
 Important : You  can only view or create issues for sites and countries assigned to you. 
 To learn more, see  Create, View, and Edit Issues from Data Anomaly Detection Plots .

===== PAGE: investigate_data_using_qtl_dashboard.html | Investigate Data Using the QTL Dashboard =====
## Investigate Data Using the QTL Dashboard
 The QTL Dashboard graphically renders:
- Each predefined study parameter's QTL percentage value. 
- RBQM's statistical analysis and approximation of the QTL threshold and upper limit . 
- RBQM's statistical analysis of whether the parameter's QTL value is within a healthy range of the expected QTL value or whether it exceeds the threshold value or upper limit value. 
 You can observe and track RBQM's analyses on the QTL Dashboard from three different perspectives:
- Live View – Meters that show each study parameter's currently observed QTL value and QTL performance based on RBQM's most recent study data analysis. The Live View depicts the QTL performance relative to the expectation , threshold, and upper limit.  
- Patients View – Funnel plots that show each study parameter's currently observed QTL performance relative to the expectation, threshold, and upper limit based on the number of patients enrolled in the study. However, in particular, the Patient View shows the QTL's projected threshold and upper limit values based on number of enrolled patients using RBQM's statistical analysis. 
- Time View – Line graphs that show each study parameter's observed QTL value recorded over time on each date that RBQM performed a study data analysis. The Time View depicts the QTL's historical performance relative to the expectation, threshold, and upper limit. 
 Note: Last Updated Timestamp
 The Last Updated timestamp reflects the date and time when the most recent data snapshot generation process started. It does not represent the date and time when the data on the QTL Dashboard was last refreshed. Therefore, the Last Updated timestamp may be earlier than the time at which the refreshed data becomes available on the QTL Dashboard.
 Tip : Play the video below to watch how to investigate data using the QTL Dashboard.

## Evaluate Live QTL Data
 You can observe the current QTL percentages derived from your most recent study data analysis. Live QTL data shows you the current health and status of the QTL and confirms whether or not the parameter is performing as expected.

 The QTL Dashboard page Live View shows by default. 
- If necessary, click Live in the upper-right part of the QTL Dashboard.
 The QTL Dashboard's Live View shows each study parameter's currently observed QTL value and QTL performance using a meter . The following details explain how to read and interpret the QTL meters:
- The name and description of the parameter appears at the top of each QTL meter.

- A status bar shows above the QTL meter. Statuses can be:

 Status 
 Description 
 Example

 | 
 The percentage of patients that do not meet the study parameter's specified criteria have exceeded the tolerance threshold . ## Evaluate and Predict QTL Performance Based on Number of Patients in the Study
 You can observe a QTL's projected performance based on the number of enrolled patients in the study. By viewing a QTL's projected performance based on number of patients, you position yourself earlier on in study to make sound study criteria adjustments to avoid potential systemic issues.

 The QTL Dashboard page Live View shows by default. 
- Click Patients in the upper right of the QTL Dashboard.
The QTL Dashboard's Patients View uses funnel plots  to show each study parameter's currently observed QTL performance relative to the expectation , threshold , and upper limit based on the number of patients enrolled in the study . The following details explain how to read and interpret the QTL funnel plots: 
- The name and description of the parameter appears at the top of each QTL funnel plot.

P arameters whose QTL values exceed the threshold indicate potential underlying systemic issues, which may compromise study safety and integrity. You should investigate such parameters to determine root cause and to prevent or mitigate study issues.

===== PAGE: investigate_data_using_the_event_incidence_plot.html | Investigate Data Using the Event Incidence Plot =====
## Investigate Data Using the Event Incidence Plot
 You can use the Event Incidence Plot to view and analyze: 
- Which specific event terms were reported as experienced by patients within a domain at the site level. 
- How many patients at a specific site reported an event term compared to all patients at the site. This is also known as the incidence rate . 
- The incidence rate for reported event terms at each individual site compared to the overall study event incidence rates. 
- Which sites have incidence rates for a given event that are considered  statistically normal,  outliers , or extreme outliers when compared to that event's overall incidence rate across all sites. 
- The total number of subjects at the study, site, and country level who experienced each event at least once over the life of the study. 
 You can also log and track issues on the Event Incidence Plot. 
 Note: Last Updated Timestamp
 The Last Updated timestamp reflects the date and time when the most recent data snapshot generation process started. It does not represent the date and time when the data on the Event Incidence Plot was last refreshed. Therefore, the Last Updated timestamp may be earlier than the time at which the refreshed data becomes available on the Event Incidence Plot.

## Access and View the Event Incidence Plot
 You can select which of your study data's domain sets you want to view in the Statistical Monitoring > Event Incidence Plot page.
- Access RBQM , and then click Statistical Monitoring > Event Incidence in the left-hand menu.
The Event Incidence page shows. 
- Select the Domain .
The data pertaining to the selected domain displays in the Event Incidence Plot and Summary table.  
## Find Pertinent Event Incidence Plot Data
 By default, the Event Incidence Plot lists coded event terms by incidence rate . That is, the event terms with the highest incidence rate at the study level appear at the top of the list; event terms with the lowest rate appear at the bottom.
 To help you find pertinent study data in the Event Incidence Plot, you can:
- Page through the listed events, 
- Sort the plot's event terms by incidence rate or alphabetical order, and 
- Filter the plot data. 
## Page Through the Event Terms
 If the Event Incidence Plot lists a high volume of event terms, you can page through the plot to find the terms you need.
- Immediately below the Event Incidence Plot, use the page navigation,  , to find the pertinent listed events. 
## Sort the Event Terms
 You can sort the Event Incidence Plot event terms to give yourself a different perspective when evaluating the data.
- Click Sort by , and select either of the following:
- Incidence Rate – Sorts the list of event terms on the y-axis by  incidence rate in descending order. That is, terms with the highest incidence rate listed at the top; terms with the lowest incidence rate at the bottom. 
- Alphabetical  – Sorts the list of event terms on the y-axis in ascending alphabetical order. That is, terms starting with A at the top of the list; terms starting with Z at the bottom. 
## Filter the Plot Data
 You can filter the plot data to simplify the plot view, which helps you locate and focus on the data that most requires your attention. 
- Click any of the following: 
- Domain – Select a domain to filter the plot to show only event terms reported within a specific domain. 
- View by – Select Site or Country to filter the plot to show patient-reported event terms at the site level or country level, respectively. 
- Site – Select a site to filter the plot to show only event terms reported within a specific site. The Site dropdown only appears when you select Site from the View by dropdown. 
- Country – Select a country to filter the plot to show only event terms reported within a specific country. The Country dropdown only appears when you select County from the View by dropdown. 
- More Filters... – Displays the following additional filters: 
- Select Term(s)  – Select or enter one or more specific event terms whose data you want the Event Incidence Plot to filter for and display. 
- Study Level Threshold – To filter the plot to show only event terms whose study-level incidence rate exceeds a particular threshold , enter the incidence rate threshold percentage in Study Level Threshold , and click Set . For example, if you only want to view event terms  that have a study incidence rate of 10% or higher , enter 10 in  Study Level Threshold , and click Set . 
- Show Outliers Site Only – Select to show only events that are considered outliers or extreme outliers for the selected domain. 
## Zoom In on Event Incidence Plot Data
 You can zoom in on a specific section of the Event Incidence Plot. Zooming in helps you see a closer, more granular view of specific data points on the plot. 
- Click, hold, and drag your cursor to draw a box on a specific section of the plot that you want to zoom in on. 
- If necessary, click   Reset Zoom   at the upper right of the visualization to return to the default zoom level. 
## Interpret the Event Incidence Plot
 Your proficiency in reading and understanding Event Incidence Plots greatly affects your ability to:
- Identify whether sites are tracking events correctly. 
- View event trending patterns and  correlation between events. 
- Identify sites that have significantly higher or lower incidence rates for individual events compared to overall study event incidence rates. 
 The following details explain how to read and interpret the Event Incidence Plot.
- The Y-axis vertically charts the event terms within the domain at the site level. 
- The X-axis horizontally shows the incidence rate, represented as a percentage.
- Each row represents an event term. Within each row are the data points, which represent individual sites that contain the event term. 
- Where the site lies on the X-axis reflects the corresponding incidence rate in which the event term occurs at the site. For example, if a site is listed underneath the 30, then the corresponding reported event term has a 30% incidence rate at that site. 
-  – A site that contains at least one reported incidence of the event term. The site  has an event incidence rate that has a statistically normal probability of occurring when compared to the event's incidence rate across all other sites. 
-  – A site that contains at least one reported incidence of the event term. The site has an event incidence rate that has a very low probability of occurring when compared to the event's incidence rate across all other sites.  This indicates that there may be issues with how this event has been reported at the site, which may require further investigation. The site is considered an  outlier site. 
-  – A site that contains at least one reported incidence of the event term. The site has an event incidence rate that has an extremely low probability of occurring when compared to the event's incidence rate across all other sites.  This indicates that there may be issues with how this event has been reported at the site, which may require further investigation. The site  is considered an extreme outlier site. 
- You can hover your cursor on any  ,  , or  icon to view information specific to that site.
 Field Descriptions 
- Site  – The Site ID in which the reported events occurred. 
- Country  – The country in which the site is located. 
- N  – Depicts the number of patients who experienced the event compared to all total patients at the site. 
- Incidence  – The percentage of patients at the site who reported experiencing the event. 
- You can click any  ,  , or   icon to highlight only that specific site on the plot across all event terms. All other sites get dimmed. This gives you a clearer view of how the incidence of event terms is trending at that specific site.
- You can also click any  ,  , or  icon to view additional patient-related information specific to that site in a slide-out panel on the right side of the page.
 Field Descriptions 
- Site  – The Site ID in which the reported events occurred. 
- Country  – The country in which the site is located. 
- N  – Depicts the number of patients who experienced the event compared to all total patients at the site. 
- Incidence  – The percentage of patients at the site who reported experiencing the event. 
- Term  – The coded term in which the reported term is classified. If a coded term is available, Statistical Monitoring auto-codes reported terms so that synonymous terms are represented under one standardized medical term. 
- Patient  – The ID of the patient at the site who reported the event term. 
- #  – The number of times in which the patient reported experiencing the event. 
- Reported Term  – The actual term reported by the patient as entered in the eCRF . 
- X  – Click X in the upper right of the panel to close and return to the regular plot view. 
-  – The proportion—or incidence rate—of patients who reported the event term across all patients in the study. You can use this icon to gauge which event terms have the highest incidence rate across the study. Also, all sites to the left of   have a relatively lower incidence rate than the study-level event incidence rate for the corresponding reported event term. All sites to the right have a higher event incidence rate. 
- You can click any   icon to highlight only the study-level incidence rate for each reported event term and dim all site-related data points. This gives you a clearer view of how the incidence of event terms is trending across the study. Click Reset Plot to return to the default plot view. 
-  – The group of sites in the study that did not report the corresponding event term. One or more sites in the group have an event incidence rate that has an extremely low probability of occurring when compared to the event's incidence rate across all other sites.  This indicates that there may be issues with how this event has been reported at one or more of these sites, which may require further investigation.  This icon only displays at the 0% mark on the X-axis. 
-  – The group of sites in the study that did not report the corresponding event term.  One or more sites in the group have an event incidence rate that has a very low probability of occurring when compared to the event's incidence rate across all other sites.  This indicates that there may be issues with how this event has been reported at one or more of these sites, which may require further investigation. This icon only displays at the 0% mark on the X-axis. 
-  – The group of sites in the study that did not report the corresponding event term.  All sites in the group have an event incidence rate that has a statistically normal probability of occurring when compared to the event's incidence rate across all other sites. This icon only displays at the 0% mark on the X-axis. 
- You can click any  ,  , or   icon to display information pertaining to the specific sites in the site grouping in a slide-out panel on the right side of the page.
 Field Descriptions 
- <First Column>  – Displays  ,  , or   to indicate whether the site in the corresponding row is statistically normal, an outlier, or an extreme outlier. 
- Site  – The ID for the site at which the event was not reported. 
- Country  – The country in which the site is located. 
- # Patients  – The number of patients enrolled at the site. 
- Items  – The number of sites in which the event was not reported. 
- X  – Click X in the upper right of the panel to close and return to the regular plot view. 
- <#> Total Event(s)  – The number of individual reported event terms listed in the Event Incidence Plot. 
- <selected domain name> records not displayed – The number of reported events reported by only one patient. The Event Incidence Plot excludes events reported by only one patient. 
## Use and Interpret the Event Incidence Plot Summary Table
 The Event Incidence Summary table lists all sites and countries with patient-reported events in the Event Incidence Plot visualization. The Summary table also summarizes key event incidence-related metrics for each site and country. From the Summary table, you can: 
- View all of the selected variable's data points by site or country. 
- Sort by column to find and view data. 
 View Summary Table Data by Site 
- Do either of the following: 
- To view the Event Incidence Summary Table by site: click the View by dropdown above the event incidence plot visualization, and then select Site . 
- To view the Event Incidence Summary Table by country: click the View by dropdown above the event incidence plot visualization, and then select Country . 
- Scroll down to the Summary section below the event incidence plot visualization. 
- View or select the following: 
 Column Descriptions 
- Site  – The site the patient belongs to. 
- Country  – The country in which the site is located.
- # Outlier Incidences – The total number of patient events reported at the site considered as outliers based on Statistical Monitoring's data analysis after subtracting the number of events reported in one patient in the study. The Event Incidence Summary table is sorted by # Outlier Incidences in ascending order by default. 
- # of Incidences –  The total number of patient events reported at the site after subtracting the number of events reported in one patient in the study. 
-  The number of events that have only occurred in one patient in the study subtracted from the number of patient events reported at the site. 
- # Patients  – The number of patients belonging to the site. 
- # Outliers Above Study Incidence – The number of reported events for the site or country that are considered outliers, and have an incidence rate higher than the study’s rate. 
- # Outliers Below Study Incidence – The number of reported events for the site or country that are considered outliers, and have an incidence rate lower than the study’s rate. 
- Status  – Indicates the status of any issues logged against the site. You can click a status icon to view more details about the issues reported at the site. 
- <Blank> – A blank cell indicates that an issue has never been logged at the site.  
-  – Indicates that at least one issue at the site or country remains unresolved. 
-  – Indicates all reported issues at the site or country are resolved. 
- The number next to the flag; for example, , represents the number of issues reported at the site or country. 
- Actions  –  Click  in the row that corresponds with the site or country you want to create an issue for. You can create a Protocol Deviation or Non-protocol Deviation.
 Note : You can create protocol deviation issues and non-protocol deviations when viewing the summary table by site. But you can only create non-protocol deviation issues when viewing the summary table by country. 
- Items  – The number of sites in the study containing patient-reported events. 
 Sort the Summary Table 
- Navigate to the Summary section below the plot visualization.
By default, the Summary table is sorted by # Outlier Incidences  in descending order (highest score at the top; lowest at the bottom). 
- Click any column header to sort by the column. The sorted header appears in blue font.  indicates that the column is sorted in ascending alphabetical (A at the top; Z at the bottom) or descending numeric order (highest value at the top, lowest at the bottom). 
- Click a column header twice  to sort in descending alphabetical (Z at the top; A at the bottom) or ascending numeric order (lowest value at the top, highest at the bottom). 
## Review Individual Patients with Critical Data
 RBQM users with authorized Medidata Patient Profiles access can access and view individual patient profiles from Statistical Monitoring's Event Incidence Plot page. This enables you to: 
- Quickly drill into Patient Profiles directly from Statistical Monitoring's event incidence plot to help you better understand the patient's data in context. 
- Seamlessly perform data point analysis on specific patients to determine why the patient is an outlier. 
- Conveniently view data in a per-patient format to understand the patients’ journey throughout the trial. 
 To learn more, see  View Individual Patient Profiles from the Event Incidence Plot Page .
## Log and Track Issues
 Authorized users working in RBQM can log, track, and manage  issues while jointly reviewing Statistical Monitoring's study data analysis.   This yields the following benefits: 
- Streamlined issue logging. 
- Reduced recurrence of duplicate issues. 
- Clear line of sight of site or country  issues and issue status. 
- Reduced time and cost required to create and manage issues. 
- Enhanced work experience and productivity in a centralized location. 
- Improved ability to identify and mitigate risks to protocol compliance, patient safety, data integrity, and overall study quality. 
 Important : You  can only view or create issues for sites and countries assigned to you. 
 To learn more, see  Create, View, and Edit Issues from the Event Incidence Table .

## Investigate Data Using the KRI Dashboard
 The KRI Dashboard  helps you identify, assess, monitor, and mitigate the issues and risks that could affect the quality or safety of your study.  
 The KRI Dashboard enables you to: 
- View all KRI values that your study tracks at the site and country level. 
- Determine which site and country KRI values are outliers and non-outliers. 
- View which sites and countries RBQM assesses as being medium or high risk to your study's performance. 
- View high-level metadata for each KRI. 
- View the distribution of KRI -specific data in a box-and-whisker plot at the site or country level for a visual perspective. 
- View historical trends in site- and country-level KRI data. 
- View site- and country-level KRI summary data 
- Filter and sort the KRI Dashboard to help you find and view the information of most concern to you. 
- Log, track, and manage issues   while jointly reviewing RBQM's KRI analysis. 
 Note: Last Updated Timestamp
 The Last Updated timestamp reflects the date and time when the most recent data snapshot generation process started. It does not represent the date and time when the data on the KRI Dashboard was last refreshed. Therefore, the Last Updated timestamp may be earlier than the time at which the refreshed data becomes available on the KRI Dashboard.
## View High-Level KRI Attributes
 You can v iew high-level attributes for each KRI. 
- Access RBQM , and then click KRIs in the left-hand menu.
The KRI Dashboard shows and  initially lists site-level KRI values by default. 
 Tip : Click Refresh to trigger RBQM to render KRI data from the most recent study data analysis. Only users with proper permissions can perform a data refresh. 
- If necessary, filter or sort the KRI Dashboard to find the KRIs you need. 
- Hover your cursor over any KRI column header in the KRI Dashboard . 
A tooltip shows: 
- KRI Label – KRI name and description as defined in KRI Configuration . 
- KRI Type – Specifies whether the KRI is a system KRI or custom KRI . 
- Calculation Type – Specifies whether the KRI calculation uses a statistical threshold or user set threshold as defined in RBQM Configuration. For KRIs calculated using user set threshold limits, color-coded threshold values and ranges also show in the tooltip.  
## View Medium-risk and High-risk Sites
 The   KRI Dashboard   visually signifies sites that RBQM assesses as being medium or high risk to your study's performance by appending the site name with  a or icon. The Medium and High signal icons help you quickly identify and determine sites that may warrant investigation. 
 Tip : You can filter the KRI Dashboard to show KRI values only for medium- or high-risk sites.
 To learn more about how RBQM determines risks that are medium or high risk, see  Site Risk Alert Methodology . 
## Interpret the KRI Dashboard
 Your proficiency in reading and understanding the KRI Dashboard greatly affects your ability to  determine: 
- The issues or risks in your study that require further investigate or mitigation.  
- The best approach or mitigating actions to take on the issues or risks. 
- The effect the mitigating actions have made on the issues or risks over time. 
 The following details explain how to read and interpret the KRI Dashboard . 
- The KRI Dashboard lists the KRIs being tracked in your study and their respective KRI values  at each site and country.  To learn more about each KRI type and how RBQM  calculates KRI values, see  KRI Descriptions and Calculation Methodologies .  
- The KRI Dashboard shows site-level KRI values by default. Sites initially list vertically in the Site Name column in alphanumeric, ascending order.  
 Tip : You can  filter the KRI Dashboard to show site- or country-level KRI values . You can also sort the KRI Dashboard by Site Name, Country Name, Enrolled Patient Count, or by a specific KRI's values in ascending or descending order.
- A single column shows a KRI risk category in the first row, the KRI name in second row, and then the KRI's values across all currently displayed sites or countries in each subsequent row. To learn more about KRI risk categories or specific KRIs, see KRI Descriptions and Calculation Methodologies .
 Tip : You can choose which KRI risk categories and which specific KRIs you want to view in the KRI Dashboard . See Filter the Key Risk Indicators Table by KRI Category .
- By default, KRI risk categories appear from left to right in ascending alphabetical order (A on the left; Z on the right). 
- By default, KRI column headers are grouped and listed in ascending alphabetical order within their respective KRI risk category.
 Tip : You can reposition the KRI column headers in the KRI Dashboard. 
- A single row lists a given site or country's KRI values across all KRIs currently in view in the KRI Dashboard. 
- The KRI Dashboard visually signifies medium- and high-risk sites with a or icon. 
- The KRI Dashboard indicates a KRI’s level of risk based on color-coded risk thresholds , which are configured based on RBQM's statistical analysis of the study data. RBQM automatically adjusts the thresholds with each new data refresh. 
- Red** indicates  that  there is a strong association indicating that there may be an underlying cause at the site or country resulting in its KRI value to be an extreme outlier. The risk being monitored may warrant investigation at the site or country level. 
- Orange*   indicates  there is a strong association indicating that there may be an underlying cause at the site or country resulting in its KRI value to be an outlier. The risk being monitored may warrant investigation at the site or country level. 
- Green   suggests that there is nothing about the study data at the site or country that would raise alarm about the risk being monitored. The site or country is likely operating and reporting data as expected. 
- Gray  indicates that  there are fewer than two patients at the site or country, which is not enough data to determine risk level. 
 Tip : To learn more about how RBQM determines KRI risk level and color-codes KRI values, see KRI Risk Level Alert Methodology .

## Interpret the KRI Box Plot Visualization
- The KRI Box Plot visualization shows the selected KRI's distribution of site or country data points on a box-and-whisker plot . 
- The y-axis indicates the KRI value .
 Note : The y-axis indicates the percentage of screen failures for Screen Failure Rate KRI data points.
- Each site or country KRI data point on the plot is represented by a red triangle,  yellow square,  green diamond, or a gray circle. 
- Red Triangle –  Indicates that there is a strong association indicating that there may be an underlying cause at the site or country resulting in its KRI value to be an extreme outlier. The risk being monitored may warrant investigation at the site or country level. 
- Yellow Square  – I ndicates  there is a strong association indicating that there may be an underlying cause at the site or country resulting in its KRI value to be an outlier. The risk being monitored may warrant investigation at the site or country level. 
- Green Diamond – Suggests that there is nothing about the study data at the site or country that would raise alarm about the risk being monitored. The site or country is likely operating and reporting data as expected. 
- Gray Circle  – I ndicates that  there are fewer than two patients at the site or country, which is not enough data to determine risk level.
 Tip : To learn more about how RBQM determines KRI risk level and color-codes KRI values, see KRI Risk Level Alert Methodology .
- KRIs can be either two-sided or one-sided. Two-sided KRIs alert you to both high- and low-level thresholds. One-sided KRIs only indicate either a high-level threshold or low-level threshold, but not both. 
- You can view the KRI's distribution  of site or country data in terms of (from top to bottom) the  KRI's upper whisker value , 75th percentile value, median, 25th percentile value, and lower whisker value . 
- All data points that lie within the green box,  , are within the interquartile range  for all site or country data points within the KRI. 
- Any site or country data points located outside of the 75th and 25th percentile values are considered  outliers . 
- The line within the green box represents the median value.  
- When you hover your mouse on a data point of a particular color, then all KRI values with the same color code are highlighted. Meanwhile, all other KRI values are faded. 
- Hovering your cursor on an individual data point shows the following KRI-related details:
- Site  – The site name appears if you are looking at a site-level KRI. 
- Country  – The country name appears if you are looking at a country-level KRI. 
- Value  – The KRI value. 
- Total  – The total number of enrolled patients at the site or country. 
- Hovering your cursor on an individual data point of a particular color highlights all other KRI data points of the same color and fades all other data points. For example, if you hover your cursor on a red data point, all red data points highlight, while all other data points fade. 
- Hovering your cursor on a box plot line fades all data points and shows the following KRI details: 
- Maximum  –  The 75th percentile plus 1.5 times the difference between the 75th and 25th percentile values.  If no data points exceed 1.5 times the interquartile range, then RBQM draws the whisker at the maximum data point that is within 1.5 times interquartile range. 
- Upper quartile  – The KRI's 75th percentile KRI value. 
- Median  – The KRI's median KRI value. 
- Low quartile  – The KRI's 25th percentile KRI value. 
- Minimum  – T he 25th percentile minus 1.5 times the difference between the 75th and 25th percentile values.  If no data points exceed 1.5 times the interquartile range, then RBQM draws the whisker at the minimum data point that is within 1.5 times interquartile range.
