===== PAGE: rbqm_configuration.html | RBQM Configuration =====
## RBQM Configuration
 RBQM Configuration is an RBQM capability that allows you: 
- Map the specific study data that you want Data Surveillance and RBQM to report on and visualize. 
- Configure the risk scoring scale and data you want to capture in the risk assessment. 
- Create and manage: 
- KRIs and QTLs 
- Derived variables 
- Stacked datasets 
- Review reports 
## What Is RBQM Configuration?
 RBQM Configuration is a n RBQM  capability that enables you to perform all data mapping and various study configuration tasks in one central location. 
## What Is the Purpose of RBQM Configuration?
 RBQM Configuration provides a single, centralized location for: 
- Mapping the data that Data Surveillance and RBQM consume to produce the reports, statistical analysis, and visual output for :
- Data Anomaly Detection Plots 
- Event incidence plots 
- Under-over reporting events 
- Potential duplicate patients 
- Rounding and propagation of vital sign records. 
- AI Data Reconciliation reports 
- RECIST 1.1 Dashboard 
- Configuring the risk scoring scale and data you want to capture in the risk assessment. 
- Creating and managing:
- KRIs and QTLs that you want Data Surveillance and RBQM to report and analyze. 
- Derived variables that you want to add for inclusion in your study's list of datasets. 
- Stacked datasets, which enable you to merge datasets with common variables into one dataset. 
- Review reports, which allow you to capture activity logs and findings across data review and reconciliation cycles conducted within Data Surveillance and RBQM. 
 To learn more, see: 
- Data Mapping 
- Risk Assessment Configuration 
- KRI Configuration 
- QTL Configuration 
- Derived Variables 
- Stacked Datasets 
- Review Reports 
## Who Uses RBQM Configuration?
 Risk managers, data managers, and any personnel involved with study risk management use RBQM Configuration. 
## What Are the Benefits of RBQM Configuration?
 RBQM Configuration: 
- Allows you to quickly configure in a simple, centralized workspace the specific study data that you want Data Surveillance and RBQM to analyze. 
- Promotes platform-wide standardization and consistency and among the QTLs and KRIs you are tracking in your studies. 
- Helps your organization target and review unique and specific facets of your study that you want to monitor for risk. 
## How Does RBQM Configuration Work?
 Study teams must first properly set up studies in Medidata Rave , and then sites must enter study data directly in Rave or upload third-party data through Ingestor . To learn more, see Medidata Detect's Data Pipeline . Medidata's platform data workflow enriches and transforms all tagged study data , at which point, RBQM pulls in the study's data sets and variables into your study environment. You can use RBQM Configuration to: 
- Map the data that Statistical Monitoring and Data Surveillance use consume to produce the statistical analysis and visual renderings for:
- Data anomaly detection and trends 
- Event incidence and under-over reporting events 
- Potential duplicate patients 
- Rounding and propagation of vital sign records 
- AI Data Reconciliation reports 
- RECIST 1.1 
- Configure the risk scoring scale and data you want to capture in the risk assessment . 
- Create custom QTLs and   custom KRIs so that you can track your study's QTLs and KRIs on the QTL Dashboard and  KRI Dashboard . 
- Activate QTLs and   KRIs to get consumed, analyzed, and calculated by RBQM's data science microservice algorithms. 
- Create and update derived variables . 
- Create stacked datasets and view the list of stacked datasets in your study. 
- Add, Edit, And Delete Review Reports. 
 The KRI Dashboard, QTL Dashboard, and Statistical Monitoring capabilities enable you to refresh the modules to render analyses based on RBQM's most recently ingested study data. You can schedule data refreshes to occur and on a preset frequency or manually trigger data refreshes ad-hoc. W ith each data refresh, Medidata RBQM's microservice algorithms consume and analyze the configured study data mappings and all activated KRIs and QTLs, and then Data Surveillance and RBQM visualizes the statistical analyses in: 
- Data Anomaly Detection 
- Trends 
- Event Incidence 
- Under-Over Reporting Events 
- Weekend and Holiday Visits 
- Potential Duplicate Patients 
- Rounding and Propagation 
- AI Reconciliation 
- Custom Graphs 
- RECIST 1.1 
- KRI Dashboard 
- QTL Dashboard 
- Risk Assessment 
- Risk Inventory 
 Note :   In RBQM, s tudy data automatically refreshes twice daily at approximately 9:00am (EST) and 9:00pm (EST), and the data presented within the user interface is current as of 11:00 pm (EST) the previous day, and 11:00 am (EST) the same day, respectively. Each study data refresh produces a data snapshot. Updated data from Rave and   activated datasets from Data Connect   is available in 12 to 18 hours within   RBQM. For more information, see   Clinical Data Studio Data Pipeline .

## RBQM Template Library
 The RBQM Template Library is an RBQM capability that enables RBQM administrations to:
- Create study level   critical data, critical processes, and risk categorization   templates for critical data, critical process, and risk category elements that the study team plans to include in the risk assessment for multiple studies.
- Update critical data, critical processes, and risk categorization template details 
- Activate and deactivate critical data, critical processes, and risk categorization templates for use across the study . 
 To learn more, see: 
- Manage Critical Data Templates 
- Manage Critical Processes Templates 
- Manage Risk Categorization Templates 
 The RBQM Template Library also enables RBQM administrations to: 
- Store and reuse common data listing, QTL, and KRI configurations that your organization is likely to include in multiple study configurations. To learn more, see  Listing, KRI, and QTL Template Library .

## Reassign Master Designs
 The master design is the main study design used for overall study review. You can publish multiple designs and assign them as the master design for use across Clinical Data Studio. But only one design can be assigned as the master design at one time . However, Patient Profiles designates the published design with the most recent date and time stamp as the master design. 
## Reassign Designs as Master for Detect
 You can reassign patient profile designs as master for Detect so that you can directly access the design from other Data Surveillance and RBQM capabilities.
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click Patient Profiles in the left-hand menu.
The Patient Profile Designs page shows. 
- Click the Draft Designs tab, and then find the design you want to assign as the master design.
 Tip : The Published Designs list shows current and previous master designs. The current master design appears with a  next to the design name. You can copy the current master design, make changes to the duplicate, and reassign the copy as the new master design .
- Click   within the row of corresponding design. 
- Click  Make Master for Detect . 
- Master designs display under the Published Designs list. 
- The new master design becomes read-only, however you can copy the master design.
- The master design with the latest Published Date and Time becomes the current master. displays next to the design name in the Published Designs list, indicating that it is the current master design.
## Publish Designs as View Only
 You can mark designs as “View Only” to publish designs as only available for viewing.  
 Note : You cannot edit View Only designs. You can copy them to another study, or create a duplicate within the same study.

===== PAGE: recist_1_1.html | RECIST 1.1 =====
## RECIST 1.1
 Malignant tumors in patients participating in oncology studies are measured at baseline or screening, and at protocol defined intervals throughout the study. Tumor burden is the total amount of cancer in the body. Using imaging scanning methods such as Computed Tomography (CT) or Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), medical monitors and principal investigators monitor the growth, shrinkage, disappearance, or appearance of new tumors closely. Clinicians are then able to assess how patients respond to the treatment in the study based on the change in tumor burden (decreases versus increases). 
 Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) v1.1 is a widely used set of criteria used in oncology studies to measure the response to treatment. By defining all malignant tumors as Target and Non-Target lesions as per the defined criteria, RECIST 1.1 tracks changes in tumor burden, and determines the disease response throughout the study using imaging scans. The overall response criteria are classified as: 
- Complete Response (CR) 
- Partial Response (PR) 
- Stable Disease (SD) 
- Progressive Disease (PD) 
- Not Assessable (NA) 
- Not Evaluable (NE) 
 The assessments are critical in determining the success of any cancer treatment. 
 The RECIST 1.1 dashboard is a visualization and reporting tool in Data Surveillance that captures the treatment response and disease progression metrics for patients based on the RECIST 1.1 methodology. 
 Note : Clinical Data Studio only uses RECIST v1.1 . The RECIST 1.1 Dashboard does not use or support any other versions such as mRECIST and iRECIST.
## What Is the RECIST 1.1 Dashboard?
 The RECIST 1.1 dashboard is a Data Surveillance capability that shows the treatment response for patients in oncology studies. S tudy teams can view key RECIST 1.1 data in a visually appealing format. Study personnel such as medical monitors can monitor disease response (tumor burden) to study drugs using the waterfall plot or spaghetti plot. 
## What Is the Purpose of RECIST 1.1 Dashboard?
 You can use the RECIST 1.1 dashboard to track the tumor burden change, compare tumor responses, and identify discrepancies in overall tumor response that sites enter and that the RECIST 1.1 algorithm calculates. 
## Who Uses the RECIST 1.1 Dashboard?
 Study Managers, Medical Monitors, and Data Managers.
 All Data Surveillance users with View Oncology Analytics and Detect Oncology Reviewer access.
## What are the Benefits of Using the RECIST 1.1 Dashboard?
 The RECIST 1.1 dashboard enables you to visualize disease progression response for oncology trial patients. For example,  
- Study Managers can monitor the growth, shrinkage, disappearance, or appearance of new tumors and the set of target tumors. 
- Medical Monitors can assess how patients respond to a particular treatment based on the tumor change. 
- Data Managers can identify discrepancies between site entered and algorithm-calculated overall tumor response. 
 You can also view the tumor burden change in graphical formats, namely, in a waterfall plot or a spaghetti plot. In addition, Medidata Rave data from the tumor assessment and disease response eCRFs are available in the patient records table along with calculated values using the RECIST 1.1 algorithms . Viewing data graphically and in tabular forms, enables you to more efficiently:  
- Quantify tumor burden and outcome calculations for patients. 
- Summarize the total count of patients, and those in various stages of treatment response at the selected scan visit type and site. 
- Track tumor burden over a period, and identify discrepant records. 
- Assess the accuracy of RECIST 1.1 calculations and safety monitoring. 
## How Does the RECIST 1.1 dashboard Work?
 The RECIST 1.1 dashboard surfaces data from Rave, and produces a waterfall plot, which shows the tumor burden change for all patients at specific scan visits. You can also view an individual patient's tumor progression throughout the study in a spaghetti plot.
 The tumor burden response by patient table lists site entered tumor measurements alongside tumor calculations from the RECIST 1.1 algorithm. You can use the tumor burden response by patient table to compare the overall tumor response discrepancies in site-entered and algorithm-calculated values. You can also mark patient records as reviewed or unreviewed.
 Note : In Data Surveillance and RBQM, s tudy data automatically refreshes four times daily at approximately 9:00am (EST), 3:00pm (EST), 9:00pm (EST) and 3:00am (EST), and the data presented within the user interface is current as of 11:00 pm (EST) the previous day, 5:00 am (EST) the same day, 11:00 am (EST) the same day, 5:00 pm (EST) the same day, respectively. Each study data refresh produces a data snapshot. Updated data from Rave, and   activated datasets from Data Connect   are available in 6 to 12 hours within Data Surveillance and RBQM. 
 You can refresh data in RECIST 1.1 up to two times a day based on Rave refresh schedules. For more information, see Clinical Data Studio Data Pipeline .

===== PAGE: recist_1_1_dashboard_tumor_burden_and_response_calculation_methodology.html | RECIST 1.1 Dashboard Tumor Burden and Response Calculation Methodology =====
## RECIST 1.1 Dashboard Tumor Burden and Response Calculation Methodology
 The interactive waterfall plot and the patient table on the RECIST 1.1 Dashboard show the tumor burden and the tumor burden response respectively, for patients in your study. T he tumor burden response by patient table: 
- Shows tumor response measurements that sites enter, and that the RECIST 1.1 algorithm calculates. 
- Enables you to check if tumor measurements align with the clinical status of the patient. 
- Enables you to compare discrepant patient records.  
- Provides information needed to act further on discrepant records. 
 While the site entered data flows from Medidata Rave to Data Surveillance, the built-in RECIST 1.1 algorithm calculates the following metrics:
- Calculated Overall Response   – Overall tumor response.
- Calculated TL Response   –   Tumor response stages (CR, PR, PD, SD, NE, NA) for target lesions. 
- Calculated NTL Response   –   Tumor response stages (CR, PR, PD, SD, NE, NA) for non target lesions. 
- Calculated NL Response   – Indicates if the algorithm calculated the occurrence of new lesions for the visit. 
## RECIST 1.1 Algorithm Calculation Premise
 The RECIST 1.1 algorithm uses the following assumptions for calculations:
## Study Design Type 
 The RECIST 1.1 algorithm supports a study only if it can extract the visit name from the folder name, and the visit date from folder date or folder name. The RECIST 1.1 calculations are accurate only if the extracted visit information is unique across patient visits. 
 Type of Study Design 
 Sample Image 
 Supported By RECIST 1.1 Algorithm  
 | Studies which capture oncology forms in different folders for every visit.
 | 
 | Yes.
The algorithm extracts visit data from the individual visit folders, Screening , Cycle 1 Day 1 (0 ), Cycle 2 Day 1 (0) etc.  
 | Studies which capture oncology forms in grouped folders for every visit.
 | 
 | 
- If the visit name and visit date are not configured, the algorithm automatically extracts information from the folder. V isit name and visit date default to performed event name or folder name and date respectively, if not configured. You cannot use planned event name and date as the RECIST 1.1 algorithm does not consider these values. 
 Note : Visit name and visit date are optional fields. For more information, see  Map RECIST 1.1 Data .
Yes, but the study design has a limitation. As the visit name is extracted from the sub-older name which varies by patient even for same visit, the bar chart that compares patients across the same visit on the RECIST 1.1 Dashboard  does not render all patients.  
 Here forms like Target Lesions, Non Target Lesions are recorded in a different folder from the visit folder. Within parent folders like Tumor Assessments , subfolders like Assessment + 01/0123(0) , Assessment + 01/02/23 (1) etc. exist, which contain the visit information. The algorithm extracts the visit data from the subfolders. 
- If the visit name and visit date are configured, the algorithm correctly distinguishes between different visits.  
 | Studies which capture oncology data in grouped forms for every visit.
 | 
 | Yes.
 Here parent folders like Tumor Assessments exist, but without any subfolders specific to a visit. Instead, the study captures different visits as loglines within same form . For example, all visits for target lesions in the  Target Lesions (1, 2...) form, all visits for non target lesions in the Non Target Lesions form. Visit data can be correctly extracted if visit name and visit date are mapped in Configuration Management > RECIST 1.1.
## Other Assumptions
- The data must contain at least one screening target lesion diameter entry to provide a non-empty calculation. 
- Screening target lesions and on-study target lesions are differentiated by checking if the folder where they are stored contains the terms screen or base. 
- Scheduled visits are determined by looking at folder names without keywords  unsc or end . 
- If the visit date is empty, the algorithm uses the folder name to identify a visit date. If this is not possible, the algorithm ignores the visit with no date for the final calculation, including any assessments at that visit, for example, target lesions. For studies with no visit date identified, the final output is empty. 
- In case the long and short-axis diameters are collected in the same field for target lesions, the algorithm checks if the location field contains the term lymph. If the location field is empty, the location is assumed as non-nodal. 
- All calculations are made in mm units, so any diameter provided is converted to mm. If no diameter unit field is specified, the algorithm checks for a unit dictionary associated with the diameter measurement field. If no unit is provided or recognized, the algorithm uses mm. 
- If a visit has no target lesion diameter information, the algorithm does not include the visit in the output.  
## Tumor Burden Calculation
 The tumor burden evaluation includes the following calculated variables:
- Sum of diameters – Also known as tumor burden, calculated at each visit by adding all the short-axis diameters and all the long diameters provided. 
- Tumor burden change ( y ) – Calculated by subtracting the sum of diameters at screening ( x) from the sum of diameters at the current visit ( x) , then div iding that by the sum of diameters at screening ( x) and multiplying by 100. At screening, the value is 0.  
 y = 100 ( x 1 − x 2) / x 2
- NADIR – The smallest sum of diameters observed up until, and including the current visit. At screening, the NADIR = screening sum of diameters. 
NADIR is the smallest of the the sum of diameters at baseline or the smallest sum of diameters during the trial. For more information on NADIR, see  RECIST 1.1 NIH Clarification . 
 Note : The algorithm calculates values in millimeters (mm). 
## Response Calculation
 The algorithm calculates tumor response per visit by considering the lesions per category reported at the visit. 
## Target Lesion Response Calculation 
 Tumor burden calculations are used to calculate response for a patient visit. Tumor % change is measured for target lesions only as per RECIST 1.1 guidelines . The following table shows calculations by tumor response category: 
 Calculated Response 
 Conditions when the algorithm calculates the response. 
 | Complete Response (CR) 
 | When all target lesions (TLs) disappear. That is, the longest diameter of all non-nodal locations = 0 mm, and short axis of all lymph nodes is < 10 mm. 
 | Partial Response (PR) 
 | When a  >= 30% decrease in the sum of diameters occurs from the baseline sum of diameters. 
 | Progressive Disease (PD) 
 | When a >= 20% increase in the sum of diameters from NADIR and an absolute increase of >= 5 mm in the sum of diameters from NADIR occurs. 
 | Stable Disease (SD) 
 | When there is not sufficient change to qualify for PR or PD. 
 | NE / NA 
 | If any of the following criteria are met: 
- If the patient visit does not qualify for any other response. 
- if at least one lesion has an empty diameter 
- if the short axis diameter for at least one lymph node is 10 mm or the longest diameter of at least one non-nodal location is 5 mm and the patient visit does not qualify for any other response. 
## Non-Target Lesion Response Calculation
 The algorithm uses the tumor status field to calculate non-target lesion response for a patient visit.
 Calculated Response 
 Conditions when the algorithm calculates the response 
 | Complete Response (CR) 
 | When all non-target lesions (NTL) disappear. That is, the status of all non-nodal locations is absent and the status of all lymph nodes is normal. 
 | Progressive Disease (PD) 
 | When at least on NTL has the status as Unequivocal Progression. 
 | Non-CR/Non-PD (NN) 
 | When at least one NTL has status as Present, and all the remaining are either Normal or Absent. 
 | NE/NA 
 | If any of the following criteria are met:
- If the patient visit does not qualify for a response. 
- If at least one NTL as the status as Unable ti Evaluate at the current visit, and no NTL has the status as Unequivocal Progression. 
- If no NTL is present at a patient visit. 
- If at least one NTL has an empty status. 
## New Lesion Response Calculation
 The algorithm calculates the new lesion response as follows:
- Yes: If the New Lesions Tumor Status for the visit is Yes. 
- No: If the New Lesions Tumor Status for the visit is No or empty.

## Refresh AI Reconciliation Report Data
 With proper  permissions , y ou can manually start an on-demand refresh,  or set up a scheduled refresh to reflect the latest study data in AI Reconciliation reports . Manual refreshes work independently of predefined automated schedules. 
 Items already scheduled or queued for data refresh today disable automatically and are unavailable for selection for on-demand refreshes. 
 Total daily refreshes combine both scheduled and on-demand refreshes. You can refresh each AI Reconciliation report up to two times each day manually. However, you can have only one scheduled refresh combining all the AI Reconciliation reports in a study. 
 For more information, see scheduled refreshes .
 Tip : We recommend refreshing AI Reconciliation before data cleaning to ensure the records captured in each AI Reconciliation report's findings are based on the most recent study data. 
 Note : In Data Surveillance and RBQM, s tudy data automatically refreshes four times daily at approximately 9:00am (EST), 3:00pm (EST), 9:00pm (EST) and 3:00am (EST), and the data presented within the user interface is current as of 11:00 pm (EST) the previous day, 5:00 am (EST) the same day, 11:00 am (EST) the same day, 5:00 pm (EST) the same day, respectively. Each study data refresh produces a data snapshot. Updated data from Medidata Rave and activated datasets from Data Connect are available in 6 to 12 hours within Data Surveillance and RBQM. 
## Refresh AI Reconciliation Data On-demand
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click AI Reconciliation in the left-hand menu.
The AI Reconciliation page shows. 
- Click Refresh  from the top right corner of the page.
A "Refresh is currently in progress" message appears. The AI Reconciliation reports show the most recent data from the study once the refresh is complete. The Current Refresh Date and Time show the latest refresh details.
 Note : The Current Refresh Date and Time appear next to the Refresh Data button.
 The individual refresh status appears next to the report name in the Conditions and Treatments tabs. The report refresh status also shows on the individual report. For example, if a report refresh failed, you must contact the administrator for further action. A single report can have any of the following four statuses.
- –   In dicates the report failed to refresh. If you open the report, a Report Refresh Failed label shows next to the report name.  
- – I ndicates the report was skipped during the data refresh process. This status may appear when required configurations for the report are missing. To learn more, see Required Configurations for AI Reconciliation Reports. You must contact your system administrator to update report configurations. 
- – I ndicates the report refreshed successfully. If you open the report, it shows the timestamp when the data was last refreshed along with a Success label next to the report name.  
- – Indicates the report is still refreshing.

## Refresh Approved Listings to View the Listing's Latest Results
 You can refresh listings to produce listing results based on the most recent study data.  You can schedule a maximum of 15 listing refreshes  in total to run on a  daily cadence . However there is no limit for all other cadences of scheduled refreshes (monthly, weekly, quarterly) that can run  simultaneously . You can manually refresh listings on-demand each day.  
 You need the Refresh Listings building block to refresh listings manually. For more information, see  Data Surveillance Building Blocks and Permissions . 
 Tip : We recommend refreshing listings before data cleaning to ensure the records captured in the listings' results are based on the most recent study data. As Data Surveillance refreshes four times daily, you can obtain the updated Medidata Rave data from four separate snapshots in a day. For more information, see Clinical Data Studio Data Pipeline .
## Refresh Listing Data On-Demand
 Unified Scheduler does not replace on-demand refresh capabilities . You can start an on-demand refresh from within Listings  to manually update data independently of predefined automated schedules . 
 Items already scheduled or queued for data refresh today disable automatically and are unavailable for selection . Total daily refreshes combine both scheduled and on-demand refreshes. Listings allow up to four refreshes per day for a listing. 
- 
 If necessary, access and view your study's approved listings. 
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click Listings in the left-hand menu.
The Listings page shows. 
- On the Data Listings page, click the  Approved Listings tab.
The Approved Listings table shows the following:
 Column Descriptions 
- Name – The listing's Object identifier (OID) 
- Description – The listing's description used to provide additional details 
- Expression – The listing's conditional expression that is used to identify and flag patient data that meet the specified conditions. 
- Protocol Deviation – A check mark indicates the listing is included in protocol deviation. No check mark indicates that the listing is not part of protocol deviation. 
- EDC Queries – A check mark indicates that the listing is Rave enabled, meaning that you can view the listing's Rave query status in Data Surveillance. No check mark indicates that the listing is not Rave enabled. 
- Vendor Queries – A check mark indicates that the listing is part of a vendor query set, meaning that the listing's records have vendor queries raised . No check mark indicates that the listing has no vendor queries raised. 
- Created By – The user who created the approved listing to show the latest results. 
- Refreshed By – The last user who refreshed the approved listing to show the latest results. 
- Included in Refresh Schedule – A check mark indicates that the listing is included in a scheduled refresh, meaning that the listing's data refreshes at a specific cadence . No check mark indicates that the listing is not part of a refresh schedule. 
- Track – Enables you to activate or inactivate the approved listing for Clean Patient Tracker analysis. 
- If necessary, filter or sort  the Approved Listings table to help find the listing you need. 
- Above the approved listing results table, click  Refresh .
The On-demand Refresh page appears.
- Select a maximum of 15 records.
 Note : Records currently being refreshed or part of a scheduled refresh do not appear for selection.

 Note : The Status column shows a warning symbol to indicate changed data against data point values that changed after a refresh.  If a record marked as reviewed undergoes changes in its data point values, it is marked as unreviewed.

===== PAGE: refresh_designs_to_reflect_the_latest_available_study_data.html | Refresh Designs to Reflect the Latest Available Study Data =====
## Refresh Designs to Reflect the Latest Available Study Data
 You can set scheduled refreshes or manually refresh individual published patient profile designs to show and reflect data based on the latest study data ingested by Data Surveillance. 
 Performing data refreshes on individual patient profile designs enables you to: 
- Control the data that you want to show for your patient profile designs. 
- Control the pace of your patient profile review cycles. 
- Gain clearer visibility and understanding of the data that: 
- Requires initial review. 
- Is reviewed and up to date. 
- Was previously reviewed but now requires rereview due to post-review data changes. 
 Therefore, conducting patient profile design reviews is now clearer, simpler, and more efficient. 
 Important : We highly recommend r eviewing patients marked with the Requiring Review status before refreshing profile designs. You can filter the Patient Selector by the Review Status column > Requiring Review filter to find patients that require review. Otherwise, you risk losing track of and not reviewing new and updated data from previous data snapshots. 
## Refresh Patient Profiles Data On-Demand
 Patient Profiles supports on-demand refresh directly within the application to instantly trigger manual data updates independently of predefined automated schedules .  Items already scheduled or queued for data refresh today disable automatically, and are unavailable for selection for on-demand refreshes. 
 Total daily refreshes combine both scheduled and on-demand refreshes : You can perform up to two refreshes per day per design. 
 Tip : We recommend refreshing data for patient profile designs only when you need to see new data. For example, you might want to refresh a patient profile design to review data after a specific study milestone date. 
- 
 Access a published design. 
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click Patient Profiles in the left-hand menu.
 The Patient Profile Designs page shows the Published Designs and Draft Designs   tabs, which contain the list of designs in your study environment.

- Name  – The patient profile design's name. 
- Type – Indicates whether the patient profile is one of the following types: 
- Detect – The patient profile design is integrated with an accessible directly from other Data Surveillance and RBQM capabilities. 
- View Only – A read-only patient profile design. 
- Published Date – The time stamp when the profile design was marked as master. This field displays for Published Designs. 
- Updated By  – The user who most recently updated the patient profile design. 
- Optional . Click any column header to sort the designs list. Clicking once sorts the list in descending order (A to Z, 0 to 9) by the selected column header; twice sorts in ascending order (Z to A, 9 to 0).
 Note : Published Designs lists appear in the reverse chronological order based on the Published Date and the Last Updated dates, respectively. 
- Click anywhere within the row of the design you want to access. 
 The Design page appears and shows the Profiles tab by default.

===== PAGE: refresh_signals_to_view_the_latest_observations.html | Refresh Signals to View the Latest Observations =====
## Refresh Signals to View the Latest Observations
 You can refresh data on the Signals page to view the latest signal observations. Signals generate automatically based on the modules you configure in Signal Configuration .  
 You can refresh data on the Signals page to generate signals for configured modules based on the source module's last successful data update and the threshold set for each module. A slide out panel on the Signals page shows the module's snapshot date from which signals data is extracted. 
## Refresh Signals Data
 On the Signals page, each configured module shows the last snapshot date and time from its source module. On the Signal Configuration page,  you can choose the modules you want the signals to report on.   Once you configure a signal, observations appear as signals based on custom configurations and the source modules' latest data snapshot when you next refresh data on the Signals page. For more information, see  Signal Configuration . 
- Access RBQM , and then click  Signals  in the left-hand menu. 
- Optional . Click to know the latest data snapshot for the following modules.
- Patient Profiles 
- KRIs 
- QTLs 
- Potential Duplicate Patients 
- Rounding  
- Propagation 
- Under/over Reporting 
- Weekend and Holiday Visits 
- Click Refresh from the top right-corner above the Signals table. 
 The Signals table shows signals that meet the set threshold for each module. For more information, see Signal Behavior Based on Data Refresh . The Changed Data column in the Signals table shows a for a signal indicating observation value changes between data refreshes, 
 Note : To get the most updated signals, you must refresh the Signals page and the configured source modules .   Signals data appears based on the configured modules' latest data snapshot at 7:30 am (EST). Signal configuration changes made after 7:30 am (EST) do not show in the automated signals report until the next day. 
## Signal Behavior Based on Data Refresh
## 
 New Signal 
 By default, a new signal on the Signals report appears with the status New . For example, the following image shows a new signal for Rounding. If no action is taken , the signal status remains new. If no action occurs on the signal, and you refresh the source  Rounding module and the Signals report , the signal continues to appear as new if the observation meets the updated threshold. However, if the signal value no longer meets the updated threshold after a data refresh, and the signal status is still new, that is, no action occurred on the signal, it drops from the signal report. 
 Tip: Click the image to enlarge.
 Signal Acted Upon 
## Signal Acted Upon
 For any new signal in the signal report, once you  add an assignee , create action , watch , raise issue , and so on, the signal continues to appear after every data refresh. For such a signal, the status is one of the following depending on the action performed:
- Open
- Resolved
- Watched
- Closed
- Reopened
 The signal continues to appear on the Signals page even if the threshold changes after the data refresh. The signal status remains unchanged. However, if the observation falls below the set threshold, the signal does not drop out from the signal report, instead the last observation value that met the threshold appears in the signal report.
 For example, the following image shows a signal for Rounding. If you refresh the source Rounding module, and the Signals page, the signal continues to appear with its status unchanged if the observation meets the updated threshold. If the central monitor resolves the signal or the CRA sets the status to Watched , these actions indicate that the signal is in progress or under investigation. For example, if rounding is at 90%, the signal continues to appear. However, if it falls to 50%, then the last observation value that met the threshold for rounding appears in the signal.
 Tip: Click the image to enlarge.
 Dismissed Signal 
## Dismissed Signal
 If you dismiss a signal in the Signal report and set the signal status as Dismissed, the signal continues to appear as dismissed even if the observation value goes up after a data refresh.   However, if the central monitor decides on further action and adds an assignee to the signal, the status changes to Open . If the observation drops below the threshold for a dismissed signal, the signal no longer appears in the signal report after a data refresh.
 For example, the following image shows a dismissed signal for Rounding. If you refresh the source Rounding module, and the Signals report, the signal continues to appear as Dismissed even if the observation value meets the threshold. If you  add an assignee to the signal for further investigation, the signal status changes to Open . 
 Tip: Click the image to enlarge.
 Inactive Signal Configuration Module 
## Inactive Signal Configuration Module
 If you turn off modules configured in Signal Configuration after automated signals generate, then those modules do not contribute new data when you refresh data from individual source modules and on the Signals page.  If auto-generated signals are acted upon, that is, signals with statuses Open, Watched, Closed, Resolved, or Reopened, then the signals continue to appear on the Signals page. 
 Signal Persists 
## Signal Persists 
 Signals with status as Resolved continue to appear appear on the Signals page , and retain their default descriptions and status across data refreshes.
## Identify Changed Signal Data After Refresh
 Once you refresh signals, based on threshold set for modules configured and activated in Signal Configuration , observation values may go above or below the threshold.  The Changed Data column in the Signals table shows a for a signal if observation values change between data refreshes. If you hover over the icon, a tooltip shows the changed values. The following table lists common changes in signal data.

## Respond To Queries As A Vendor
 As a vendor user part of an approved vendor group configured in Data Surveillance, you can respond to assigned vendor queries. You must have access in Cloud Administration, and also have the Submit Vendor Feedback building block added to your role.
Responding to vendor queries enables you to provide comments, clarifications, or missing data for external data ingested into a study. Data managers can then use this data to reconcile study data, and ensure study data accuracy.
 For every vendor query assigned, you receive an email notification.
## Respond to Assigned Queries

- Click View in Notification Center .

## Accessing the Notification Center
 The Notification Center enables the Medidata platform to securely send notifications to users to inform about events of importance. These events can be information, warnings, or critical messages. 
 The Notification Center sends alerts in two forms:
- In-app notifications accessible by way of the user interface. 
- Email notifications with a deep-link sent to the user's email inbox. 
 All users have access to notifications. However, these are not available until an event is triggered for users by the app. Users can then access the information from the email or by clicking a link in the user profile dropdown.
 For more information, see About Notification Center .

===== PAGE: review_ai_data_reconciliation_reports_findings.html | Review AI Reconciliation Reports Findings =====
## Review AI Reconciliation Reports Findings
 AI Reconciliation runs proprietary AI-based algorithms   on study data and identifies and lists discrepant records that require reconciliation in the following eight reports: 
- Conditions Without Treatments 
- Worsening Conditions 
- Overlapping Conditions 
- Overlapping non-Worsening Conditions and Ongoing Medical History 
- Invalid CTCAE Grade 
- Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade 
- Overlapping Treatments 
- Treatments Without Conditions or Ongoing Medical History 
 Within the reports, you can:
- View the list of report findings and associated finding details. 
- Investigate the patient profile of the patient associated with a record. 
- View and link other treatments, conditions, or ongoing medical history as being related to a finding.
 Note : You can only do this for the Conditions without Treatments, Worsening Conditions, Treatments without Conditions or ongoing MH reports.
- View and submit Medidata Rave queries on report findings. 
- Manually agree or disagree with findings. 
- Manually mark findings as reviewed or unreviewed. 
## View Report Findings
 Each AI Data Reconciliation report lists records that Data Surveillance considers as being findings. Findings may have additional, related, or unrelated findings associated with them. Data Managers can query finding details, review records, mark records as reviewed, or unreviewed and link findings during the data reconciliation process.
- 
 Access the AI Data Reconciliation report you want to view. 
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click AI Reconciliation in the left-hand menu.
The AI Data Reconciliation page shows. 
- Click the Conditions or Treatment tab. 
- From the list, click a report name. 
- If necessary, filter the report to help find the information you need. 
- View the following findings for reports:
 Column Descriptions 
- Patient ID – The ID of the patient associated with the report record. 
- Site – The site the patient belongs to. 
- Country – The three-letter abbreviation for country in which the site resides. 
- Status – Indicates the record has a Rave query; indicates the record is marked as reviewed. 
- Data Set – For Conditions record data originates from the AE data set; for Treatments record data originates from the CP or CM data set. 
- Reported Term – The condition or treatment the patient reported. 
- Preferred Term – The coded term for the reported term in the record. 
- Start Date – The date when the patient first experienced the condition or treatment. 
- End Date – The last date when the patient experienced the condition or treatment. 
- Confidence – The AI Data Reconciliation algorithm's level of confidence that the record is a finding or a discrepancy. Values are High, Medium, Low.
- High confidence indicates that the algorithm considers with high confidence that the finding details are accurate. 
- Medium confidence indicates that the algorithm has neither high or low confidence that the finding details are accurate. 
- Low confidence indicates that the algorithm has low confidence that the finding is accurate, often due to missing or ambiguous information. 
- Additional Fields - Conditions without Treatmen t
- Action Taken CM – A indicates that a site took action, for example, provided medication for a reported condition. 
- Action Taken CP – A indicates that a site took action, for example, performed a procedure for a reported condition. 
- Same Time Frame Treatments – Treatments the patient undertook in the same time frame as the reported conditions. 
- Outside Time Frame Treatments – Treatments the patient undertook outside the time frame of the conditions experienced. 
- Additional Fields - Worsening Conditions 
- Ongoing MH – Medical history for the patient experiencing worsening conditions. 
- Conditions Reported Before – Additional, unrelated conditions the patient reported before experiencing worsening conditions. 
- Conditions Reported After – Additional, unrelated conditions the patient reported after experiencing worsening conditions. 
- Additional Fields - Overlapping Conditions 
- Overlapping Data Set – The data set from where the patient's overlapping conditions originate. 
- Overlapping Reported Term – The overlapping condition or reactogenicity the patient reported. 
- Overlapping Start Date – The date the patient first experienced the conditions. 
- Overlapping End Date – The last date the patient experienced the conditions. 
- Same Time Frame Conditions – Conditions the patient experienced in exactly the same time period as the reported conditions. 
- Additional Fields - Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade 
- Same Time Frame Lab  – Additional, unrelated lab records taken in the same time frame as the patient's reported condition, where either the analyte name or sample type, or neither, matches. 
- Outside Time Frame Lab  – Additional, related lab records taken outside the time frame of the patient's reported condition, where either the analyte name or sample type, or both match. 
- Additional Fields - Overlapping Non-worsening Conditions and Ongoing MH 
- Overlapping Data Set – The data set from where the patient's overlapping conditions originate. 
- Overlapping Reported Term – The overlapping condition or reactogenicity the patient reported. 
- Overlapping Preferred Term – The coded term for the condition the patient experienced. 
- Additional Fields - Overlapping Treatments 
- Overlapping Data Set – The data set from where the patient's overlapping treatments originate. 
- Overlapping Reported Term – The overlapping treatment the patient undertook. 
- Overlapping Start Date – The date the patient first undertook the treatments. 
- Overlapping End Date – The last date the patient experienced the treatments. 
- Same Time Frame Treatments –Treatments the patient undertook over exactly the same time period as the reported treatment. 
- Additional Fields - Treatments without Conditions or Ongoing MH 
- Indication – Indicates the conditions or ongoing medical history for which the patient took the treatments. 
- Same Time Frame Conditions – Conditions the patient experienced in the same time as the treatments taken. 
- Outside Time Frame Conditions – Conditions the patient experienced outside the time frame of the treatments taken. 
- Ongoing MH – The ongoing medical history of the patient. 
## Filter AI Reconciliation Reports
 Filtering enables you to locate and view record details of interest in a report. For each report, you can filter to view:
- All report records.  
- Only specific columns. 
- Only unreviewed listing results. 
- Only reviewed listing results. 
- Only records with specific values in specific columns. For example, you can filter to view records for a specific Patient ID. 
- Do any of the following or a combination to filter reports to view specific records:
- 
 Filter by Record Review Status 
 Click the any one of the cards once you open a report:
- Unreviewed  – Shows all unreviewed in the report. This is the default view. 
- Reviewed – Shows all records marked as reviewed in the report. 
- 
 Filter to Show Specific Columns 
- Click the filter icon to further restrict the records shown by the report columns. For example, you can select the Preferred Term column, and select a few preferred term names from the list to filter further. 
- Click the More icon , and then click Columns Configuration and select, or clear the columns you want to show or hide, respectively, and then click  Apply . 
- 
 Filter the Records Shown in Specific Columns 
 For the Patient ID, Site, Country, Data Set, Reported Term, Preferred Term, and Confidence columns, you can filter to show records with specific values.
 For example, from the Patient ID column list, select 10041004 and 10141006, then click Apply . The table shows records for the selected patient IDs. You can also filter the records further, for example, to show only records where Confidence is High.

- Same Time Frame Lab  – Shows unrelated lab records taken in the same time frame as the patient's reported condition, where either the analyte name or sample type, or neither, matches. 
- Outside Time Frame Lab  – Shows related lab records taken outside the time frame of the patient's reported condition, where either the analyte name or sample type, or both match. 
- For Overlapping Treatments, click the hyperlinked number in:
 Overlapping Treatments 
- Same Time Frame Treatments – Shows treatments the patient took over the same time period as the reported treatments. 
- For Treatments Without Conditions or Ongoing MH, click the hyperlinked number in:
 Treatments without Conditions or ongoing MH 
- Same Time Frame Conditions – Shows conditions the patient experienced  in the same time as the treatments taken. 
- Outside Time Frame Conditions – Shows conditions the patient experienced outside the time frame of the treatments taken. 
- Ongoing MH – Shows the ongoing medical history of the patient. 
## Link Treatments, Conditions, or Ongoing Medical History (MH) to Findings
 You can link additional treatments, conditions, or medical history for the findings in the following reports:
- Conditions without Treatments 
- Worsening Conditions 
- Treatments without Conditions or Ongoing Medical History (MH) 
- Missing Lab for CTCAE  
 Linking records indicates you identified missing data corresponding to the reported term in the finding, or you disagree with the report findings and the algorithm's high confidence level, and that the algorithm missed a possible connection between events. Linking reports outside the event time frame does not impact the confidence level as the algorithm is already aware that the finding and the outside time frame record are related.  
 Note : Linking records does not automatically train the algorithm that two records are in the same time frame. 
## Linking in Conditions without Treatments and Treatments without Conditions or Ongoing MH Reports
 By linking records, you can train the AI Reconciliation algorithm to identify similar findings in future, and build a relation based on the WHODRUG and MEDRA databases.  When you link one or more conditions, treatments, medical history (MH), or lab records, the confidence level changes to low and Data Surveillance stores the information for future occurrences of similar conditions and treatments. For more information see, Condition Without Treatments Algorithm Methodology and  Treatments Without Conditions and Ongoing MH Algorithm Methodology .

## Missing Dates 
 If you link treatments, conditions or ongoing medical history that occur within the same time frame as the event, then the confidence level lowers. If any part of the date that connects the findings is missing either due to incorrect information or human error, the AI Reconciliation algorithm sets this to the first day of the month or the first month of the year, depending on the piece of information missing from the date. For example, if the date is UN MAR 2019 , the algorithm assumes it as 1 MAR 2019. Similarly, if the date is 5 UNK 2019, the algorithm takes it as 5 Jan 2019. 
 Note : This rule does not apply to non-conformant dates. 
 If no date is given, then the AE, or CM, or CP start date is taken as the start of the clinical study, and there is no end date. That is, the record is assumed ongoing.

## Agree or Disagree with Findings 
 AI Reconciliation assigns to each report finding the algorithm's level of confidence that a record is indeed a finding. A finding is a data anomaly. The confidence levels are: High, Medium, and Low. High confidence means that the algorithm has a high confidence that the finding is accurate. Low confidence means that the algorithm has a low level of confidence that the finding is accurate, often due to missing or ambiguous information. Note though, that depending on the report you are working in, the criteria for High, Medium, and Low confidence levels vary. To learn more, see Confidence Level for Individual Reports .
 As a data manager, you can provide feedback on the finding by agreeing or disagreeing with the finding. The green thumbs up and the red thumbs down icons in  the Feedback column in the row corresponding to a finding indicate if you agree or disagree, respectively. A gray thumbs up and thumbs down icon together indicate that no feedback exists yet for the finding.
## Automatically Disagree 
 You disagree automatically with a finding when you link conditions, treatments, or medical history to findings . The record's confidence level also lowers, and t he thumbs down icon replaces the thumbs up or the gray thumbs up icon in the corresponding row. The in the Feedback column in a reviewed record indicates the built-in algorithm missed a possible relation between the finding and another event, and acts as feedback for marking similar records in future.  
## Automatically Agree 
 When you submit a query , AI Reconciliation adds a thumbs up icon in the Feedback column in the row corresponding to the finding. This indicates you agree that the finding is indeed a data anomaly. The confidence level for the finding remains high. 
## Manually Disagree 
 You can also manually indicate that you disagree with a finding. 
- 
 Access the AI Data Reconciliation report you want to view. 
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click AI Reconciliation in the left-hand menu.
The AI Data Reconciliation page shows. 
- Click the Conditions or Treatment tab. 
- Click   a report name. 
- In the row corresponding to the finding you disagree with, click the gray thumbs down icon, . A red thumbs down icon appears instead. Once the data refreshes, the confidence level for the finding lowers. 
## Confidence Level for Individual Reports
 Overlapping Conditions Report 
 Confidence Level 
 Explanation by Specific Report 
 | High  
 | The Confidence level is high if the reported term of overlapping records match.  
 | Medium  
 | The Confidence level is medium if the reported term of overlapping records do not match.
 | Low 
 | A finding has low confidence if the start date of one record matches the end date of another or vice versa. 
 Conditions without Treatments Report 
 Confidence Level 
 Explanation by Specific Report 
 | High  
 | A finding has high confidence when low confidence criteria do not apply.  
 | Medium  
 | The Conditions without Treatments report do not assign a medium confidence level to any finding. 
 | Low 
 | A finding has low confidence when:
- It includes conditions that cannot be treated. 
- The patient with a condition undertakes a treatment for which another patient within the study has linked as treating the condition. 
 Worsening Conditions Report 
 Confidence Level 
 Explanation by Specific Report 
 | High  
 | All findings are assigned a high confidence level.
 | Medium  
 | The Worsening Conditions report does not assign a medium confidence level to any finding. 
 | Low 
 | The Worsening Conditions report does not assign a low confidence level to any finding. 
 Treatments Without Conditions Report 
 Confidence Level 
 Explanation by Specific Report 
 | High  
 | A finding has high confidence when low or medium confidence criterion does not apply.  
 | Medium  
 | The Treatments without Conditions report do not assign a medium confidence level to any finding. 
 | Low 
 | A finding is low confidence if either: 
- The treatment is not known to treat any condition/history. 
- The patient has a condition or history for which some user within the study has linked as being treated by the treatment. 
 Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade Report 
 Confidence Level 
 Explanation by Specific Report 
 | High  
 | The confidence level is high if no lab record exists within the same time frame as the adverse event for the record.
 | Medium  
 | The confidence level is medium if the lab record exists within the same time frame as the adverse event, but neither the analyte name nor the sample type match the lab record. 
 | Low 
 | The confidence level is low if the lab record exists within the same time frame as the adverse event and matches either the sample type or analyte name, but not both. 
 Invalid CTCAE Grade Report 
 Confidence Level 
 Explanation by Specific Report 
 | High  
 | The confidence level is high:
- if the patient adverse event record has an assigned numeric CTCAE grade but the adverse event is not present in the CTCAE version 5.0 criteria. 
- If the patient adverse event record does not have an assigned numeric CTCAE grade but the adverse is present in the CTCAE version 5.0 criteria. 
- If the patient adverse event record has an assigned numeric CTCAE grade and that adverse event is present in the CTCAE version 5.0 criteria, but the grade is not a permissible one.  
 | Medium  
 | Not applicable 
 | Low 
 | Not applicable 
 Overlapping Non-worsening Conditions and Ongoing History Report 
 Confidence Level 
 Explanation by Specific Report 
 | High  
 | The confidence level is high if the preferred term of the non-worsening condition and the ongoing medical history have the same reported term. 
 | Medium  
 | The confidence level is medium if the preferred term of the non-worsening condition and the ongoing medical history have different reported terms. 
 | Low 
 | The Overlapping non-worsening conditions and ongoing history report do not assign a low confidence level to any finding. 
 Overlapping Treatments Report 
 Confidence Level 
 Explanation by Specific Report 
 | High  
 | The Confidence level is high if the reported term of overlapping records match. 
 | Medium  
 | The Confidence level is medium if the reported term of overlapping records do not match. 
 | Low 
 | A finding has low confidence if the start date of one record matches the end date of another or vice versa

## View a Patient Profile
 During the profile design process, patient profile designers and users with view-only privileges can view a patient profile with actual study data to help you evaluate how the profile design is taking shape in real time. As a designer, this provides the convenience of iteratively editing the design and then viewing the profile again with the modified design against the subject data. Therefore, you always have a clear and accurate picture of whether the design is correct and showing the required results. If not, you can quickly recognize what you need to edit in your design to achieve your design goals. 
- 
 Access the design.

- Click the Published Designs tab.
 Published Designs Tab Column Descriptions

- Detect – The patient profile design is integrated with an accessible directly from other Data Surveillance and RBQM capabilities.

- Last Refresh Date – The time stamp when the last data refresh was performed for the profile design. 
- Published Date  – The time stamp when the profile design was marked as master. This field displays for Published Designs. 
- Updated By  – The user who most recently updated the patient profile design. 
- Click the Draft Designs tab.
 Draft Designs Tab Column Descriptions 
- Name  – The patient profile design's name. 
- Last Updated – The time stamp of when the most recent update was made to the draft patient profile design. 
- Updated By  – The user who most recently updated the patient profile design. 
- Optional . Click any column header to sort the designs list. Clicking once sorts the list in descending order (A to Z, 0 to 9) by the selected column header; twice sorts in ascending order (Z to A, 9 to 0).

## Best Practices for Finding Profile Data for Specific Elements
 On the Profiles tab, the Patient Profile tab below the Patient Selector section and all element tables in the patient profile appear as expanded by default. However, for patient profiles with many elements, having all elements expanded can require a lot of effort and page scrolling to find a particular element in the profile. Therefore, you can collapse all elements to help you scan the profile data and find the elements you need. And then you can expand individual element tables as needed. 
- Click  Collapse All  below the section header and above the first element. 
- Scan the profile data, and click  on each specific element you want to expand and view. 
 Note : When you export a patient profile to PDF, all elements always display as expanded. 
## Identify and Review Patient Profile Data Updates
 When viewing an individual patient profile within a published patient profile design, you can quickly view an automated list of specific data within the selected patient profile that is new or updated as of the latest data refresh. 
 The automatic listing and reporting of specific data changes in a patient profile:
- Gives you clearer visibility and understanding of the data that w as previously reviewed but now requires rereview due to post-review data changes. 
- Reduces the time and effort required to analyze patient profile data to determine which specific data requires review. 
 Therefore, conducting patient profile design reviews is now clearer, simpler, and more efficient. 
 Note : Patient Profiles only identifies and reports new and updated data for patient profiles that have been marked as reviewed prior to the most recent data refresh. It does not report new and updated data for patient profiles that have never been marked as reviewed.

 Tip : Filter the Patient Selector > Review Status column by Requiring Review to quickly show and identify patient profiles that were previously reviewed and have since had data updates as of the latest data refresh. 
- Click within the corresponding row of a Patient ID to view that patient's patient profile. 
- In the profile view, click Updates .
 Note : When the Updates button is tagged with a small, blue circle in the upper-right corner, you can click the Updates button to open a Profile Updates panel and view data within the selected patient profile that is new or updated as of the latest data refresh. 
 However, i f the Updates button does not show a blue dot, then there are currently no new patient data updates available. 
- On the Profile Updates panel > Data Changes tab, do any of the following: 
- Click All to view details on all new data and modified data in the patient profile. 
- A blue plus icon indicates new data in the patient profile. 
- An orange triangle icon  indicates modified data. 
- Click Modified Data to view details on modified data. 
- Click New Data to view details on new data. 
- Click Mark Reviewed to mark the patient profile as reviewed.

## Add and View Patient-level Internal Review Comments Within Patient Profile Designs
 When reviewing patient profiles, you can add patient-level review comments directly within published patient profile designs. You can also view the historical list of comments submitted by you and others on your team at the patient level.  Review comments: 
- Provide a convenient, centralized way to summarize or notate interesting review findings. 
- Facilitate a highly visible and continuous flow of notes and findings to reference across review cycles. 
 Notes:
- All team members in your study can view all patient profile comments. 
- You cannot add comments to a patient profile design while a data refresh for that design processes.

- States the number of patients who failed bulk PDF generation. 
- Includes an attachment listing the corresponding patient IDs.

===== PAGE: review_approved_listing_results.html | Review Approved Listing Results =====
## Review Approved Listing Results
 You can use Data Surveillance to investigate and review an approved listing's results. As part of the review process, you can:
- View, sort, and filter an approved listing's results. 
- Add, view, edit, or delete internal review comments on individual records captured in listings. 
- View and submit Medidata Rave queries on patient records. 
- Mark individual records as reviewed or unreviewed. 
- View and export the audit trail of actions made on the listings' records 
## View an Approved Listing's Results
 You can view all data records captured by an approved listing's conditional expression. You can then perform any necessary investigative or review actions on those data records.
- 
 If necessary, access and view your study's approved listings 
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click Listings in the left-hand menu.
The Listings page shows. 
- On the Listings page, click the  Approved Listings tab.
The Approved Listings table shows the following:
 Column Descriptions 
- Name – The listing's object identifier (OID). 
- Expression – The listing's user-defined conditional expression, which Data Surveillance runs against your study data to capture the patient records within a specified variable that match the expression's defined specifications. In general, expressions are built to identify and report high-risk data points that your study team can review and investigate as necessary. 
- Rave Enabled – A check mark indicates that you can submit Rave queries on the patient records captured by the listing. 
- Refreshed By – The last user who refreshed the approved listing to show the latest results. 
- Track – Enables you to activate or inactivate the approved listing for Clean Patient Tracker analysis. To learn more, see  Track and Untrack Individual Approved Listings for Clean Patient Data Analysis . 
- If necessary, filter or sort the Approved Listings table. 
- In the Approved Listings table, select an approved listing.
 All data records that match the conditions specified in the listing's expression as of the listing's latest data snapshot appear in the table at the bottom of the page. 
 Table Column Descriptions 
- PatientID – The ID of the patient whose data matched the criteria specified in the listings conditional expression. 
- Site – The site that the patient belongs to. 
- Country – The country in which the site resides. 
- Status – Indicates whether the listing record is reviewed, queried, or commented on. 
- – Indicates that the listing record is marked as reviewed. The absence of the icon means the listing record is unreviewed. To learn more, see Mark Individual Listing Results as Reviewed or Unreviewed . 
- – Indicates that the listing record has been queried. The absence of the icon means the listing record has no queries. To learn more, see View and Submit Rave Queries on Patient Records . 
- – Indicates that the listing record contains internal review comments. The absence of the icon means the listing record has no comments. To learn more, see Add, View, Edit, or Delete Comments on Individual Listing Results . 
- – Indicates that the listing record has vendor queries.The absence of the icon means the listing record has no vendor queries. If you click the icon, a slide out panel appears with the query set hyperlink. Clicking the hyperlink shows the Vendor Queries page  with the specific vendor query highlighted. To learn more, see Create, View, Delete, and Submit Vendor Query Sets . 
- – Indicates the changed data against any data point values that changed. You can hover over the symbol to view the previous value. 
- – Indicates that the listing record is marked as in progress. The absence of the icon means that the listing is not marked as in progress. 
- Disabled record – Indicates that the listing record has been dropped after a data refresh as it no longer meets the criteria defined in the listing configuration.  
- Variable – Each column header to the right of the Status column header represents a variable that the listing's expression is configured to run against. The variable column header shows the human-readable variable name at the top and the variable object identifier (OID) at the bottom. And then the column lists the variable's data point entries captured by the listing's conditional expression. 
 Tip : If necessary filter or sort the approved listing's results table to find the listing you need. 
## Filter an Approved Listing's Results Table
 To help scan an approved listing's results or find specific records , you can filter an approved listing's results table to show:
- All listing results. 
- Only data records for specific tables columns 
- Only unreviewed listing results. 
- Only reviewed listing results. 
- Only listing results for specific patient IDs, sites, countries, or variables. 
- Only listing results for specific variables whose data records contain specific values or values within a specific numeric range. 
- If necessary, view an approved listing's results . 
- Do any of the following:
- To show only data records for specific table columns:   click the   Show Columns   filter at the top-right corner of the listing records table (for example, ), select or clear the columns you want to show or hide, respectively, and then click   Apply . 
- To show all listing results, only unreviewed listing results, or only reviewed listing results : click the filter next to the table header, , , , , , and then select  All ,  Unreviewed , Reviewed,  In Progress, or Dropped. 
All is the filter's default selection. 
- To show only listing results recorded for specific patient IDs : click the Filter button, , at the top-right corner of the listing result's table, click the PatientId filter, , select one or more patient IDs, and then click Apply . 
- To show only listing results recorded for specific sites or countries : click the Filter button, , at the top-right corner of the listing result's table, click + Add Filter , select Site or Country , click the Site or Country filter (for example, , select one or more sites or countries, and then click Apply . 
- To show only listing results recorded for specific variables : click the Show Columns filter at the top-right corner of the listing result's table (for example, ), select or clear the variables you want to show or hide, respectively, and then click Apply . 
- To show only listing results for specific variables whose data records contain specific values or values within a specific numeric range : click the Filter button, , at the top-right corner of the listing result's table, click + Add Filter , select a variable name, click the variable filter (for example, ), select all data values or enter the range of values you want to view in the table, and then click Apply . 
## Sort an Approved Listing's Results Table
 To help scan an approved listing's results or find specific records, you can sort an approved listing's table columns vertically in ascending or descending alphanumeric order. For example, you can sort to more quickly find a patient ID or site. Or you could sort a variable column to show the highest data record values at the top. 
- If necessary, view an approved listing's results . 
- In the Draft Listings table, click any column header to sort the table by column in ascending alphanumeric order.
An up arrow, , appears next to the column name. 
- Click a column header twice to sort the table by column in descending alphanumeric order.
A down arrow, , appears next to the column name. 
## Customize Column Configurations
 You can customize column configurations directly using the   More icon, above the Listing table when previewing a draft or approved listing. 
 Note: 
- If you specify column configuration while creating a draft listing, the listing retains the configuration when it is approved. 
- You can reconfigure columns of an approved listing, but these changes are temporary and only visible to you. If you refresh or reload the page, the columns revert back to the original configuration. 
- If you move an approved listing back to draft listing without modifying the expression, the column configuration remains unchanged. 
- If you edit the expression in an approved listing, newly added columns are automatically enabled for column configuration, and the existing columns retain their original configuration. 
- If you use the Copy Listings or Import Listing feature, you lose column configuration of the original listing. 
 Fix Column Configurations 
 To better customise the results, you can hide, unhide, fix a table's columns to appear to the left or right. For example, you can hide columns of no interest.
- If necessary, view an approved listing's results . 
- Click ,  More icon, above the Listing table. 
- Click Columns Configuration .
A slide out panel appears. 
- Drag and drop fields under Columns to either Left Fixed Columns or Right Fixed Columns . The fields you place under each appear as such in the listings table. For example, you fix Patient, Site or Country to the left.
 Note : We recommend:
- Fixing only Patient, Site and Country columns as left columns. 
- Only fixing columns that you can see on your screen as per your screen resolution. 
- Including some columns that are neither fixed as left or right fixed columns, so that horizontal scrolling remains. 
 Do not fix all columns in the listings table. That is, fix some columns to the left, and the remaining to the right. This may cause the screen to freeze (UI Gridlock), where the fixed elements from the left and right sides have essentially met in the middle, leaving no room for the scrollable data to actually render.   
## Add, View, Edit, or Delete Internal Review Comments on Individual Records 
 You can add comments directly on individual records that appear in a listing's results. Comments enable you to share review notations with your study team. For example, you could comment on your rationale for marking a record as reviewed. Or you might communicate with others your intention to review a record once its query is closed.
 You can also:
- View a record's comment history. 
- Edit and delete your own comments. 
## Add Comments

 If necessary, access and view your study's approved listings. 
- Access Data Surveillance , and then click Listings in the left-hand menu.
The Listings page shows. 
- On the Listings page, click the Approved Listings tab.
The Approved Listings table shows the following:
 Column Descriptions 
- Name – The listing's Object identifier (OID) 
- Expression – The listing's conditional expression used to identify and flag patient data that meet the specified conditions. 
- EDC Enabled – A check mark indicates that the listing is Rave enabled, meaning that you can view the listing's Rave query status in Data Surveillance. No check mark indicates that the listing is not Rave enabled. 
- Refreshed By – The last user who refreshed the approved listing to show the latest results. 
- Track – Enables you to activate or inactivate the approved listing for Clean Patient Tracker analysis. 
- If necessary, filter or sort  the Approved Listings table to help find the listing you need. 
- On the Listings page > Approved Listings table, select an approved listing.
All patients with data that match the criteria specified in the listing's conditional expression show in a table at the bottom of the page.
 Table Column Descriptions 
- PatientID – The ID of the patient whose data matched the criteria specified in the listings conditional expression. 
- Site – The site that the patient belongs to. 
- Country – The country in which the site resides. 
- Status – Indicates whether the listing record is reviewed, queried, or commented on. 
- – Indicates that the listing record is marked as reviewed. The absence of the icon means the listing record is unreviewed. To learn more, see Mark Individual Listing Results as Reviewed or Unreviewed . 
- – Indicates that the listing record has been queried. The absence of the icon means the listing record has no queries. To learn more, see View and Submit Rave Queries on Patient Records . 
- – Indicates that the listing record contains internal review comments. The absence of the icon means the listing record has no comments. To learn more, see Add, View, Edit, or Delete Comments on Individual Listing Results . 
- – Indicates that the listing record has vendor querys.The absence of the icon means the listing record has no vendor queries. To learn more, see Create, View, Delete, and Submit Vendor Query Sets . 
- – Indicates the changed data against any data point values that changed. You can hover over the  symbol to view the previous value. 
- – Indicates that the listing record is marked as in progress. The absence of the icon means that the listing is not marked as in progress. 
- Disabled record – Indicates that the listing record has been dropped after a data refresh as it no longer meets the criteria defined in the listing configuration.  
- Variable – Each column header to the right of the Status column header represents a variable that the listing's expression is configured to run against. The variable column header shows the human-readable variable name at the top and the variable Object identifier (OID) at the bottom. And then the column lists the variable's data point entries captured by the listing's conditional expression.

## View and Submit Queries on Patient Records
 You can view and submit queries on EDC-enabled listings directly in Data Surveillance for studies using Medidata Coder or an external coder, or even an external EDC like Veeva. EDC-enabled listings allow you to directly within Data Surveillance view and submit standardized, predefined queries simultaneously on multiple patient records captured in the listing's results. EDC-enabled listings: 
- Save time and effort required to investigate and query patient records by allowing you to simultaneously query multiple patients records. 
- Ensure uniform, consistent query text on the same variable across multiple records. 
 Within Data Surveillance, you can only submit queries on patient records captured by EDC-enabled listings. 
 Note: You can submit EDC queries only if you have the Submit Queries building block access. To submit queries in Data Surveillance, you must have the required permissions to submit queries in Rave. Data Surveillance does not verify your query permissions in Rave. You cannot create EDC-enabled listings using the queries data set. 
We recommend you do not submit queries for system fields as Rave does not support query submission for the following fields:
 System fields 
- PATIENT ID 
- SITE 
- SITE COUNTRY 
- STUDY 
- ENVIRONMENT 
- PLANNED EVENT 
- PLANNED EVENT NAME 
- PERFORMED EVENT DATE 
- PERFORMED EVENT NAME 
- ITEM GROUP REPEAT KEY 
 Important: 
- Data Surveillance does not support bulk query submission for Rave queries on nested forms. 
- If your study uses Rave, you can submit queries for EDC enabled listings. If your study uses an external EDC like Veeva, you can submit multiple queries into Veeva for non-system fields in your study data. The query you submit appears approximately five minutes after submission in Veeva. The status icon appears updated on the Listings page for queries submitted into Veeva in approximately three hours. 
 Non-system fields 
- STUDYID 
- COUNTRY 
- SITENUM 
- SUBJID 
- EGROUP 
- EGROUPDEF 
- EGROUPEID 
- EVENT 
- EVENTDEF 
- EVENTEID 
- EVENTDT 
- ESEQ 
- FORM 
- FORMDEF 
- FORMEID 
- FSEQ 
- FORMSTATUS 
- CREATEDT 
- FIRSTSUBMITDT 
- LASTSUBMITDT 
- IGSEQ 
- DLASTMOD 
- FGUID 
- IGGUID 
- LASTRUN

- Folder – Optional.
 Note : You can update the query to another form, field, or folder that is not part of the listing expression. However, if you change the query to a log line, Data Surveillance submits the query to the first record in that log line (log form) because it cannot determine which specific record the query should be associated with.
 This is true even when the log line (log form) is part in the listing expression, because during data refreshes, Data Surveillance only retrieves the log line associated with the default query field.
