 Note : Published Designs and Draft Designs lists appear in the reverse chronological order based on the Published Date and the Last Updated dates, respectively. 
- Click anywhere within the row of the design you want to access. 
 The Design page appears and shows the Profiles tab by default. 
- Select a patient by Patient ID in the Profiles tab > Patient Selector section. 
- From below the Patient Selector section, click the Patient Query tab. All the queries for the patient show in the Patient Query table. 
- From the top of the Profiles page, click  . Filter fields add to all columns under the column header in the Patient Query table. 
- For any column, if you enter the first three characters or digits in the  field, the list shows queries that include the filter parameter.  The filter response differs slightly depending on the selected parameter. For example, for the Created User column if you enter DON and click Enter, the Patient Query table shows query data with  Created User names like DONALD, BRANDON, MARDONE in an ascending order. The first query that matches the filter parameter shows at the top of the Patient Query table. 
- If you enter most part of the column data in the  field, then select from  list, the Patient Query table shows the corresponding query data. 
- If you enter a date for columns like Resolved Date , Answered Date , Resolved Date , then query data shows only for the specific date you enter. 
- If you apply filters to more than one column at a time, the Patient Query table shows the corresponding query data that matches all filters. 
- For any column, the   field allows you to filter on All , Blanks , Non-Blanks in addition to query data in the respective column. 
- Click   from the top of the Profiles page. Filter fields remove from all columns in the Patient Query table.

===== PAGE: view_patients_that_meet_kri_configuration_query_conditions.html | View Patients That Meet KRI Configuration Query Conditions =====
## View Patients That Meet KRI Configuration Query Conditions
 You can view for each currently active percentage KRI in your study, the enrolled patients that meet or do not meet the conditions specified in the KRI configuration's numerator query and denominator query. Viewing the patients that meet a KRI configuration's query conditions enables you to reconcile patient-level study data between the KRI and a data listing in Data Reviewer. For example, if a data listing shows 10% of patients withdraw from a study but a KRI indicates that 50% withdraw, then you can compare the KRI configuration's patient matches with the data listing. 
 Note : You cannot view patient matches for KRIs configured using audit datasets.
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > KRIs in the left-hand menu.
- On the Key Risk Indicators page > KRI Configurations tab, click the button next to an active percentage KRI name. 
- Click KRI Patient Matches .
The KRI Patient Matches window shows the following information:
 Field Descriptions 
- Total Patients – The number of patients enrolled in the study. 
- # Patients Matching Numerator – The number of enrolled patients in the study whose patient data meets the specifications defined in the KRI configuration's numerator query. 
- # Patients Matching Denominators – The number of enrolled patients in the study whose patient data meets the specifications defined in the KRI configuration's denominator query. 
- Enrolled Patients – Only shows if the KRI configuration does not have a defined denominator query. A check mark always shows for all patients. 
- Last Updated – The time stamp in which the most recent data refresh occurred. 
- Patient ID – The patient's ID number. 
- Site – The site the patient belongs to. 
- Country – The country that the site resides in. 
- Numerator Query – A check mark shows if the patient's data meets the conditions specified in the KRI configuration's numerator query. Otherwise, no check mark shows. A numerator query is the KRI configuration's manually defined conditional expression that parses your study data to capture patient records within a specified variable that   match the expression's defined conditions .   For example, you can configure an expression to capture patient data records for patients who recorded having a headache and a systolic blood pressure of greater than 115 . 
- Denominator Query – A check mark shows if the patient's data meets the conditions specified in the KRI configuration's denominator query. Otherwise, no check mark shows. A denominator query is the KRI configuration's specific data population subset defined in which the numerator query runs against. For example, you can create a KRI configuration to capture patients who recorded having a headache and a systolic blood pressure of greater than 115 and are specifically female patients below age 50 .

===== PAGE: view_patients_that_meet_qtl_configuration_query_conditions.html | View Patients That Meet QTL Configuration Query Conditions =====
## View Patients That Meet QTL Configuration Query Conditions
 You can view for each currently active QTL in your study, the enrolled patients that meet or do not meet the conditions specified in the QTL configuration's numerator query and denominator query. Viewing the patients that meet a QTL configuration's query conditions enables you to reconcile patient-level study data between the QTL and a data listing in Data Reviewer. For example, if a data listing shows 10% of patients withdrew from a study but a QTL indicates that 50% withdrew, then you can compare the QTL configuration's patient matches with the data listing. 
- Access RBQM , and then click Configuration > QTLs in the left-hand menu.
- On the Quality Tolerance Limits page, click the button next to an active QTL name. 
- Click QTL Patient Matches .
The QTL Patient Matches window shows the following information:
 Field Descriptions 
- Total Patients – The number of patients enrolled in the study. 
- # Patients Matching Numerator – The number of enrolled patients in the study whose patient data meets the specifications defined in the QTL configuration's numerator query. 
- # Patients Matching Denominators – The number of enrolled patients in the study whose patient data meets the specifications defined in the QTL configuration's denominator query. 
- Last Updated – The time stamp in which the RBQM's most recent data refresh occurred. 
- Patient ID – The patient's ID number. 
- Site – The site the patient belongs to. 
- Country – The country that the site resides in. 
- Numerator Query – A check mark shows if the patient's data meets the conditions specified in the QTL configuration's numerator query. Otherwise, no check mark shows. A numerator query is the QTL configuration's manually defined conditional expression that parses your study data to capture patient records within a specified variable that   match the expression's defined conditions .   For example, you can configure an expression to capture patient data records for patients who discontinued the study treatment prematurely . 
- Denominator Query – A check mark shows if the patient's data meets the conditions specified in the QTL configuration's denominator query. Otherwise, no check mark shows. A denominator query is the QTL configuration's specific data population subset defined in which the numerator query runs against. For example, you can create a QTL configuration to capture patient data records for patients who discontinued the study treatment prematurely  and are specifically female patients below age 50 .

===== PAGE: view_qtl_notifications.html | View QTL Notifications =====
## View QTL Notifications
 You can opt in to receive the following automated QTL notifications: 
- Information – Informs you when the QTL Dashboard successfully processes a scheduled or manual data refresh.
- Warning – Informs you that RBQM considers at least one QTL in your study as having exceeded the tolerance  threshold and is therefore considered  as out of range as of the latest QTL Dashboard data refresh. 
- Critical – Informs you that RBQM considers at least one QTL in your study as an excursion as of the latest QTL Dashboard data refresh. 
 Notifications are processed and sent through the Medidata's Notification Center . 
 You can view QTL notifications in two forms: 
- Email notifications with a deep-link sent to your email inbox. 
- In-app notifications accessible by way of the Medidata platform user interface. 
 QTL notifications keep you closely informed regarding the latest available QTL Dashboard study data and analysis to help you monitor and manage study risks as necessary.
 Important : To subscribe or unsubscribe to QTL notifications, provide your Medidata Professional Services representative a list of emails of users who wish to subscribe or unsubscribe.
## View QTL Notifications Through Email
- Open the email notification you receive from Medidata. 
- Click  View in Notification Center .
 On the Notifications page, depending on the QTL status, a message regarding the QTL appears. You can take further steps as necessary to manage the risk to the study parameter.  
## View QTL Notifications in the Notification Center
- Log in to iMedidata.com . 
- Click the Notifications icon in the iMedidata toolbar.
 Note : An icon with a red circle  indicates new, unread notifications.
The Notifications page shows all notifications you have received, listed in order from newest at top.
 Note : You can continuously scroll through notifications to the end. When you reach the bottom, if there are more notifications, then the page automatically shows the notifications.
- Optional . In the left-hand pane, click to filter the Notifications page to show specific notifications by type: All, Information, Warning, or Critical.

## View Rave Queries in Data Anomaly Detection Plots
 In Statistical Monitoring, you can view historical information for Rave queries made against a Data Anomaly Detection plot's top 100 outlier data points. Therefore, reviewers can view queried data points and query information directly in RBQM without logging into Medidata Rave.
 Note : You cannot create queries in Statistical Monitoring. You can only see queries and associated information that come from Rave.
- If necessary,  access the Data Anomaly Detection page . 
- Select a Domain Set. 
- Select a Variable.
The list of plots associated with the selected variable shows in the Plot table below. Only plots with outlier data show.
- Plot Name – The variable or variables that RBQM analyzes. 
- # Outliers – The total number of the variable's data point that are considered outliers. 
- Click a plot name.
 The selected plot shows in the plot visualization along with summary information. 
- Navigate to the Summary section below the Data Anomaly Detection visualization. 
- From the View By filter, select Data: Top 100 Outliers .
- In the Status column, click   in the corresponding row of the patient whose Rave query information you want to view.
The Query History pane appears on the right side of the page.
 Tip : You can click to sort by column.
- Patient  – The patient ID of the queried patient. 
- Variable  – The currently selected variable in view of the Data Anomaly Detection plot visualization. 
- Value  – The queried data point value. 
- Query Type  – Specifies the marking group defined in Rave.
 Tip : Query types that contain AutoQuery in the name are system queries; otherwise, they are manual queries.
 Action  – Specifies the action made on the query. 
- Query Data  – The data point's value when the query was originally opened.
 Note :  The data point value reads as the coded term rather than the manually entered term. 
- Text  – Information entered by the user when the query was created. 
- Action By  – User who performed the query action. 
- Action Date  – Date in which the query action occurred.

 Viewing the audit trail of actions made on each schedule , ensures traceability using a reportable single source of truth.

 You can view the risk notifications in two forms: 
- Email notifications with a deep-link sent to your email inbox. 
- In-app notifications accessible by way of the Medidata platform user interface. 
 Risk Management provides two types of notifications at the risk level.
- Risk Review Due Soon (warning). 
- Risk Review Overdue (Critical). 
 All users have access to notifications. However, these are not available until an event is triggered for users by the app. Users can then access the information from the email or by clicking a link in the user profile dropdown.
 Note : You must be assigned as a Risk Owner to receive notifications.
 Additionally, a new notification is available at the Risk Assessment level. The notification is sent to all participants of the risk assessment when the next planned assessment date has passed

===== PAGE: visualizations.html | Custom Graphs =====
## Custom Graphs
 Custom Graphs is a self-serve data visualization and reporting tool that enables you to chart the relationship between any combination of datasets on a single visual using real-time study data on demand. 
 You can plot any study data you want to visualize based on your specific needs or area of interest to: 
- Gain a clearer understanding or perspective of the data. 
- Identify study trends and patterns. 
- Track study performance. 
- Build and share reports. 
## What Is Custom Graphs?
 Custom Graphs is a self-serve study data visualization and reporting tool. 
## What is the Purpose of Custom Graphs?
 You can use Custom Graphs to chart the relationship between any combination of datasets on a single visual using real-time study data on demand. 
## Who Uses Custom Graphs?
 All study team members can use Custom Graphs to create or view data visualizations.
## What Are the Benefits of Using Custom Graphs?
 Custom Graphs enables you to flexibly plot any study data you want to visualize, catering to your specific needs or area of interest. For example: 
- Medical monitors can view the number of adverse events per site.
- Site monitors can track patient enrollment rate.   
- Data managers can view missed visits or data entry delays. 
- CRAs can view, track, and compare patients records for pulse against blood pressure.  
- Study managers can see the number of nonrandomized patients in the study or track the number of study dropouts per month. 
 You can also view the data in the optimal graphical rendering—whether in a bar chart, stacked bar chart, line chart, multiline chart, scatter chart, donut chart, or segmented donut chart. 
 Graphically visualizing study data relationships enables you to more effectively: 
- Gain a clearer understanding or perspective of the study data. 
- Identify study trends and patterns. 
- Track study performance. 
- Build and share reports or present on study data metrics using clear, visually appealing graphical renderings. 
 And you can create Custom Graphs on your own anytime you want. 
## How Does Custom Graphs Work?
 You can plot study data in a bar chart, stacked bar chart, line chart, multiline chart, scatter chart, donut chart, segmented donut chart, or tabular chart. 
 You can create, view, edit, and delete study data visualizations. 
 Note : In Data Surveillance and RBQM, s tudy data automatically refreshes four times daily at approximately 9:00am (EST), 3:00pm (EST), 9:00pm (EST) and 3:00am (EST), and the data presented within the user interface is current as of 11:00 pm (EST) the previous day, 5:00 am (EST) the same day, 11:00 am (EST) the same day, 5:00 pm (EST) the same day, respectively. Each study data refresh produces a data snapshot. Updated data from Medidata Rave, and   activated datasets from Data Connect   are available in 6 to 12 hours within Data Surveillance and RBQM. 
## How Do I Create Custom Graphs?
 See Create Custom Graphs .

===== PAGE: weekend_and_holiday_visits.html | Weekend and Holiday Visits =====
## Weekend and Holiday Visits
 You can view at the study or country level:
- How many patient visits occurred on each day of the week throughout the study. 
- The complete list of patient visits recorded on each day of the week. 
 Identifying scheduled patient visits that occurred on weekends or holidays can help you investigate whether falsified or erroneous patient records exist in your study data. 
## What Are Weekend and Holiday Visits?
 Scheduled patient visits that occur on a weekend or holiday. 
## Why Should I Care About Visits That Occur on Weekends or Holidays?
 Scheduled patient visits typically do not occur on weekends or holidays. Visits recorded as taking place on weekends or holidays can indicate potential fraud, misconduct, or simple data entry errors by sites. 
## What Are the Patient Visit Listings?
 Statistical Monitoring's Weekend and Holiday Visits capability contains patient visit listings for each day of the week. The listings break down at the study or selected country level how many scheduled patient visits occurred on each day of the week throughout the study. You can further view the complete list of scheduled patient visits recorded on a specific weekday and investigate visit details such as: 
- Site   – The site where the visit occurred. 
- Country   – The country where the visit occurred 
- Patient   – The patient ID of the patient who attended the visit. 
- Visit Name   – The type of visit; for example, an unscheduled visit. 
- Visit Date   – The date that the visit occurred. 
## What Is the Purpose of the Patient Visit Listings?
 Viewing the scheduled patient visits that occurred on weekends or holidays can help you investigate whether falsified or erroneous patient records exist in your study data. Based on your findings, you can monitor sites of interest to determine any mitigating actions. 
## What Are the Benefits of the Patient Visit Listings?
 Identifying erroneous or potentially falsified patient visit data in a study data puts you and your life sciences team in an optimal position to: 
- Monitor sites of interest to:
- Prevent financial loss. 
- Ensure data integrity.  
- Improve the chance of study success. 
- Avoid delayed time to market. 
- Prevent extreme adverse events(AEs) in study patients. 
- Prevent failed clinical trials. 
## Who Reviews the Patient Visit Listings?
 Anyone assigned with ensuring study data integrity. For example, central monitors or site monitors.
## How Do I Review the Patient Visit Listings to Identify Non-Business Day Visits?
 See  Investigate Site Visits On Non-Business Days .
## How Do I Refresh Weekend and Holiday Visits to Output the Latest Study Data Analysis?
 See  Schedule or Trigger When Statistical Monitoring Refreshes and Outputs the Latest Study Data Analysis .
## How Do I Export Patient Visit Listings by Weekday?
 See Export Patient Visit Listings by Weekday .
## How Do I Log and Track Issues?
 You can manually raise signals for Weekend and Holiday Visits, and raise issues for the signals. See log issues that require further investigation or mitigation on the   Signals page .
